translations.hypothesis: Cuomo, dị afọ 53, malitere ọrụ ya dịka onye obereokwu n'ụbọchị ole na ole gara aga, ma kwadoro iwu nke e wepụtara n'ọnwa gara aga nke na-akpọrọ azụ azụ maka agụ nwoke na nwoke.

translations.source: He referred to the rumors as "political chatter and silliness".
translations.reference: Ọ kpọrọ asịrị ndị ahụ "mkparịta ụka ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na nzuzu".
translations.hypothesis: Ọ kpọrọ akụkọ ifo ndị ahụ "mkparịta ụka na ihe ndị enweghị isi nke ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị."

translations.source: He is speculated to make a run for president in 2016.
translations.reference: A na-aka na ọ ga-azọ ọkwa onye isi ala n'afọ 2016.
translations.hypothesis: A na-akọwapụta na ọ nwere ike ịgbalị ịtakọrịta maka ọkwa presindentị na afọ 2016.

translations.source: NextGen is a system the FAA claims would allow aircraft to fly shorter routes and save millions of gallons of fuel each year and cut carbon emissions.
translations.reference: NextGen bụ otu sistemụ FAA na-asị ga-enye ụgbọ elu òhèerè ife site n’ụzọ kara pee mpe ma chekwa ọtụtụ nde galọnụ nke mmanụ kwa afọ na mkpọfụ anwụrụ.
translations.hypothesis: NextGen bụ usoro nke FAA na-ekwu na ọ ga-enyere ụgbọ elu ohere ịnya ụzọ dị mkpụrụ ma na-adị gịrị, wee chekwa ọtụtụ miriyọrọ nke akụ na ụlọ ọrụ kwa afọ, yana belata mmepụta gasị nke na-ebute oke ihu igwe.

translations.source: It uses satellite-based technology as opposed to older ground-radar-based technology to allow air traffic controllers to pinpoint aircraft with greater precision and give pilots more accurate information.
translations.reference: O ji teknụzụ satilaịti dị iche na teknụzụ rada nọ n'ala were enyere ndị na-ejikwa nfegharị ụgbọelu aka ịma ebe ụgbọelu nọ kpọmkwem ma nyekwa ndị ọkwọ ụgbọelu ozi ziri ezi.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ na-eji teknụlọji nke dabere na satelite, ọ bụghị teknụlọji ochie nke dabere na radar nke dị n'ala, iji nyere ndị na-ahụ maka njem ụgbọ elu ohere ịmatị ụgbọ elu nke ọma karị, ma jikwa nye ndị ọkwọ ụgbọ elu ozi zuru oke.

translations.source: No extra transport is being put on and overground trains will not stop at Wembley, and car parking and park-and-ride facilities are unavailable at the ground.
translations.reference: Anaghị etinyekwasị ihe njem, ma ụgbọoloko elu ala agaghị akwụsị na Wembli, ma ndowe ụgbọala makwa akụrụngwa dowe ma gbakwaa adịghị ebe ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dịghị ụgbọ ala ọzọ na-abịa, ma ụgbọ ọkwu nke na-agba elu agba agba adịghị ezi n'ebe Wembley. Ọ bụghịkwa ụlọ ọkwọ ụlọ ọkwu na ebe a na-etinye ụgbọ ala, yana ọdụ ụgbọ ala ebe ndị mmadụ na-apụ na ụgbọ ala ha wee bido ije adịghị ebe ahụ.

translations.source: Fears of lack of transportation raised the possibility that the game would be forced to play behind closed doors without the team's supporters.
translations.reference: Ụjọ ụbịam ụzọ njem mere na onwere ike ndị egwuregwu ga egwu n'enweghị ndị nkwado ha.
translations.hypothesis: N'ihi ụdị atụmụta na-adịghị mma banyere itinye ego maka ụgbọ ala, enwere olileanya na egwuregwu ahụ ga-adị na enweghị ndị na-eleta, na-eme naanị n'ime ụlọ, na-enweghị ndị na-akwado otu egwuregwu ahụ.

translations.source: Researchers from Princeton University in the United States and Uppsala University in Sweden reported the new species evolved in just two generations, though this process had been believed to take much longer, due to breeding between an endemic Darwin finch, Geospiza fortes, and the immigrant cactus finch, Geospiza conirostris.
translations.reference: Ndị nchọcha sitere na Mahadum Princeton dị na mba Amerịka na Mahadum Uppsala dị na mba Sweden kọwara ụdịdị ọhụrụ pụtara na naanị ọgbọ abụọ, ọ bụ ezie na ụkpụrụ a ka e chere na ọ na-ewe oge karịa, n'ihi ọmụmụ n’etiti otu ụdị nnụnụ bụ Dawin Finchi na-ebi otu ebe, Jiospiza Fọtisi, nakwa Kakụtus Finchi si esi bata, Jiospiza konirostrisi.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị nyocha sitere na Mahadum Princeton na United States na Mahadum Uppsala na Sweden kọwara na ụdị anụ ọhịa ọhụrụ ahụ mụtara n'ime abụọ naanị ọgbọ, ọ bụ ezie na a tụrụ anya na usoro a ga-ewe ọtụtụ oge, n'ihi mmepụta ụmụ sitere n'etiti Darwin finch, Geospiza fortes, nke dị naanị na ebe ahụ, na cactus finch, Geospiza conirostris, nke sitere n'ebe ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: Gold may be worked into all sorts of shapes. It can be rolled into tiny shapes.
translations.reference: E nwere ike ịrụpụta ọla edo n'ime ụdị ụdịdị niile. E nwere ike ịpịakọta ya n'ime ụdịdị ndị pere mpe.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ahụ nwere ike ịkpụnye ya n'ọtụtụ ụdị. Ọ nwere ike ịkpụnye ya n'ime obere ụdị.

translations.source: It can be pulled into thin wire, which can be twisted and plaited. It can be hammered or rolled into sheets.
translations.reference: Enwere ike itinye ya n'ime waya girigiri, nke e nwere ike ịghịkọta ma tee ya ihe otite. Enwere ike itisa ya ma ọ bụ rọkụlọ ya n'ime mpempe akwụkwọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ nwere ike ịgbanye ya n'igwe ọla na-adịkarị mma, nke pụrụ ịgbanye ya ma ọ bụ jikọọ ya ọnụ. Ọ nwekwara ike ịkpụta ya ma ọ bụ gbanye ya n'ọkwụ.

translations.source: It can be made very thin, and stuck onto other metal. It can be made so thin that it was sometimes used to decorate the hand-painted pictures in books called "illuminated manuscripts".
translations.reference: Enwere ike ime ya ọ dị oke gịrịgịrị, ma mado ya n'ahụ igwe ọzọ. Enwere ike ime ya ọ dị oke gịrịgịrị ruo na ụfọdụ oge eji ya achọ ọrụ agba ejiri aka tee n'akwụkwọ akpọrọ "akwụkwọ ihe ngosi" mma.
translations.hypothesis: Enwere ike ịme ya nke ukwuu na ọdịmma, wee jikọọ ya na ihe ndị ọzọ dị na metal. Enwere ike ịme ya nke ukwuu na ọdịmma ruo ebe ọ bụ na ọ bụrụla nke dị mfe, na mgbe ụfọdụ, a na-eji ya edebe ihe osiriisi nke eserese ndị e chiri akwụkwọ n'akwụkwọ ndị a na-akpọ "akwụkwọ eserese."

translations.source: This is called a chemical's pH. You can make an indicator using red cabbage juice.
translations.reference: A na-akpọ nke a PH nke kemịkal. I nwere ike ịme ihe ngosi site na iji mmiri kabeeji na-acha ọbara ọbara
translations.hypothesis: A na-akpọ pH nke kemịkalụ. Ị nwere ike mee ihe ọzọ na-egosi pH site n'ịji mmiri nke cabbage na-acha uhie uhie.

translations.source: The cabbage juice changes color depending on how acidic or basic (alkaline) the chemical is.
translations.reference: Ihu mmanya kabej a na-agbanwe agba dabere na otu kemikal ya si dị asidik maọbụ bezik (alkaline).
translations.hypothesis: Mmiri nke a na-esi n'ọ́kụsụ na-agbanwe agba, dabere na ọkwa acidity ma ọ bụ alkalinity (ihe na-adị elu) nke kemịkal ahụ.

translations.source: The pH level is indicated by the amount of Hydrogen (the H in pH) ions in the tested chemical.
translations.reference: Nha nke ayọn Hydrogen nọ na kemịkal ọbụla bụ ihe na-egosi ogo pH ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọnọọgụ pH na-egosiwe site n'ihe ọkụkọ Hydrogen (akpọrọ "H" na pH) dị na kemịkal ahụ a na-anwale.

translations.source: Hydrogen ions are protons that had their electrons stripped off them (since Hydrogen atoms consist of one proton and one electron).
translations.reference: Ayọn Haịdrojin bụ protọn anaarala elektrọn ya (ebe atọm Haịdrojin nwere otu protọn na otu elektrọn).
translations.hypothesis: Ahụ ụzọ (hydrogen) bụ proton ndị e wepụrụ eletrọnụ ha (ebe ahụ ụzọ nwere proton otu na eletrọn otu).

translations.source: Swirl the two dry powders together and then, with clean wet hands, squeeze them into a ball.
translations.reference: Kpaharia kota nzu abuo ahu kporo-nku onu ma mgbe-ahu, na aka di mmiri ma dikwa ocha, pikoo ha ka ha ghoo boolu.
translations.hypothesis: Joo ndị afo efu abụọ ahụ ọnụ, wee, site n'aka dị ọcha na mmiri, pịa ha wee mee ha ka bụrụ nkụ.

translations.source: The moisture on your hands will react with the outer layers, which will feel funny and form a sort of shell.
translations.reference: Mpụta ya na mmiri dị gị n'aka ga-enwe mmekọrịta, nke ga-enye gị mmetụta dị aghaa ma mepụta ihe dị ka ọkpụkpụ mkpuchi.
translations.hypothesis: Mmiri dị n'aka gị ga-ebute mgbanwe na akụkụ ndị ọzọ, nke ga-adị iche na otu e ji ya, ma ọ ga-ebute ụdị akpụkpọ.

translations.source: The cities of Harappa and Mohenjo-daro had a flush toilet in almost every house, attached to a sophisticated sewage system.
translations.reference: Ọ fọrọ obere ka ụlọ niile dị n'obodo Harappa na Mohenjo-daro nwee mpochi mmiri, ya na usoro mkpopu kara aka.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo Harappa na Mohenjo-daro nwere ụlọ mposi dị ọcha na ụlọ karịa ọtụtụ, nke jikọtara ya na usoro mmechi mmiri dị mma.

translations.source: Remains of sewage systems have been found in the houses of the Minoan cities of Crete and Santorini in Greece.
translations.reference: A chọtala sistemu nsi fọdụrụnụ n’ụlọ Minoan ndị dị n’obodo Crete na Santorini na Greece
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ụlọ akụ na-egbuke egbuke emetụtawo n'ime ụlọ obodo ndị Minoan dị na Crete na Santorini, bụ ndị dị na Greece.

translations.source: There were also toilets in ancient Egypt, Persia and China. In Roman civilization, toilets were sometimes part of public bath houses where men and women were together in mixed company.
translations.reference: Ha nwekwara ụlọ mposi n'Ijipt mgbe ochie, Peshia na Chaịna. N'okpuru ọchịchị ndị Rom, mgbe ụfọdụ ụlọ mposi na-abụkarị otu akụkụ nke ụlọ ọsịsa ahụ ọha ebe ụmụ nwoke na ụmụ nwanyị nọkọtara ọnụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ebe ụlọ mposi dị na akụkọ ihe mere eme nke Egypt, Persia, na China. N'ime ọha Rome, ụlọ mposi bụkwa akụkụ nke ụlọ ịsa ọha ebe ndị nwoke na ndị inyom nọrọ ọnụ.

translations.source: When you call someone who is thousands of miles away, you are using a satellite.
translations.reference: Mgbe ikporo mmadu onye no otutu puku maili site n’ebe ino , ihe iji bu igwe satalaiti.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe ị na-akpọ onye dị na ebe dị anya, dị ka ebe dị elu narị kilomita, ị na-eji akụrịta.

translations.source: The satellite in space gets the call and then reflects it back down, almost instantly.
translations.reference: Satilaịti nọ n'ikuku na enweta oku ma zighachi ya n'ala na ntabi anya.
translations.hypothesis: Satelaịtị ahụ na-eri oku ahụ n'elu ụwa, wee gaa n'azụ na-ebufe ya na-agbaji, n'oge adịghị ka ọtụtụ.

translations.source: The satellite was sent into space by a rocket. Scientists use telescopes in space because the Earth’s atmosphere distorts some of our light and view.
translations.reference: E ji ụgbọelu rọkeetị zije satilaịti n'ikuku. Ndị ọka mmụta sayensị na eji igwe nyocha kpakpando afụ ụzọ n'ikuku mpụga ụwa n'ihi na igwe ụwa anyị na arọgharị ụfọdụ ọkụ anyị na ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ nduzi ahụ bịarutere n'elu ụwa site na obere ọkpụkpụ. Ndị ọkàiwu na-eji teleskọpụ n'elu ụwa n'ihi na ikuku ụwa na-agbanwe ụfọdụ ọkụ na ihe anyị na-ahụ.

translations.source: It takes a giant rocket over a 100 feet high to put a satellite or telescope in space.
translations.reference: O na-ewe nnukwu rọketi gafere ụkwụ otu narị n’elu itinye otu satịlaịtị na teliskop n’eluụwa.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ chọrọ obere ọgụgụọ dị ukwuu, karịrị ụkwụ 100, iji tinye satelaịtị ma ọ bụ teleskọpụ n'elu ụwa.

translations.source: The wheel has changed the world in incredible ways. The biggest thing that the wheel has done for us is given us much easier and faster transportation.
translations.reference: Wiilu agbanweela ụwa n'ụdị enweghị atụ. Ihe kachasị ukwu nke wiilu merela anyị bụ na o nyere anyị ụzọ njem dị mfe ma dị ọsịsọ karịa.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ahụ emeela mgbanwe dị ukwuu n'ụwa. Uche kachasị mma bụ na ọrụ ahụ nyere anyị ụzọ ije ije na-adị mfe na ngwa ngwa.

translations.source: It has brought us the train, the car, and many other transportation devices.
translations.reference: O wetegoro anyị ụgbọoloko, ụgbọala na ọtụtụ akụrụngwa njem dị iche iche.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bịara anyị ụgbọ oloko, ụgbọ ala, na ọtụtụ ụdị ọrụ ndị ọzọ na-enyere anyị aka na njem.

translations.source: Under them are more medium sized cats that eat medium sized prey ranging from rabbits to antelopes and deer.
translations.reference: N'okpuru ha bụ ụmụ nwamba ha ọkara na-eri anụoriri ha ọkara nke nwere ike isi na oke bekee ruo na ele nakwa mgbada.
translations.hypothesis: N'okpuru ha, enwere ụmụ osisi ndị dị obere, bụ ndị na-eri anụ ndị dịkwa obere, dị ka ụmụ nkita, ụmụ ntị, na ụmụ ọzụ.

translations.source: Finally, there are many small cats (including loose pet cats) that eat the far more numerous small prey like insects, rodents, lizards, and birds.
translations.reference: N’ikpeazụ, e nwere ọtụtụ obere nwamba (gụnyere anụ ụlọ nwamba furu efu) na-eri ọtụtụ obere ụmụ anụmanụ dị ka ụmụ ahụhụ, oke, ngwere, na nnụnụ.
translations.hypothesis: N'aka nke ọzọ, enwere ọtụtụ ụmụ agụrụ obere (gụnyere agụrụ obere ndị na-agba egwu) na-eri nri obere, dị ka anụ ọhịa, ụmụ anụ, ụmụ aja, na ụmụ anụ ọhịa, bụ ndị dịkarị elu.

translations.source: The secret to their success is the concept of the niche, a special job each cat holds that keeps it from competing with others.
translations.reference: Ihe nzuzo nke ọganihu ha bụ gburugburu ebe obibi, ọrụ nwamba niile ji nke na egbochi ịsọmpi ha na ndị ọzọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịmma ha bụ ihe omume "niche," nke bụ ọrụ pụrụ iche nke ọ bụla n'ime ụmụ agụụ ahụ na-eme, nke na-egbochi ya ịmakụrịta ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: Lions are the most social cats, living in large groups called prides.
translations.reference: Ọdụm bụ nwamba kachasị emekọrịta n'onwe ha, na-ebi na nnukwu òtù akpọrọ nganga.
translations.hypothesis: Anya ụlọ bụ ụmụ anụ ụlọ nke na-adịkarị na otu, na ha bi n'ọtụtụ otu ndị ahụ nke a na-akpọ "pride".

translations.source: Prides are made up of one to three related adult males, along with as many as thirty females and cubs.
translations.reference: Mpako gasị bụ otu ruo atọ ụmụ nwoke tozuru oke metụtaranụ mejupụtara ya, yana ụmụ nwanyị na ụmụ ya dị ọtụtụ dị ka iri atọ.
translations.hypothesis: Otu "pride" nwere otu ruo atọ nwoke ndị toro, na-akpọrọ ha, yana ụdị ụmụ nwanyị na ụmụaka ruo otu iri atọ.

translations.source: The females are usually closely related to each other, being a large family of sisters and daughters.
translations.reference: Ndị nwanyị na-emetụtakarị nke ukwu n’onwe ha, n’ibu otu nnukwu ezinụlọ nke ụmụnne nwanyị na ụmụ nwa nwanyị.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ndị nwanyị ahụ na-abụkarị ndị nọ n'otu ezinụlọ, bụ ndị chị na ụmụ nwanyị na-erubeghị.

translations.source: Lion prides act much like packs of wolves or dogs, animals surprisingly similar to lions (but not other big cats) in behavior, and also very deadly to their prey.
translations.reference: Ezinụlọ Ọdụm na-akpa agwa ka ezinụlọ oke nkịta ọhịa maọbụ nkịta ụlọ, anụ ndị nwere oyiyi dị ịtụ n'anya nye Ọdụm (mana odịghị otu a n'ebe nnukwu nwamba ndị ọzọ nọ) n'omume, ma bụrụ ihe oke iyi egwu nye ihe ọbụla ha na-achụ na nta.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị ọdụm, mgbe ha na-eme ihe, na-eme otu ụzọ ahụ dị ka otu ndị enwe ma ọ bụ nkita, bụ ndị anụmanụ nke na-erughị iche iche na ndị ọdụm (ma ọ bụghị ndị ụlọ ọdụ ndị ọzọ), na ha na-ekwesịkarịkwa ime ihe ike na ndị ha na-eji eme nri.

translations.source: A well rounded athlete, the tiger can climb (though not well), swim, leap great distances and pull with five times the force of a strong human.
translations.reference: Ome ihe egwuregwu zuruoke nkeoma, agu ahu ga enyili elu (obu ezie na obughi nkeoma), gwuo mmiri, maa-amaa garuo ebe di oke anya ma doo okpukpu ise dika ike mmadu di ike nwere ike ido.
translations.hypothesis: Onye ndi egwuregwu na-eme nke ọma, ụjọ ahụ nwere ike ịgbawa (ọ bụ ezie na ọ naghị eme ya nke ọma), ịsa, ịgbawa n'ebe dị anya, na ịdọta ihe site na ike karịrị ụma mmadụ ike karịrị ise.

translations.source: The tiger is in the same group (Genus Panthera) as lions, leopards, and jaguars. These four cats are the only ones who can roar.
translations.reference: Agụ nọ n’otu otu (Genus Panthera) dika ọdụm, owuru, na jaguar. Nwamba anọ ndị a bụ naanị ndị nwere ike ime mbigbọ.
translations.hypothesis: Anya, nke bụ ụlọ osisi, dị n'otu otu (genus) ahụ na ụlọ ọdụ, ụlọ ọdụ agwaetiti, na ụlọ ọdụ obere. Ndị ọdụ anọ ndị a bụ naanị ndị nwere ike ịgba egwu.

translations.source: The tiger's roar is not like the full-voiced roar of a lion, but more like a sentence of snarly, shouted words.
translations.reference: Ụja agụ adịghị ka mgbọpụta n'uju ụja ọdụm, mana ọ dị nnọọ ka okwu e kwuputara n'iti mkpu.
translations.hypothesis: Ọkụkọ ahụ anaghị eme mkparịta ụda dị ka ọkụkọ ahụ na-eme, kama ọ na-eme ụda dị ka okwu ndị na-agba gbaa na-agba ihu.

translations.source: Ocelots like to eat small animals. They will catch monkeys, snakes, rodents and birds if they can. Almost all of the animals that the ocelot hunts are far smaller than it is.
translations.reference: Ona amasi Ocelot iri obere umu-anumanu. Ha ga anwuchi enwe, agwo, oke na nnunu ma ha nwee ike. Oka-na-onuogugu anu anumanu nile Ocelot na achu-nta di obere nnukwu karia ka odi.
translations.hypothesis: Ocelot na-amasị iri anụmanụ obere. Ha ga-achọta mkpụrụ osisi, mkpụrụ nkwụ, anụ ọhịa, na ụma ma ha nwee ike. Anụmanụ nke ukwuu nke ocelot na-achọ bụkarị obere karịa ya.

translations.source: Scientists think that ocelots follow and find animals to eat (prey) by smell, sniffing for where they've been on the ground.
translations.reference: Ndị oke mmụta sayensị cheere na nwamba Oselọt ji isi esochi ma na-achọta anụ ha ga eri, site na ịkpọkwa imi n'ala iji site ebe ha gara.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị ọchịchịmma na-eche na ụmụ oké-egwu oké-obosara na-eso ụmụ anụmanụ ma chọpụta ha iji rie (anụ), site n'ịlegharị ihu na ịghachite ụzọ ha gara n'ala.

translations.source: They can see very well in the dark with night vision, and move very stealthily, too. Ocelots hunt their prey by blending in with their surroundings then pouncing on their prey.
translations.reference: Ha na-ahụ ụzọ nke ọma n'abalị, ma na ejegharịkwa na nzuzo karịa. Oselọotụ na agwakọta onwe ha na gburugburu ha iji nwude anụ ha na achụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ha nwere ike ịhụ nke ọma n'okwu, ọbụna n'ime obere ọkụ, site n'aka nke ọzọ, ha na-agba ọsọ nke ọma. Oké otu anụ ọhịa na-achọ anụ ndị ọ na-eri site n'ịgbatị onwe ha na gburugburu ha, wee gbaa anụ ndị ahụ.

translations.source: When a small group of living things (a small population) gets separated from the main population that they came from (like if they move over a mountain range or a river, or if they move to a new island so that they can't easily move back) they will often find themselves in a different environment than they were in before.
translations.reference: Mgbe ọbụla ụmụ obere ihe dị ndụ (obere ọnụ ọgụgụ yiri onwe ha) si na ndị otu ha pụọ (dịka ha gafee ugwu, osimiri, maọbụ gaa n'agwaetiti ọzọ ebe ọ ga-ara ahụ isi laghachi) ha ga-achọta onwe ha na gburugburu di iche ọtụtụ mgbe.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe otu obere ndị ndụ (otu obere ọha) kewara wee pụọ n'ọha bụọzi ha si, (dịka mgbe ha gaa site n'ihe ndụ, ma ọ bụ osimiri, ma ọ bụ mgbe ha gaa n'ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ọhụrụ ebe ha enweghịkwa mfe ịlaghachi) ha ga-ahụ onwe ha na-anọ n'ebe dị iche na ebe ha nọ tupu.

translations.source: This new environment has different resources and different competitors, so the new population will need different features or adaptations to be a strong competitor than what they had needed before.
translations.reference: Gburugburu ọhụrụ a nwere akụrụngwa dị iche ma ndị ịsọmpi dị iche, n'ihi nke a ọnụọgụgụ ọhụrụ ahụ kwesịrị inwe akụrụngwa dị iche maọbụ ihe mmegharị ọzọ ga eme ya ka ọbụrụ onye ịsọmpi dị ike karịa ka ọdịbu.
translations.hypothesis: Ebe ọhụrụ a nwere ụdị akụrụngwa dị iche iche na ndị asọmpi dị iche iche, ya mere, ndị bi ebe ahụ ga-achọ ụdị ihe dị iche iche ma ọ bụ mmezi iji bụrụ onye asọmpi ike karịa ihe ha chọrọ tupu.

translations.source: The original population hasn't changed at all, they still need the same adaptations as before.
translations.reference: Ọnụọgụgụ nke izizi agbanwebeghị maọlị, ha ka chọrọ ihe mmegharị dịka nke mgbe mbụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịdị mmadụ mbụ ahụ adịghị agbanwe, ha ka chọrọ otu ihe ndị ahụ ha na-achọrọ tupu.

translations.source: Over time, as the new population begins to adapt to their new environment, they start to look less and less like the other population.
translations.reference: Ka oge na-aga, dịka gburugburu ha ọhụrụ bidoro mawa ha ahụ, oyiyi ha na ndị ha hapụrụ ebido na-ebelata.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge na-aga, ka ndị mmadụ ahụ ochie na-amụta ibanye n'ebe ha jiri, ha na-amalite ịbụkarị ndị dị iche na ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: Eventually, after thousands or even millions of years, the two populations will look so different that they can't be called the same species.
translations.reference: Mgbe puku afọ maọbụ rịị nde afọ ụfọdụ gasịrị, otu abụọ a ga adị nnọọ iche ruo oke ebe agaghịzị akpọ ha abụọ otu ụdị.
translations.hypothesis: N'aka ekwu, mgbe ọtụtụ puku, ma ọ bụ ọbụrụ na ọtụtụ nde afọ gasịrị, abụọ ndị otu ahụ ga-adị iche nke ukwuu, ruo ebe ha agaghịzi enwe ike ịkọwa ha dị ka otu ụdị anụmanụ.

translations.source: We call this process speciation, which just means the formation of new species. Speciation is an unavoidable consequence and a very important part of evolution.
translations.reference: Anyi na-akpọ usoro a speciation, nke pụtara nguzobe nke ụdị okike ọhụụ. Speciation bụ nsonaazụ a na-apụghị ịgbagha agbagha na akụkụ dị oke mkpa nke evolushọn.
translations.hypothesis: Anyị na-akpọ usoro a "speciation," nke pụtara naanị mmepụta ụdị anụmanụ ọhụrụ. Speciation bụ ihe zuru ezu na-abịa n'ụzọ zuru oke, yana akụkụ dị mkpa nke mmegharị.

translations.source: Plants make oxygen which humans breathe, and they take in carbon-dioxide which humans exhale (that is, breathe out).
translations.reference: Osisi na-eme ikuku oksigin nke mmadụ na-ekuru, ma ha na e kubanye carbon-dioxide nke mmadụ na-ekufu ume (ya bụ, na-ekufu ume).
translations.hypothesis: Ahụhụ na-emepụta oxygen nke mmadụ na-asụ, ma ha na-etinye carbon dioxide nke mmadụ na-akụ (nke bụ ihe ọzọ dị ka ịsụ ụfụ).

translations.source: Plants make their food from the sun by photosynthesis. They also provide shade.
translations.reference: Akụmakụ osisi na emepụta nri nke ha site n’anyanwụ site n’aka fotosintesis. Ha na-enyekwa ndo.
translations.hypothesis: Osisi na-emepụta nri ha site na anyanwụ site na usoro ahụ nke a na-akpọ "photosynthesis." Ha na-enyekwa ụdị ụgwọ.

translations.source: We make our houses from plants and make clothes from plants. Most foods that we eat are plants. Without plants, animals could not survive.
translations.reference: Anyị ji osisi eme ụlọ na akwa. Ọtụtụ nri anyị na-eri bụ osisi. Ewepụ osisi, anụmanụ agaghị adị ndụ.
translations.hypothesis: Anyị na-ewu ụlọ anyị site na osisi, nakwa na-eme uwe site na osisi. Ọtụtụ nri anyị na-eri bụ osisi. Ọ bụrụ na enweghị osisi, anụ ọhịa enweghị ike ịdiri ndụ.

translations.source: Mosasaurus was the apex predator of its time, so it feared nothing, except other mosasaurs.
translations.reference: Mosasaurus bụbu isi n'anụ na-eri anụ n’oge ya, nke a mere na onweghi ihe na-atụ ya egwu, karịa mosasaurs ibe ya.
translations.hypothesis: Mosasaurus bụ onye na-eri ndị ọzọ n'oge ahụ, ya mere ọ nwere ọghọm na ihe ọ bụla, eweghachịrị ndị mosasaurus ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: Its long jaws were studded with more than 70 razor-sharp teeth, along with an extra set in the roof of its mouth, meaning that there was no escape for anything that crossed its path.
translations.reference: Agba ogologo ya bụ nke emejupụtara n'iji ihe karịrị eze dị aguba-nkọ iri asaa, yana òtú òtù mmezi n'elu ọnụ ya, nke pụtara na ọ nweghị ụzọ mgbapụ maka ihe ọ bụla gafere n'ụzọ ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ahụ ya nwere obere afọ dị ogologo, na-ebu karịa 70 ezigbo ntutu dị mkpụrụ, yana otu ọzọ na elu afọ ya, nke pụtara na ọ nweghị ebe ọ bụla ọ pụrụ ịgbapụ maka ihe ọ bụla bụ nke guzoro n'ụzọ ya.

translations.source: We don't know for sure, but it may have had a forked tongue. Its diet included turtles, large fish, other mosasaurs, and it may even have been a cannibal.
translations.reference: Onweghị anyị anya, mana ọ dịka onwere ire abụọ. Ọ na eri mbe mmiri, nnukwu azụ, anụ ndị yiri ya, onwekwara ike na eri ụdị nke ya.
translations.hypothesis: Anyị amabeghị nke ọma, mana ọ nwere ike inwe olili dị ka mkpụrụ osisi. Nri ya gụnyere ụkọ, azụ ndị dị ukwuu, mosasaurs ndị ọzọ, ọ bụghị naanị ya, ọ nwere ike ịbụ onye na-eri ndị mmadụ.

translations.source: It also attacked anything that entered the water; even a giant dinosaur such as T. rex would be no match for it.
translations.reference: Ọ wakpọkwara ihe ọ bụla banyere n’ime mmiri ahụ; ọbụná nnukwu dainosọọ dị ka T. rex abụghị atụ n’ebe ọ nọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ nakwa ihe ọ bụla tinyere n'ime mmiri; ọbụna onye ndụ ọhụrụ dị ukwuu dịka T. rex enweghịkwa ike ịlụ ọgụ ya.

translations.source: While most of their food would be familiar to us, Romans did have their share of strange or unusual feast items, including wild boar, peacock, snails, and a type of rodent called a dormouse
translations.reference: Ka anyị maara nke ọma imirikiti nri ha, ndị Rom nwere oke ha na ihe erimeeri ijuanya ma ọ bụ pụrụ iche, gụnyere ezi ọhịa, piikọkụ, ejula, na ụdị oke akpọrọ dormouse.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na ọtụtụ nri ndị Rom ha na-eri ga-adị anyị ma ama, ndị Rom nwekwara ụdị nri ndị ọzọ na-adị iche ma ọ bụ na-adịghị ahụ anya, gụnyere anụ ọhịa, ọkụkọ, akwụkwọ nri, na ụdị anụ ọhịa nke a na-akpọ "dormouse."

translations.source: Another difference was that while the poor people and the woman ate their food while sitting in chairs, the rich men liked to have banquets together where they would lounge on their sides while they ate their meals.
translations.reference: Ihe ọzọ dị iche bụ na ebe ndị ogbenye na nwanyị ahụ riri nri ha ka ha nọ ọdụ n'oche, ndị ọgaranya na-enwe mmasị inwe mmemme oriri ebe ha ga-eri nke ha n'ezumike.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ ọ dị iche bụ na, ebe ndị mmadụ na-ebute nri ha na nwanyị ahụ nọrịrị na oche, ndị mmadụ ndị nwere akụ nwere mmasị ịgbakọta ọnụ iji rie nri, ebe ha nọrịrị n'akụkụ ha na-eri nri ha.

translations.source: Ancient Roman meals couldn't have included foods that came to Europe from America or from Asia in later centuries.
translations.reference: Ụmụ nri Ndị Rome Ndị mgbe ochie enwughị ike ịgụnye nri ndị batara Yurop site na Amerịka ma ọ bụ Eshịa na narị afọ ndị na-esotenu.
translations.hypothesis: Nri ndị Romano ochie enweghị ike ịgụ nri ndị sitere na Amerika ma ọ bụ Asia, nke bịara Europe n'oge ndị na-abịa.

translations.source: For instance, they didn't have corn, nor tomatoes, nor potatoes, nor cocoa, and no ancient Roman ever tasted a turkey.
translations.reference: Na imaatu, ha enweghi oka, nweghi tomato, nweghi poteto, nweghi koko, na onweghi onye Rome mgbeochie deturu anu toro-toro ire.
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, ha nweghị ọka, ọ bụla, tomato, ọ bụla, poteto, ọ bụla, na cocoa, ọ bụla, ọ dịkwa mma na onye ọ bụla n'oge Rome ochie adịghị eji anụ ọkụkpa.

translations.source: The Babylonians built each of their gods a primary temple that was considered the home of the god.
translations.reference: Ndị Babịlọn rụrụ otu n’ime chi ha otu isi ụlọ nsọ nke e were ka ebe obibi chi ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị Babylon bụrụla otu ụlọ elu dị mkpa maka onye ọ bụla n'ime chi ha, bụ́ọla ụlọ echekwara dị ka ebe oburu chi ahụ.

translations.source: People would bring sacrifices to the gods and the priests would try to attend to the needs of the gods through ceremonies and festivals.
translations.reference: Ebe ndị mmadụ wetaara chi ndị ahụ aja, ndị nchụ aja ahụ maka ihe ha bụ chi na-achọ, site n'emume na mmemme di iche iche.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị mmadụ na-ebute ihe ndị a na-eji eme nsọ na Chineke, ma ndị ohi na-agbalị inye Chineke ihe ndị ọ chọrọ site na usoro na ememme.

translations.source: Each temple had an open temple courtyard and then an inner sanctuary that only the priests could enter.
translations.reference: Ulo-uka n’otu n’otu nwere mbara-ezi ulo-uka ma nwekazie ime ebe nchuaja ebe nani onye-isi nchu-aja nwere-ike ibanye.
translations.hypothesis: Otu ụlọ elu ọkụ nwere ebe mpụta dị n'èzí, wee n'ime ya nwere ụlọ dị ukwuu ebe naanị ndị ntorobịa ka nwee ike ịbanye.

translations.source: Sometimes special pyramid shaped towers, called ziggurats, were built to be a part of the temples.
translations.reference: Ụfọdụ oge a na arụnye ụlọ elu nwere oyiyi oiramid, ndị akpọrọ ziggurats, ka ha bụrụ osonye ụlọ okpukpe.
translations.hypothesis: N'ọtụtụ oge, ụlọ elu dị iche, nke a na-akpọ "ziggurats," nke nwere ọdịdị pyramid, a na-ewu ha iji bụrụ akụkụ nke ụlọ nsọ.

translations.source: The top of the tower was special sanctuary for the god.
translations.reference: Elu ụlọ elu a bụ ebe dị nsọ pụrụ iche nye chi ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdụ elu ụlọ ahụ bụ ebe nzuzo pụrụ iche ebe chi ahụ nọrịrị.

translations.source: In the warm climate of the Middle East, the house was not so important.
translations.reference: Na ekpem-oku nke udidi na mba ndi etiti owuwa-anyanwu, ulo ahu abachaghi uru.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime ihu igwe ọkụ nke ebe ugwu na ndịda Anyịshịa, ụlọ ahụ abụghị ihe dị mkpa.

translations.source: Most of the life of the Hebrew family happened in the open air.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ ihe ezinụlọ ndị juu a mere, ọ bụ n'anya onye ọbụla ka ha mere ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ akụkụ nke ndụ ezinụlọ ndị Ijipt bụ na ha nọrịrị n'ebe mpụta.

translations.source: Women did the cooking in the yard; stores were just open counters looking into the street. Stone was used for building houses.
translations.reference: Ụmụ nwanyị siri nri na mbara eze; ụmụ ụlọ ahịa wụbụ naanị ọgụego mepere emepe na-elefe anya n'okporo ámá. E jire okwute maka ịrụ ụlọ.
translations.hypothesis: Nwanyị ndị na-eme nri n'ụlọ. Ụlọ ahịa ndị ahụ bụ naanị tebụl ndị emere, na-egosi ụzọ. A na-eji ígwè eme ụlọ.

translations.source: There were no large forests in the land of Canaan, so wood was extremely expensive.
translations.reference: O nweghị ụmụ ọhịa buru ibu n’ala nke Keenan, ya mere osisi na-ada oke ọnụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dịghị ọhịa dị ukwuu n'obodo Canaan, ya mere, ọnụ ahịa osisi dị oke ọnụ.

translations.source: Greenland was settled sparsely. In the Norse sagas they say that Erik the Red was exiled from Iceland for murder, and when travelling further west, found Greenland and named it Greenland.
translations.reference: Ndị mmadụ anọjughị otu ebe na Grinland. N'akụkọ Norse ha sị na achụfuru Erik the Red n'obodo Iceland n'ihi igbu ọchụ, ma mgbe ọ na aga njem na mgbada ọdịda anyanwụ, ọchọpụtara Grinland wee gụọ ya Grinland.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ụlọ Greenland nwere obere mmadụ. N'ọtụtụ akụkọ ndị Norse, a kwuru na Erik "Ọkpụkpụ Ọhịa" bịarutere n'Iceland n'ihi mmejọ ọrụ, ma mgbe ọ gara n'ebe ndịda ọdịda anyanwụ, ọ chọpụtara Greenland wee kpọọ ya Greenland.

translations.source: But regardless of his discovery, Eskimo tribes were already living there at the time.
translations.reference: Mana n'agbanyeghi nchọpụta ya, agbụrụ Ezkimo ebirilarị ebe ahụ n'oge ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Mana, n'agbanyeghị ihe ọ chọpụtara, ndị otu Eskimo ka nọrị na ebe ahụ na oge ahụ.

translations.source: Though each country was 'Scandinavian', there were many differences between the people, kings, customs and history of Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Iceland.
translations.reference: N'agbanyeghị na obodo ọbụla bụ 'mba Skandinevia', enwere ọtụtụ ihe dị iche n'etiti ndị, ndị eze, omenala, na akụkọ ihe mere na Denmak, Swiden, Nọọwe na Aisland.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na ọ bụ "Scandinavia" maka mba ọ bụla, enwere ọtụtụ ọdịiche n'etiti ndị mmadụ, ndị ala, ọdịnụ na akụkọ ihe mere dị na Denmark, Sweden, Norway, na Iceland.

translations.source: If you have watched the movie National Treasure, you may think a treasure map was written on the back of the Declaration of Independence.
translations.reference: Ọ bụrụ na ileela ihe nkiri a na-akpọ Akụ nke Mba, i nwere ike chee na e dere otu maapụ akụ n'azụ nke Nkwupụta nke Nnwere Onwe ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na ị hụrụ ihe nkiri ahụ bụ "National Treasure," ọ nwere ike ịbụ na ị chere na akwụkwọ akụkọ nke ụlọ ọrụ ahụ (Declaration of Independence) nwere akụkọ nke ebe ezuola ihe omume.

translations.source: However, that is not true. Although there is something written on the back of the document, it is not a treasure map.
translations.reference: Agbanyeghị, nke ahụ abụghị eziokwu. N’agbanyeghị na enwere ihe edere n’azụ nke dọkumentị ahụ, ọ bụghị otu maapụ akụ.
translations.hypothesis: Otú ọ dị, nke ahụ abụghị eziokwu. Ọ bụ ezie na enwere ihe edebiiri n'azụ akwụkwọ ahụ, ọ bụghị akwụkwọ nduzi maka ịchọta ihe omume.

translations.source: Written on the back of the Declaration of Independence were the words "Original Declaration of Independence dated 4th July 1776". The text appears on the bottom of the document, upside down.
translations.reference: Ka-edere na azu nkwuputa nke nnoro-onwe bu okwua “Nkwuputa nke Nnoro-onwe Nke bu ezie ubochi abali 4 juli 1776” .Ederede ahu putara na ala-ala akwukwo ahu, kpodo isi na-ala.
translations.hypothesis: N'azụ akwụkwọ "Declaration of Independence" (Nkwuputa Ọnwe), e dere okwu ndị a: "Akwụkwọ Nkwuputa Ọnwe mbụ, nke e mere na 4th Julaị, afọ 1776". Ozi ahụ egosiri n'okpuru akwụkwọ ahụ, na ụdị nke efu.

translations.source: While no one knows for certain who wrote it, it is known that early in its life, the large parchment document (it measures 29¾ inches by 24½ inches) was rolled up for storage.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ ezie na ọnweghị onye maara nke ọma onye dere ya, amaara na mmalite na ndụ ya, afụkọtara nnukwu dọkụment e jiri akpụkpọ anụ mee (o nwere nha inchì 29¾ site na inchì 24½) ọnụ maka nchekwa.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na enweghị onye ma nke ọma onye dere akwụkwọ ahụ, amaliwo na na ngwá ọrụ ahụ (onyere ibu 29¾ inch site na 24½ inch) bịara na mbụ, a jiri ya tụgharịa wee tọgharịa ya maka nchekwa.

translations.source: So, it is likely that the notation was added simply as a label.
translations.reference: Ya mere, ọ dị ka agbakwụnyere ihe ngosi a dị ka akara njirimara naanị.
translations.hypothesis: Ya mere, ọ bụ ihe dị mma na akwụkwọ ahụ echetara ahụrụ ya naanị dịka akara iji akọwa ya.

translations.source: The D-Day landings and the following battles had freed the north of France, but the south still wasn't free.
translations.reference: Ubochi-ubochi nladata ya agha ndi na esota atohapula mpaghara ugwu nke France, mana mpaghara ndida enwerebekwa onwe ha.
translations.hypothesis: Agbanyeghị na mbibi nke "D-Day" na ọgụ ndị bịara mgbe ahụ wetere ọdịmma n'ebe ugwu France, akụkụ ndịda ahụ ka nwere ọtụtụ nsogbu.

translations.source: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.
translations.reference: Ndị chịrị ya bụ ndị "Vichy" French. Ndị a bụ ndị mba Frans ndị ha na ndị mba Jamini mere udo n'afọ 1940 ma soro ndị iro rụkọọ ọrụ karịa ịlụso ha ọgụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ndị "Vichy" nke mba France nwere ikike n'ebe ahụ. Ndị a bụ ndị France nke mechara kweta udo na ndị German na afọ 1940, ma soro ndị nọrọ na mba ahụ, ọ bụghị ịlụ ọgụ ha.

translations.source: On 15 August 1940, the Allies invaded southern France, the invasion was called "Operation Dragoon".
translations.reference: N'ụbọchị nke iri na ise nke ọnwa Ọgọọstụ n'afọ 1940, ndị enyi busoro mpaghara ndịda nke Frans agha, akpọrọ nke a "Operation Dragoon".
translations.hypothesis: Ná Ọgọọgọ 15, afọ 1940, ndị otu agha nke "Allies" gbara ọsọ banye n'ebe ndịda France, ma a kpọrọ agha ahụ ahụ "Operation Dragoon".

translations.source: In just two weeks the Americans and Free French forces had liberated southern France and were turning towards Germany.
translations.reference: N'ime nanị izu abụọ ndị agha America na Ndị French nke Nweere onwe ha emeela ka ndịda France nwere onwe ha ma wee na-atụgharị echewe ihu na Germany.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime naanị izu abụọ, ndị America na ndị agha France nke ndị nchọpụta ụlọ ọrụ ahụ kọwara ụdị ọchịchị dị iche na-achọghị ịkwado akụnụba na-emepe emepe, kọwara ụdị ọchịchị dị translations.source: A civilization is a singular culture shared by a significant large group of people who live and work co-operatively, a society.
translations.reference: Ọdịnala bụ otu omenaala ọha mmadụ buru ibu na-ebi ma na-arụkọ ọrụ ọnụ, a na-akpọ ọha mmadụ a sosayiti.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịnala bụ usoro ndụ na ọrụ otu, nke ndi mmadụ na-echekwube, na-eme uche dị iche iche, na-arụkọ ọrụ ọnụ, na-eme ka ọ dị ka otu obodo.

translations.source: The word civilization comes from the Latin civilis, meaning civil, related to the Latin civis, meaning citizen, and civitas, meaning city or city-state, and that also somehow defines the size of the society.
translations.reference: Ahịrịokwu "civilization" si n'okwu Latin bụ civilis, nke pụtara "gbasara obodo", nke metụtara okwu Latin bụ civis, nke pụtara onye obodo, na civitas, nke pụtara obodo maọbụ obodo-steeti, nke ahụ nwekwara otu o si egosi nha nke ọha mmadụ.
translations.hypothesis: Asụsụ "civilization" si na Latin "civilis," nke pụtara "ọchịchị," na-esokachi Latin "civis," nke pụtara "onye obodo," na "civitas," nke pụtara "obodo" ma ọ bụ "obodo na-achị onwe ya," yana nke a, n'otu ụzọ, na-akọwapụta nha nke obodo ahụ.

translations.source: City-states are the precursors of nations. A civilizational culture implies the passing on of knowledge across several generations, a lingering cultural footprint and fair dissemination.
translations.reference: Steeti-obodo gasị bụ obu ụzọ nke ụmụ mba. Omenaala kemmepeanya pụtara nnyefe nke ihe ọmụma n'etiti ọtụtụ ọgbọ, akaraụkwụ omenaala nke ka nọ ya na mgbasa dịtụ mma.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo ndị bi n'obodo bụ ihe mbụ nke mba. Ọdịmma nke ọdịnala pụtara itinye uche na itinye akụkọ na ọmụma n'aka ndị ọgbakọ dịpụrụ adịpụ, na-eme ka ọdịnala dịgide, na-ekesa ya n'ụzọ ziri ezi.

translations.source: Minor cultures often vanish without leaving relevant historic evidence and fail to be recognized as proper civilizations.
translations.reference: Ụmụ obere ọdịnala na-apụ n'anya na-ahapụghị ihe akaebe dị mkpa ya mere anaghị ahụta ha dị ka sivilaịzeshọn kwesịrị ekwesị.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ọdịnala obere ụlọ ọrụ na-apụ n'anya n'enweghị igbochi akụkọ ihe mere eme dị mkpa, na ha adịghị achọpụta dị ka ọchịchị dị mma.

translations.source: During the Revolutionary War, the thirteen states first formed a weak central government—with the Congress being its only component—under the Articles of Confederation.
translations.reference: Ka a na alụ agha ntụgharị, steeti iri na atọ ahụ bu ụzọ gbakọọ bido gọọmenti nchịkọta nke na adịghị ike - nke nzukọ bụ sọ ngalaba onwere- n'okpuru akwụkwọ obodo.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge agha nke mgbanwe ahụ, mba iri na atọ ahụ họpụtara ọchịchị etiti nke dịkwuo ike—na National Assembly bụ naanị akụkụ ya—site na iji usoro akụkọ ndụ nke njikọta.

translations.source: Congress lacked any power to impose taxes, and, because there was no national executive or judiciary, it relied on state authorities, who were often uncooperative, to enforce all its acts.
translations.reference: Nzukọ enweghị ike ike ụtụ ma n'ihi na enweghi ndị isi ọchịchị gọọmenti etiti maọbụ ndị omeiwu, ọ dabeere na ndị isi ọchịchị steeti, ndị anaghị enwe otu obi ọtụtụ oge ịkwado iwu ya nile.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ihe dị ka ụlọ akwụkwọ ahụ (Congress) nwere ike ịkpọ oku maka ụgwọ, mana, n'ihi na enweghị ọchịchị obodo ma ọ bụ ụlọ ikpe, ọ tụfedeere na ndị na-achị obodo, bụ ndị na-adịghị adịkarị n'aka, iji mezie ihe ọ bụla ọ rụrụ.

translations.source: It also had no authority to override tax laws and tariffs between states.
translations.reference: O nweghi ikike imechi iwu ụtụisi na tarifu n'etiti steeti na steeti.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ nwekwara ike ọ bụla iji megide iwu ụka na ụgwọ ahazipụ na-eje ebe dị iche iche.

translations.source: The Articles required unanimous consent from all the states before they could be amended and states took the central government so lightly that their representatives were often absent.
translations.reference: Ederede ahụ chọrọ nkweta steeti niile n'enweghi mgbagha tupu enwee ike imezi ha ma steeti ga weere gọọmentị etiti n'ihe efu ruo na ndị nnọchiteanya ha anaghị abịa.
translations.hypothesis: Ihe ndị otu họpụtara dị mkpa ka ụkpụrụ niile gbagharịa ya tupu enwe ike atụgharị ya, ma steeti ndị ahụ adịghị enye uche dị ukwuu n'ọchịchị etiti, ya mere ọtụtụ oge, ndị nnọchite anya ha adịghị na ebe.

translations.source: Italy's national football, along with German national football team is the second most successful team in the world and were the FIFA World Cup champions in 2006.
translations.reference: Ndị otu egwuregwu bọọlụ ukwu nke mba Itali, ya na ndị otu egwuregwu bọọlụ ukw nke mba Jamani bu ndị kacha eme nke ọma n'otu bọọlụ ukwu na mbaụwa ma bụrụkwa ndị nwetara mmeri n’iko mbaụwa nke afo 2006.
translations.hypothesis: Otu egwuregwu bọọlụ mba Italy, na otu egwuregwu bọọlụ mba Germany, bụ abụọ n'ime otu ndị meriri nke ọtụtụ egwuregwu n'ụwa, ma ha meriri asọmpi FIFA World Cup na afọ 2006.

translations.source: Popular sports include football, basketball, volleyball, water-polo, fencing, rugby, cycling, ice hockey, roller hockey and F1 motor racing.
translations.reference: Egwuregwu ndị a ma ama gụnyere futbọl, basketbọl, volleybọl, polo-mmiri, fencing, rugby, ịgba ịnyịnya, hockey ice, hockey roller na ịgba ọsọ ụgbọ ala F1.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị egwuregwu ndị a ma ama gụnyere bọọlụ, bọọlụ basketball, bọọlụ volleyball, egwuregwu mmiri, egwuregwu mkpọrọ, egwuregwu rugby, ịnya egbe, egwuregwu ice hockey, egwuregwu roller hockey, na asọmpi ọkpụkpọ F1.

translations.source: Winter sports are most popular in the Northern regions, with Italians competing in international games and Olympic events.
translations.reference: Egwuregwu oge oyi kachasị ewu ewu n'ugwu, ebe ndị mba Italy so asọ mpi n'egwuregwu mba na mba makwa na Olimpik.
translations.hypothesis: Egwu egwuregwu nke oge ọkụkọ na-adịkarị elu na mpaghara ndị dị n'ebe ugwu, ebe ndị Italy na-eseakọta na egwuregwu mba ụwa na egwuregwu Olympic.

translations.source: Japans holds nearly 7,000 islands (the biggest being Honshu), making Japan the 7th largest island in the world!
translations.reference: Mba Japan nwere isuo ruru nde asaa (nke kachasị ibu bụ isuo Honshu), nke a mere mba Japan isuo nke asaa kacha ibu n'ụwa.
translations.hypothesis: Japan nwere ihe karịrị 7,000 ọkpụkpụ (ịkpụkpụ kacha ukwuu bụ Honshu), na-eme ka Japan bụrụ ọkpụkpụ nke asaa kacha ukwuu n'ụwa!

translations.source: Due to the cluster/group of islands Japan has, Japan is often referred to, on a geographical stance, as an "archipelago"
translations.reference: N’ihi mkọkụlọta/òtù agwaetiti ahụ Japan nwere, a na-arụnyekarị Japan aka, n’elu etu ala ndị ahụ sị guzogide, dị ka "archipelago"
translations.hypothesis: N'ihi na Japan nwere ọtụtụ ọkpụkpụ anyanwụ na-agbakọta ọnụ, a na-akpọ Japan, n'ụdị echiche nke ọma, "obodo anyanwụ."

translations.source: Taiwan beginning start way back in 15th century where European sailors passing by record the island’s name as Ilha Formosa, or beautiful island.
translations.reference: Mbido mmepe Taịwan malitere n’oge gara aga nke narị afọ iri na ise mgbe ndị ọkwụ ụgbọ mmiri Ndị Yurop na-agafe dekọrọ aha agwaetiti ahụ dị ka Ilha Formosa, ma ọ bụ agwaetiti mara mma.
translations.hypothesis: Akụkọ Taiwan malitere kemgbe narị nke 15, mgbe ndị njalafu Europe nke gara ụsọ wee dee aha obere agwa ahụ dị ka "Ilha Formosa," ma ọ bụ "obere agwa mara mma."

translations.source: In 1624,Dutch East India Company establishes a base in southwestern Taiwan, initiating a transformation in aboriginal grain production practices and employing Chinese laborers to work on its rice and sugar plantations.
translations.reference: N'afọ 1624, Ụlọọrụ Dọch Isti Indịa mepere ụlọọrụ na ndịda ọdịdaanyanwụ Taịwan, bido mgbanwe n'otu e si emepụta mkpụrụ n'oge gboo, ma wee ndị ọkpọkọọrụ Chaịna ka ha rụọ ọrụ n'ugbo osikapa na nke shuga ha.
translations.hypothesis: N'afọ 1624, ụlọ ọrụ Dutch East India Company kọrọ ebe obibi na mpaghara ndịda-ọhụrụ Taiwan, wee malite mgbanwe na ụzọ ndị mmadụ ebe a na-eto osisi na ọrụ ugbo, wee jiri ndị ọrụ China arụ ọrụ na ala ha na-eto osisi na shuga.

translations.source: In 1683, Qing dynasty (1644-1912) forces take control of Taiwan’s western and northern coastal areas and declared Taiwan as a province of the Qing Empire in 1885.
translations.reference: N'afọ 1683, ndị agha ezinụlọ ọchịchị Shịng (1644-1912) weghaara akụkụ mmiri Taịwan dị n'ọdịda anyanwụ na nke dị n'ugwu ma kwuputa na Taịwan bụzi mpaghara n'okpuru ọchịchị Alaeze Shịng n'afọ 1885.
translations.hypothesis: N'afọ 1683, ndị agha nke Qing Dynasty (1644-1912) jidebebe mpaghara osimiri ndịda na ugwu Taiwan, wee gosi na Taiwan bụ otu obere obodo n'ime Qing Empire n'afọ 1885.

translations.source: In 1895, after defeat in the First Sino-Japanese War (1894-1895), the Qing government signs the Treaty of Shimonoseki, by which it cedes sovereignty over Taiwan to Japan, which rules the island until 1945.
translations.reference: Na 1895, mgbe a dachara n’Agha Sino-Japanese Mbụ (1894-1895), ọchịchị Qing ahụ mere mbịanye aka na Nkwekọrịta nke Shimonoseki ahụ, site na nke o jiri nyefee Japan ọbụbụeze nke Taiwan, nke na-achị agwaetiti ahụ ruo 1945.
translations.hypothesis: N'afọ 1895, mgbe a jidere ya n'agha mbụ Sino-Japan (1894-1895), gọọmentị Qing kwadoro nkwekọrịta Shimonoseki, bụ nke mere ka ọ nye Taiwan na Japan, nke tinyere aka n'ịzi otu ahụ ruo afọ 1945.

translations.source: Machu Picchu consist of three main structures, namely Intihuatana, the Temple of the Sun, and the Room of the Three Windows.
translations.reference: Machu Picchu nwere ọdịdị atọ, ya bụ Intihuatana, Ụlọ Nsọ nke Anyanwu, yana Ime ụlọ nke Windo Atọ.
translations.hypothesis: Machu Picchu nwere ụkpụrụ atọ bụ isi, bụ nke bụ Intihuatana, ụlọ nsọ Anyanwụ, na ụlọ nke nwere windo atọ.

translations.source: Most of the buildings on the edges of the complex have been rebuilt in order to give tourists a better idea of how they originally appeared.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ n'ime ụlọ ndị nọ na mpụta ogige ụlọ ahụ ka arụgharịrị ka enwee ike gosi ndị njem nleta echiche etu ha siri pụta na mbụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ụlọ ndị dị n'akụkụ ụlọ ọrụ ahụ emeela ka emebu ya ọhụrụ iji nye ndị njalaba ohere ịhụ otu ha si dị n'oge mbụ.

translations.source: By 1976, thirty percent of Machu Picchu had been restored and restoration continues till today.
translations.reference: Mgbe 1976 ruru, e mezigharịala pasent iri atọ nke Machu Pichu; mmezi a ka na-aga n'ihu ruo taa.
translations.hypothesis: N'afọ 1976, ihe dị ka asaa percent nke Machu Picchu echetara n'ọnọdụ ọhụrụ, ma arụmọrụ nke ịchetara ahụ ka na-aga n'ihu ruo taa.

translations.source: For example, the most common still image photography format in the world is 35mm, which was the dominant film size at the close of the analog film era.
translations.reference: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, nhàzi nka osise onyinyo nkwụ n'otu ebe a na-ahụkarị n'ụwa niile bụ 35mm, nke bụ nha fim kachasị ewu ewu na ngwụcha oge fim analọgụ.
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, ụdị foto nke na-adịkarị karịa n'ụwa niile bụ foto nke 35mm, bụ nke bụla nha fim kachasị ewu ewu n'oge na-agwụsị oge fim dijital.

translations.source: It is still produced today, but more importantly its aspect ratio has been inherited by digital camera image sensor formats.
translations.reference: A ka na-emepụta ya taa, mana ihe ka mkpa bụ na ụdịdị sensọ foto nke igwefoto dijital eketala aspekt reshiyo ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ ka na-emepụta ya taa, mana ọtụtụ ihe karịrị nke ahụ, ọnọọgụ akụkụ ya emeela ka emepụta ụdị sensor onyomanya nke kamera dijitalụ.

translations.source: The 35mm format is actually, somewhat confusingly, 36mm in width by 24mm in height.
translations.reference: Ọ dịtụ mgbagwoju anya na, n'ezie, ụdịdị 35mm nwere 36mm n'obosara na 24mm n'ogo.
translations.hypothesis: Usoro vidiyo nke 35mm, n'ezie, na-adịkarị 36mm n'agụba ma 24mm n'ogologo, nke na-ebute ụfọdụ mgbagwoju anya.

translations.source: The aspect ratio of this format (dividing by twelve to obtain the simplest whole-number ratio) is therefore said to be 3:2.
translations.reference: akuku rashio nke usoro a ( iji iri na-abuo were nweta rashio onu ogugu dikasiri mfe) bu 3:2 maka nke a.
translations.hypothesis: Ọkwa uhọrọ nke ụdị vidio a (ebelata ya site na ịsa apụ na iri abụọ iji nweta uhọrọ ahụ kacha mfe bụrụ ọnụọgụ uzo) bụ, n'ihi ya, a na-akọwa ya dị ka 3:2.

translations.source: Many common formats (APS family of formats, for example) are equal to or closely approximate this aspect ratio.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ usoro nkịtị (dịka usoro APS si n'otu ezinaụlọ) ga-abụ otu ihe maọbụ ruo ihe dịka nkepụta nkewa a.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ụdị dị nkịtị (dịka ụdị APS) bụ otu ahụ ma ọ bụ na ha dịkarịrị ya nso na ọkwa akụkụ a.

translations.source: The much-abused and often-ridiculed rule of thirds is a simple guideline creating dynamism while keeping a measure of order in an image.
translations.reference: Iwu nke atọ ndị a na-akparị ma na-akwakarị oke emu bụ usoro dị mfe na-emepụta ịdịmgbanwò dị ka ọ na-edotekwa otu ụhara usoro ọrụ n'ime otu onyinyo.
translations.hypothesis: Iwu "otu nke atọ" a, nke a na-eji eme ihe nke ukwuu ma ọtụtụ ndị na-ama ife, bụ usoro dị mfe nke na-enyere aka ịmepụta ọdịmma na ịdị ọcha n'ime onyonyo.

translations.source: It states that the most effective place for the main subject is at the intersection of lines dividing the image into thirds vertically and horizontally (see example).
translations.reference: O kwuru na ebe kachasị dị ire maka isi nke isiokwu bụ na mmekọta ụmụ ahịrị na-ekebi ụmụ onyinyo ahụ n’ụzọ atọ na nke eguzoro ọtọ nakwa nke a mara afọ n’ala (hụ ọmụmatụ).
translations.hypothesis: Ọ na-akọwapụta na ebe kacha mma iji tinye ihe bụ isi bụ n'ebe ọtụtụ ahịhịa na-etolite, bụ nke na-ekewa ihe oyiyi ahụ n'ụzọ vertical na horizontal n'ime atọ (lee ihe atụ).

translations.source: During this period of European history, the Catholic Church, which had become rich and powerful, came under scrutiny.
translations.reference: N'oge a na Yurop, e bidoro lebawa anya n'Ụka Katọlik, nke bagoro ụba ma dị ike.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge a nke akụkọ ihe mere dị na Europe, ụka Katọlik, nke mechara bụrụ nke nwere akụ na ikike, bịara n'anya ndị na-ele anya.

translations.source: For over a thousand years the Christian religion had bound European states together despite differences in language and customs. I
translations.reference: Kamgbe ihe karịrị otu puku afọ, okpukpe Ndị Kraịst jikọtara obodo ndị dị na Yuropu n'agbanyeghị na asụsụ na omenala ha dịgasị iche.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime ọtụtụ narụ ọta, okwukwu Kraistian jikọrọ mba ndị Europe ọnụ, ọ bụrụkwa na ha nwere ọdịiche n'asụsụ na ọdịnade.

translations.source: Its all-pervading power affected everyone from king to commoner.
translations.reference: Ike ya juputara ebe niile metụtara onye ọbụla site n'eze ruo na mmadụ nkịtị.
translations.hypothesis: Oge ahụ nwere ike dị ukwuu na emetụta ọtụtụ mmadụ, sitere n'aka eze ruo ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: One of the main Christian tenets is that wealth should be used to alleviate suffering and poverty and that the monetary funds of the church are there specifically for that reason.
translations.reference: Otu n'ime isi okwu okwukwe Ndị Kristian bu na ekwesiri iji akụ belata nhụjuanya na ịda ogbenye nakwa na ego ụka nọ kpọmkwem ebe ahụ n'ihi nke ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Otu n'ime ihe ndị bụ isi n'ime akụkọ Kristụ bụ na akụ na ụba ekwesịrị iji belata mgbu na ogbugbu, na akụ ụlọ ibe Kristi dị naanị maka ihe ahụ.

translations.source: The central authority of the church had been in Rome for over a thousand years and this concentration of power and money led many to question whether this tenet was being met.
translations.reference: Ikike keetiti ahụ nke ụlọ uka anọọla n'ime Rom karịa otu puku afọ ma mkpọkọnata ike na ego a duru ọtụtụ ndị ịjụ sị ma a na-esokwa ụkpụrụ ya.
translations.hypothesis: Oge ruuru ọtụtụ narị afọ, ọchịchị etiti nke ụka ahụ nọọrọ na Rome, ma ọtụtụ mmadụ jụrụ ajụ ma a na-adịgide n'ụkpọrọ nke otu esi eme ihe a, n'ihi na ọtụtụ ikike na ego nọọrọ n'ebe ahụ.

translations.source: Soon after the outbreak of hostilities, Britain initiated a naval blockade of Germany.
translations.reference: Ka agha dara, mba Britenị jiri ndị agha elu mmiri gbochie ndị Jamani inweta enyemaka
translations.hypothesis: Oge dịka nke merụrụ mgbe agha malitere, Britain malitere ịkwado ụkwụ mmiri iji gbochie ụgbọ mmiri Germany ịbịa na ịwụpụ.

translations.source: The strategy proved effective, cutting off vital military and civilian supplies, although this blockade violated generally accepted international law codified by several international agreements of the past two centuries.
translations.reference: Atụmatụ ahụ rụrụ ọrụ ọfụma, na-ebepụ ụmụ ihe mbute ihe ndị agha na ndị nkiti dị oke mpka, n’agbanyeghị na mgbochi a dara iwu mba ụwa anabatara n’izugbe nke ọtụtụ nkwekọrịta n’etiti mba ụwa nke afọ narị abụọ gara aga nyere ikikere.

translations.source: Britain mined international waters to prevent any ships from entering entire sections of ocean, causing danger to even neutral ships.
translations.reference: Briten tinyere ogbunigwe na mmiri ọha mba igbochi ụgbọ mmiri ọbụla ịbata, nke a abụrụ ihe ize ndụ nye ụgbọ mmiri ndị esoghi alụ agha.
translations.hypothesis: Íngland jiri ụgbọ mmiri eme ihe iji mepụta ihe na osimiri mba ụwa, iji gbochie ụgbọ mmiri ọ bụla ịbanye n'akụkụ ụfọdụ osimiri ahụ, nke mere ka ọ bụrụ ihe ize ndụ, ọbụna maka ụgbọ mmiri ndị na-adịghị eme atụ.

translations.source: Since there was limited response to this tactic, Germany expected a similar response to its unrestricted submarine warfare.
translations.reference: Ebe nzaghachi ihe omume a pere mpe, mba Jamini lere anya na a ga emekwa otu ihe n'ebe agha okpuru mmiri nọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ebe ọtụtụ mmadụ adịghị emezi atụmatụ a, Germany tụrụ anya na otu ihe ga-eme n'ihe gbasara agha okporokpo ya na ndị mmadụ na-eji ụgbọ mmiri.

translations.source: During the 1920s, the prevailing attitudes of most citizens and nations was that of pacifism and isolation.
translations.reference: N'oge afọ ndi 1920, agwa kachasị dị ebe nile n'etiti ndị mba dị iche iche bụ nke ịchọ udo na nnọrọ onwe.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge nke 1920, ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ na mba nwere echiche na ọ dị mkpa ịkwado udo na izu ike, yana ịnọghị jikọtara na ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: After seeing the horrors and atrocities of war during World War I, nations desired to avoid such a situation again in the future.
translations.reference: Mgbe a hụchara ụmụ egwu na ajọ ọmụme nke agha n’oge Agha Ụwa I, mba gasị chọrọ izere ụdị ọnọdụ ahụ ọzọ n’ọdịnihu.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe ha hụrụ ihe ọjọọ na ihe ndị na-emerụ ahụ nke agha n'oge Agha Uwa nke mbụ, mba ndị ọzọ chọrọ inwezi iji zaghachi ihe ndị a n'ọdịnihu.

translations.source: In 1884, Tesla moved to the United States of America to accept a job with the Edison Company in New York City.
translations.reference: N'afọ 1884, Tesla kwagara na mba Amerịka ịnara ọrụ na nke Ụlọ ọrụ Edison n'Obodo Niu Yọk.
translations.hypothesis: N'afọ 1884, Tesla gbakwuru mba United States of America iji kweta ọrụ n'otuto Edison na New York City.

translations.source: He arrived in the US with 4 cents to his name, a book of poetry, and a letter of recommendation from Charles Batchelor (his manager in his previous job) to Thomas Edison.
translations.reference: Ọ bịarutere na US n’inwe centị anọ n’aha ya, otu akwụkwọ nke uri, ya na otu akwụkwọ ozi nke nkwanye sitere na Charles Batchelor (onye njikwa ya n’ọrụ ya gara aga) ruo Thomas Edison.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bịara na Amerịka n'ụzọ dị mfe, n'ihi na ọ nwere naanị cent anọ n'aka ya, akwụkwọ nke abụ abụ, na akwụkwọ ndụmọdụ nke Charles Batchelor (onye bụ onye njikwa ya na ọrụ ya gara aga) nyere Thomas Edison.

translations.source: Ancient China had a unique way of showing different time periods; each stage of China or each family that was in power was a distinctive dynasty.
translations.reference: Chaịna ndị mgbe ochie nwere ụzọ pụrụ iche igosi oge afọ; ogo ọbụla nke Chaịna ma ọ bụ ezinụlọ ọ bụla nọbụrụ n’ọchịchị wụbụ oge ọchịchị eze pụrụ iche.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge gara aga, China nwere ụzọ dị iche iche iji egosi oge dị iche iche; ọ bụla n'ime mgbe ọ bụla nke China, ma ọ bụ ọ bụla ezinụlọ nwere ikike, bụ otu ọchịchị dị iche.

translations.source: Also between each dynasty was an unstable age of divided provinces. The best-known of these periods was the Three Kingdoms epoch taking place for 60 years between the Han and the Jin Dynasty.
translations.reference: Nakwa n’etiti usoro ndị eze ọ bụla bụ otu oge ejighị n'aka mke mpaghara ndị kewara ekewa. Oge ndị a nke a kacha mara amara bụ oge nke Alaeze Atọ nke mere ruo afọ iri na isii n'etiti Usoro Ndị Eze Han na Usoro Ndị Eze Jin ndị ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọzọkwa, n'etiti ọtụtụ ọchịchị, enwetara oge nke anaghị adịkwu ike, ebe e nwere mpaghara dị iche iche. Otu n'ime oge ndị a bụ "Oge Atọ Ọchịchị," nke mere afọ 60, n'etiti ọchịchị Han na Jin.

translations.source: During these periods fierce warfare took place between many nobles fighting for the throne.
translations.reference: N'oge ndị a, a lụrụ ọtụtụ agha n'etiti ndi ukwu na-azọ oche eze.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge ndị a, agha siri ike mere n'etiti ọtụtụ ndị ọchịchị na-alụ ọgụ maka oche ịchị.

translations.source: The Three Kingdoms was one of the bloodiest eras in Ancient China’s history thousands of people died fighting to sit in the highest seat in the grand palace at Xi’an.
translations.reference: Alaeze Atọ so n'otu n'ime ọgbọ kacha dị egwu n'akụkọ ihe mere na mba Chaịna mgbe gboo. Puku kwuru puku mmadụ nwụrụ n'agha ịnọ n'oche ọchịchị nke kachasị elu na nnukwu obi eze nke dị na Xi'an.
translations.hypothesis: Oge "Ọto Udo" bụ otu n'ime oge ndị na-emetụta ọbara nke dị n'akụkọ ihe mere eme nke China ochie. Puku ndị mmadụ nwụrụ n'oge a, na-alụ ọgụ iji nọrọ n'oche kacha elu n'ụlọ ọrụ dị ukwuu na Xi'an.

translations.source: There are a lot of social and political effects such as the use of metric system, a shift from absolutism to republicanism, nationalism and the belief the country belongs to the people not to one sole ruler.
translations.reference: Nke a butere ọtụtụ mmetụta na mmekọ mmadụ na ibe ya makwa na ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị dika usoro agụm ọnụ, mgbanwe site n'ọchịchị okwu otu onye gaa na nke okwu mba, nke obodo na nkwenye na obodo bụ nke ọha karịa ịbụ nke otu onye ọchịchị.
translations.hypothesis: Enwere ọtụtụ mgbe ọdịmma na mmekọrịta na-emetụta ndụ, dịka ojiji nke usoro metrik, mgbanwe sitere na ọchịchị onye otu na-achị eme ka ọ bụrụ ọchịchị ndị mmadụ, ọchịchị mba, na echiche na obodo ahụ bụ nke ndị mmadụ, ọ bụghị naanị onye otu na-achị.

translations.source: Also after the Revolution occupations were open to all male applicants allowing the most ambitious and successful to succeed.
translations.reference: Ọzọkwa mgbe ụmụ aka ọrụ Mgbanwe ọchịchị ahụ mepechara maka ụmụ nwoke ọchọ ọrụ niile na-ekwe ka ndị kacha nwee oké ọchịchọ na ihe ịga nke ọma ka ha gaa nke ọma.
translations.hypothesis: Ọzọkwa, mgbe ọgụ ahụ gasịrị, ọrụ ndị ọzọ bịara bụrụ nke ọma n'ibu ụmụ nwoke niile nwere mmasị, na-ekwe ka ndị nwere olileanya na ọganihu kacha ukwuu nwetakwaghị uru.

translations.source: Same goes for the military because instead of army rankings being based on class they were now based on cailaber.
translations.reference: Ọ bụkwa otu ihe ahụ n'amị, maka na kama nhazi n'usoro nke ndị amị ga-adabere n'ogugo, ọ daberezie n'ikikere.
translations.hypothesis: Otú ọ dị, nke ahụ adịkwaghị iche na ndị agha. Ọ bụ ezie na ọkwa ndị agha na-abụghị na njikọ na ọkwa mmadụ, ugbu a, ha na-adabere na ọkwa ọzọ.

translations.source: The French Revolution also inspired many other repressed working class people of other country's to began their own revolutions.
translations.reference: Mgbanwe France melitere obi ndi oru ana emegbu emegbu no gasi na mba ndi ozo ha ewere wee ike ibido mgbanwe nke ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ndị ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ nke e jidere n'ọtụtụ mba ndị ọzọ, mechara enwekwu ọdịmma site na ihe mere n'oge Revolution France, wee malitekwa ụkpọbi ha nke ha.

translations.source: Muhammad was deeply interested in matters beyond this mundane life. He used to frequent a cave that became known as “Hira‘” on the Mountain of “Noor” (light) for contemplation.
translations.reference: Muhammad nwere ezigbo mmasị n’ụmụ okwu gabigara ụwa a na-agwụ ike. Ọ dịbụ na-agakarị n’otu nnukwu ọnụala nke emechara mara dị ka “Hira‘” n’ugwu nke “Noor” (light) maka ntụgharị ụche.
translations.hypothesis: Muhammad nwere mmasị dị ukwuu na ihe ndị dị n'elu ọdịnihu ndụ a. Ọ na-abịa mgbe niile na otu ọdụ ụlọ nke bụrụla maara dị ka "Hira'" na ugwu "Noor" (ọkụ) iji cheta ihe.

translations.source: he cave itself, which survived the times, gives a very vivid image of Muhammad’s spiritual inclinations.
translations.reference: ọgba ahụ n'onwe ya, nke lanarịrị oge ndị a, na-enye ezigbo ihe ngosi maka echiche gbasara ihe mmụọ nke Muhammad.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdụ ụlọ ahụ, nke nọrọ naanị, na-egosi nke ọma ọtụtụ ihe gbasara echiche spiritual nke Muhammad.

translations.source: Resting on the top of one of the mountains north of Mecca, the cave is completely isolated from the rest of the world.
translations.reference: Na-ezu ike n’elu otu n’ime ugwu ndị nọ n’uwgu nke Meeka, nnukwu ọnụala dịpụrụ adịpụ n’ozuzu site n’akụkụ ụwa ndị ọzọ niile
translations.hypothesis: Ọdụ ụlọ ahụ, nke dị n'elu otu n'ime ugwu ndị dị n'ebe ugwu Mecca, adịghị jikọta na ụwa niile.

translations.source: In fact, it is not easy to find at all even if one knew it existed. Once inside the cave, it is a total isolation.
translations.reference: N'ezie, ọ dịghị mfe maọlị ịchọta, ọbụrụgodi na mmadụ maara na ọ dị. Ozugbo abanyere n'ime ọgba ahụ, ọ bụ ndịpụ kpam kpam.
translations.hypothesis: N'ezie, ọ bụghị mfe ịchọta ya, ọbụrụ na onye ma na ọ dị. Ozugbo ị banyere n'ime obara ahụ, ọ bụ nnọchite ahụ zuru oke.

translations.source: Nothing can be seen other than the clear, beautiful sky above and the many surrounding mountains. Very little of this world can be seen or heard from inside the cave.
translations.reference: O nweghị ihe ọzọ enwere ike ịhụ na-abụghị eluigwe dị n’elu gbachapụrụ, maa mma na ọtụtụ ugwu gbara gburugburu. Nanị obere nke ụwa ka enwere ike ịhụ ma ọ bụ nụ site n’ime nnukwu ọnụala ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Echereghi ihe ọ bụla ọ bụla, eweghachi ihe oyiyi, osimiri ọcha na mara mma dị n'elu, na ọtụtụ ugwu ndị dị n'akụkụ. O doro anya na ọ dịkarịa ọcha ịhụ ma ọ bụ ịnụ ihe ọ bụla gbasara ụwa a site n'ime ụlọ ọrụ ahụ.

translations.source: The Great Pyramid at Giza is the only one of the seven wonders that is still standing today.
translations.reference: Oke Piramid na Giza bụ naanị nke ka kwụ taa n'ime ihe itụnanya asaa ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdụnwa nke ukwuu nke Giza bụ naanị otu n'ime ihe atọ nke ọma na ụwa bụ nke ka dị na ọdịnihu taa.

translations.source: Built by the Egyptians in the third century BCE, the Great Pyramid is one of many large pyramid structures built to honor dead Pharaoh.
translations.reference: Ndị Ijipt rụrụ n’ime narị afọ atọ BCE, Oke Piramidi ahụ otu n’ime ọtụtụ nnukwu ihe ọwụwụ piramidi arụrụ ịkwanye Fero nwụrụ ugwu.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ụlọ nke Egyptisi wụrụ n'afọ nke atọ tupu Kristi, Pyramid dị ukwuu bụ otu n'ime ọtụtụ ụlọ akwụkwọ dị ukwuu e wụrụ iji cheta ndị Pharaoh ndị nwụrụ.

translations.source: The Giza Plateau, or "Giza Necropolis" in the Egyptian Valley of the Dead contains several pyramids (of which the great pyramid is the largest), several small tombs, several temples, and the great Sphinx.
translations.reference: Ala ugwu Giza maọbụ "Giza Nekropolis" nke dị na ndagwurugwu ọnwụ Ijipt nwere ọtụtụ piramid (nke piramid ukwu bụ nke kachasị ibu), ọtụtụ ebe olili, ọtụtụ ụlọ ofufe nakwa oke Sfinks.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo Giza, ma ọ bụ "Obodo Ndị Olu Eme Giza" na mpaghara ndị Igbo na Egypt, nwere ọtụtụ pyramids (n'etiti ha, pyramid dị ukwuu bụ nke kacha buru ibu), ọtụtụ ụlọ nchekwa dị nta, ọtụtụ ụlọ nsọ, na Sphinx dị ukwuu.

translations.source: The great pyramid was created to honor the Pharaoh Khufu, and many of the smaller pyramids, tombs, and temples were built to honor Khufu's wives and family members.
translations.reference: Arụrụ oke piramid iji kwanyere Eze Khufu zugwu, ya na ọtụtụ piramid obere ndị ọzọ, ebe olili na ụlọ ofufe arụrụ ịkwanyere ndị inyom Khufu na ezinụlọ ya ugwu.
translations.hypothesis: Agbụrụ dị ukwuu ahụ rụpụtara iji cheta Pharaoh Khufu, yana ọtụtụ agbụrụ ndị nta, ụlọ nchekwa, na ụlọ nsọ rụpụtara iji cheta nwunye Khufu na ndị ezinụlọ ya.

translations.source: The "up bow" mark looks like a V and the "down bow mark" like a staple or a square missing its bottom side.
translations.reference: Akara “ụta elu” ahụ yiri otu V ma akara “ụta ala” ahụ yiri otu stepụlụ ma ọ bụ otu ǹkomgbaànoǹhà nke tufure ebe okpuru ya.
translations.hypothesis: Akara "up bow" na-adị ka akara V, ebe akara "down bow" na-adị ka akara nke eji eje eje (staple) ma ọ bụ akara anụkwụ na-enweghị akụkụ ya ala.

translations.source: Up means you should start at the tip and push the bow, and down means you should start at the frog (which is where your hand is holding the bow) and pull the bow.
translations.reference: Elu pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi n'ọnụnụ ya pịa ụta aka, ma ala pụtara na Ị kwesịrị isi na fụrọgụ (nke bụ ebe aka gị ji ụta) were dọọ ụta aka.
translations.hypothesis: "Ọ bụrụ na ị họọrọ "elu," ị ga-amalite n'elu akụ na ịkpụnye akụ ahụ. Ọ bụrụ na ị họọrọ "ala," ị ga-amalite n'ebe dị nso na ebe aka gị na-ejide akụ ahụ (akụ a na-akpọ "frog") wee dọta akụ ahụ."

translations.source: An up-bow usually generates a softer sound, while a down-bow is stronger and more assertive.
translations.reference: Otu ụta-elu na -emepụtakarị ụda kara dị nro, ebe ụta-ala ka sie ike ma kara kwupụta.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịmma nke ụda nke egwu egwu na-abụkarị nke dị nro, ebe ọdịmma nke egwu egwu na-agagharị ala na-abụkarị nke siri ike ma na-agagharị nke ọma.

translations.source: Feel free to pencil in your own marks, but remember the printed bowing marks are there for a musical reason, so they should usually be respected.
translations.reference: Detuo akara nke gị na nwere onwe, mana chetakwa na akara ndị ahụ ebiri ebi nwere uru egwu ha bara, n'ihi nke a ha kwesịrị ka akwanyere ha ugwu.
translations.hypothesis: Enwere ike ịgbasa akara nke ị chọrọ, mana tụkwasịrị na akara ndị e biputara maka ịgbasa bụ iji ha maka ihe gbasara egwu, ya mere ọ dị mma ka ha adịghị agbanwe.

translations.source: The terrified King Louis XVI, Queen Marie Antoinette their two young children (11 year old Marie Therese and four year old Louis-Charles) and the King's sister, Madam Elizabeth, on the 6th October 1789 were forced back to Paris from Versailles by a mob of market women.
translations.reference: N'Oktoba 6, 1789, ụmụ nwanyị ahịa iwe ji yiri Eze Luwi XVI oke egwu mgbe ha si na Versailles dọrọ ya, nwunye ya Marịa Antwanet, obere ụmụ ha abụọ (Marịa Teriza dị afọ 11 na Luwi-Chals dị afọ anọ), na nwanne nwanyị Eze, Madam Elizabet, dọghachi ha na Parii.
translations.hypothesis: N'ọnwa Ọktoba nke 6, afọ 1789, King Louis XVI, nwanyị ya bụ Queen Marie Antoinette, ụmụ ha abụọ (Marie Therese, nke afọ 11, na Louis-Charles, nke afọ anọ), na nwanne King ahụ, Madam Elizabeth, bịarutere Paris site na Versailles n'ihi otu ndị agbadoro ahụhụ nke ndị nwanyị na-ere ahịa. Ha adịghị enwe olileanya.

translations.source: In a carriage, they traveled back to Paris surrounded by a mob of people screaming and shouting threats against the King and Queen.
translations.reference: Ha laghachiri Paris n'ime moto ịnyịnya ndị iwe na-ewe gbara gburugburu, ha na-eti mkpu na-agwa Eze na Nwunye ya ihe egwu dị iche iche.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime ụgbọ mmiri, ha gbalere n'azụ na Paris, ebe ndị mmadụ na-agba ọsọ na ha, na-akpọ nkuzi na-atụ ụjọ maka Eze na Nwanyị Eze.

translations.source: The mob of people forced the King And Queen to have their carriage windows wide open.
translations.reference: Ndị iwe a manyere Eze na Queen ka ha meghee windo ụgbọ ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị mmadụ ole na ole tụgharịrị iwe, wee jide ndị eze na nwanyị eze ụkwụ, wee kpọchie windo ụgbọ ala ha ka ha wee nwee ike ịhụ ha.

translations.source: At one point a member of the mob waved the head of a royal guard killed at Versailles in front of the terrified Queen.
translations.reference: N'otu mgbe otu n'ime ndị igwe mmadụ fegharịrị isi onye nche eze egburu na Versailles n'ihu eze nwanyi ụjọ ji.
translations.hypothesis: N'otu oge, otu n'ime ndị na-eme ihe ọjọọ ahụ jiri ugo onye nche dị mkpụrụ obi nke e gburu na Versailles, wee tọọ ya n'ihu nwanyị Eze ahụ, bụ́ ndị na-atụ ụjọ.

translations.source: The war expenditures of U.S. imperialism in the conquest of the Philippines were paid for by the Filipino people themselves.
translations.reference: Mmefu ego n'agha nke ndị Amerịka mbịarachịwa na mmeri ndị Filipaị bụ nke ndị Filipino kwụrụ ụgwọ ya n’onwe ha.
translations.hypothesis: Aghụghọ ụjọ nke mba United States nke e jiri eme agha iji jide Philippines bụ ndị Igbo Filipino n'onwe ha kwere ụgwọ ya.

translations.source: They were compelled to pay taxes to the U.S. colonial regime to defray a major part of the expenditures and the interest on bonds floated in the name of the Philippine government through the Wall Street banking houses.
translations.reference: A manyere ha iwu ịkwụ ụtụisi nye ndị ọchịchị mbịarachịwa mba Amerịka iji wedata oke ego e mefuru n'aha gọọmenti mba Filipin site n'aka ụlọakụ Wọlụ Striti.
translations.hypothesis: Ha adịghị mma ịkwụ ụgwọ ụlọ akwụkwọ na-akpọ "tax" nye ọchịchị colonial nke United States iji kwụọ ọnụ ahịa dị mkpa na ụgwọ ọzụzụ nke ego a na-akwụ ụgwọ, nke a na-akpọ "bond," nke a na-emepụta n'ahụ maka gọọmentị Philippines site na ụlọ akụ dị na Wall Street.

translations.source: Of course, the superprofits derived from the protracted exploitation of the Filipino people would constitute the basic gains of U.S. imperialism.
translations.reference: N’eziokwu, nnukwu uru e nwetara na ogologo mmegbu ndị mba Filipiinụ ga-abụ ihe mejuputara isi uru omume empaya Amerịka.
translations.hypothesis: N'ezie, uru dị ukwuu nke a na-enweta site na ịgba ndị Filipino ọrụ ike ogologo oge ga-abụ uru bụ isi nke ọchịchị imperialist nke United States.

translations.source: To understand the Templars one must understand the context that prompted the creation of the order.
translations.reference: Ịghọta ndị Templars, aghaghi ịghọta ọnọdụ nke kpaliri okike nke otu a.
translations.hypothesis: Iji ghọta Templars, ọ dị mkpa ịghọta ihe kpatara ebute otu ahụ n'ụlọ.

translations.source: The age where the events took place is commonly referred as the High Middle Ages the period of European history in the 11th, 12th, and 13th centuries (AD 1000–1300).
translations.reference: Ọgbọ ihe ndị a mere na ya ka a na-akpọkarị Ọgbọ Etiti dị Elu bụ oge ihe ndị mere na mba Yuropu n'afọ narị iri na otu, narị iri na abụọ na narị iri na atọ (AD 1000-1300).
translations.hypothesis: Oge nke ihe omume ndị a mere bụ nke a na-akpọkarị "Oge Osim Uwa," bụ oge n'akụkọ Europe nke nwere ọtụtụ afọ, site na afọ 1100 ruo afọ 1300 (AD 1000–1300).

translations.source: The High Middle Ages were preceded by the Early Middle Ages and followed by the Late Middle Ages, which by convention ends around 1500.
translations.reference: Ọgbọ etiti ndị nke mbụ butere ọgbọ etiti ndị dị elu ụzọ, nke ọgbọ etiti nke ngwụcha sotere n'azụ nke gwuru ebe 1500.
translations.hypothesis: Oge nke ọwụwa anyanwụ nke Oge Etu na-abịa tupu Oge Etu nke mbụ, ma ọ bịara n'azụ Oge Etu nke ikpeazụ, nke, site n'echiche ọkachamara, na-agwụsị ihe dị ka afọ 1500.

translations.source: Technological determinism is a term that encompasses a wide range of ideas in practice, from technology-push or the technological imperative to a strict sense that human destiny is driven by an underlying logic associated with scientific laws and their manifestation in technology.
translations.reference: Mkpebi teknụụzụ bụ usoro gazuru nchịkọta nchepụta gasị etinyere n’uju, site na technụụzụ-kwàa maọbụ nye iwu siri ike nke bụ na njedebe nke onye ga-esite n’iwu metụtara sayensi na nke ngosipụta teknụụzụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịmma teknolojị bụ okwu nke na-agụnye ọtụtụ echiche dị iche iche n'ọrụ, site na usoro teknoloji na-achịkwa ma ọ bụ ihe teknoloji na-achọ, ruo echiche siri ike bụ na ọdịnihu mmadụ na-achịkọta site n'ụzọ ọrụ dị n'okpuru nke metụtara iwu sayensị na ọdịnihu ha na teknolọji.

translations.source: Most interpretations of technological determinism share two general ideas: that the development of technology itself follows a path largely beyond cultural or political influence, and that technology in turn has "effects" on societies that are inherent, rather than socially conditioned.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ nkọwa e nyere nkwenyesiike kenkanụzụ nwere echiche izugbe abụọ: na mmepụta nkanụzụ n'onwe ya na-agbaso usoro nke gbapụrụ iche site na nkwanye nke omenala maọbụ ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị, ya na kwa na nkanụzụ n'aka nke ya nwere "mmekpaahụ" ọ na-enye ọhaobodo nke dị adị, n'abụghị nke sitere na mmekọrịta.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ụdị echiche gbasara usoro teknụzụ na-achọpụta abụọ ihe bụ isi: na mmepe teknụzụ n'onwe ya na-aga n'ụzọ nke na-adịkarị n'ebe ọ bụla ebe ọdịmma ma ọ bụ ọchịchị nwere mmetụta, na teknụzụ, n'aka nke ọzọ, nwere "mmetụta" na obodo ndị na-abụkarị, ọ bụghị naanị site na usoro ọdịmma.

translations.source: For example, one might say that the motor car necessarily leads to the development of roads.
translations.reference: Maka ọmụmaatụ, mmadụ nwere ike ịsị na ụgbọala n'ịkwesị ekwesị na-eduga na mmepe nke ụzọ gasị.
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, enwere ike ikwu na ụgbọ ala na-ebute ozugbo na mmepe ụzọ.

translations.source: However, a nationwide road network is not economically viable for just a handful of cars, so new methods of production are developed to reduce the cost of car ownership.
translations.reference: N'agbanyeghị nke a, okporo ụzọ zuru obodo ọnụ bụ mmefu ego ma ọbụrụ na ụgbọ ala ehighị nne, ya mere emepụtara ụzọ ọhụrụ ịwedata ego o na ewe inwe ụgbọala.
translations.hypothesis: Otú ọ dị, ọ dịghị mma akụ na ụzọ ọkwọ ụgbọ ala nke zuru ụwa ọnụ maka obere ọtụtụ ụgbọ ala naanị. Ya mere, usoro mmepụta ọhụrụ na-emepụta iji belata ọnụ ahịa ịnweta ụgbọ ala.

translations.source: Mass car ownership also leads to a higher incidence of accidents on the roads, which leads to the invention of new techniques in healthcare for repairing damaged bodies.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ mmadụ inwe ụgbọ ala na-ebutekwa nnukwu ihe mberede n'okporo ụzọ, nke na-eweta mmepụta usoro nleta ahụike ọhụrụ maka ịrụzi ahụ mebiri emebi.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ mmadụ nwere ụgbọ ala na-ebute ọtụtụ ihe mgbu na-eme n'okporo ụzọ, nke na-ebute mkpụrụ maịsị ọhụrụ na ahụike iji dozi ahụ ndị merenụ ihe mgbu.

translations.source: Romanticism had a large element of cultural determinism, drawn from writers such as Goethe, Fichte, and Schlegel.
translations.reference: Ihunanya ya nwere otutu ihe banyere mmeme nke ọdịnala, nke sitere n'aka ndị edemede dịka Goethe, Fichte, na Schlegel.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ "Romanticism" nwere akụkọ dị ukwuu banyere otú omenala na-emetụta ihe, nke e biputere site n'aka ndị ode akụkọ dị ka Goethe, Fichte, na Schlegel.

translations.source: In the context of Romanticism, the geography molded individuals, and over time customs and culture related to that geography arose, and these, being in harmony with the place of the society, were better than arbitrarily imposed laws.
translations.reference: Na onodu romanticism, ala ebe onye no bu ihe na kpu omume mmadu, k’oge na aga odinala na omenala metutara ala ebe obibi amalite, nkea mere ndi mmadu jiri nabata odinala na omenala ndia maka na ha na ya bu odinala na omenala nwere nkwekorita karia iwu ana atukwasa n’isi oha.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime usoro nke a na-akpọ "Romanticism," ebe obibi nwere mmetụta dị ukwuu na ndị mmadụ, ma n'oge na-aga, ọdịnụ na ọdịnala ndị metụtara ebe ahụ bịrịrị, na ndị a, n'ihi na ha na-akpọrọsite na ebe obibi nke obodo ahụ, dị mma karịa iwu ndị a na-etinye n'enweghị ihe kpatara ya.

translations.source: In the manner that Paris is known as the fashion capital of the contemporary world, Constantinople was regarded as the fashion capital of feudal Europe.
translations.reference: N'otu aka a maara Paris ka isi ejiji ịchọ mma n'ụwa nke oge a, e weere Kọnstantinopul dịka isi ejiji ịchọ mma na mba Yuropu n'oge agha.
translations.hypothesis: Dị ka Paris amaara dị ka obodo ebe e ji ụkpụrụ ejiji kacha dị n'ụwa taa, Constantinople nwetara aha dị ka obodo ebe a na-achịkọta ụkpụrụ ejiji kachasị dị na Europe nke oge ochie.

translations.source: Its renown for being an epicenter of luxury began in about 400 A.D. and lasted up until about 1100 A.D.
translations.reference: Ebidoro n’afo 400A.D. ruo n’afo 1100 A.D were mara ya na o bu isi mkporindu.
translations.hypothesis: Aghụghọ ya banyere ịbụ ebe e ji akpọrọ anya na ọchịchọ dị elu malitere n'okpuru afọ 400 A.D. wee nọgide ruo n'okpuru afọ 1100 A.D.

translations.source: Its status declined during the twelfth century mainly due to the fact that Crusaders had returned bearing gifts such as silks and spices that were valued more than what Byzantine markets offered.
translations.reference: Ọkwa na gbadara n’oge narị afọ iri na abụọ tụmadị n’ihi eziokwu bụ na Ndị agha ntute alaghachila ma bute ụmụ onyinye dị ka ụmụ akwa sịlk na ngwa nri ndị nwere mbamuru karịrị ihe ahịa Byzantine nyere.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịmma ya belatara n'oge narị nke abụọ, ọkachasị n'ihi na ndị Crusaders bịara n'azụ na ngwaahịa dị ka akwa na osisi ndị a na-ere ahịa, bụ ndị dị mkpa karịa ihe ndị ahịa Byzantine na-enye.

translations.source: It was at this time that the transfer of the title of Fashion Capital from Constantinople to Paris was made.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ n'oge ahụ ka okwa isi ejiji ịchọ ma siri na Kọnstantinopul fere Paris.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ n'oge a ka akụkọ ahụi nke "Udozi Isiokwu" (Fashion Capital) gbanarịrị site na Constantinople gaa Paris.

translations.source: Gothic style peaked in the period between the 10th - 11th centuries and the 14th century.
translations.reference: Usoro Gotik kasị elu n'oge dị n'etiti afọ ndị nari nke ir na narị nke iri na otu ya na narị nke iri na anọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị arụ ọrụ Gothic ruru oke kacha elu ya n'oge dị n'etiti narị nke iri na otu na narị nke iri na abụọ, na narị nke iri na anọ.

translations.source: At the beginning dress was heavily influenced by the Byzantine culture in the east.
translations.reference: Na mbido, ọ bụ usoro ejiji ndị Byzantium n'ọwụwa anyanwụ ka onye ọbụla na-eso.
translations.hypothesis: Na mbido, afo dị ukwuu n'okpuru mmetụta nke ọdịnala Byzantine n'ebe ndịda anyanwụ.

translations.source: However, due to the slow communication channels, styles in the west could lag behind by 25 to 30 year.
translations.reference: Mana, n'ihi ụkpụrụ mkparịta ụka na adịghị ọsịsọ, usoro dị na ọdịda anyanwụ nwere ike inọzụga azụ n'oteaka afọ iri abụọ na ise ruo iri atọ.
translations.hypothesis: Otú ọ dị, n'ihi ọsọ obere nke usoro nkwukọrịta, ụdị ihe ndị e mere na mpaghara ndịda nwere ike ịlaghachite site na afọ 25 ruo 30.

translations.source: towards the end of the Middle Ages western Europe began to develop their own style. one of the biggest developments of the time as a result of the crusades people began to use buttons to fasten clothing.
translations.reference: na njedebe nke oge Mịdụl Eeji ndị ọdịda anyanwụ Europe malitere mepụtawa usoro nke ha. Otu ihe mmepụta kachasi mkpa n'oge ahụ, n'ihi ọgụ aghara, ndị mmadụ bidoro iji bọtịnụ akpọchị akwa.
