translations.hypothesis: N'ime afọ ndị dị nso na njedebe nke Oge Etu, Europe ndịda malitere ịmepụta ụdị ha nke uche. Otú ọ dị, otu n'ime mgbanwe kacha mkpa n'oge ahụ, n'ihi agha ndị Crusader, ndị mmadụ malitere iji bọta iji jikọọ uwe.

translations.source: Subsistence agriculture is agriculture carried out for the production of enough food to meet just the needs of the agriculturalist and his/her family.
translations.reference: Ugbo oru bu ihe oru ugbo bu nke eweputara iji meputa nri ga ezuru ndi mmadu choro ya ma obu ya na ulo ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ugbo nke e mere iji mepụta nri zuru ezu iji gboo naanị mkpa onye na-eme ugbo na ezinụlọ ya bụ ihe a na-akpọ "ọrụ ugbo maka ndụ."

translations.source: Subsistence agriculture is a simple, often organic, system using saved seed native to the ecoregion combined with crop rotation or other relatively simple techniques to maximize yield.
translations.reference: Ịkọ ọrụ ugbo bụ ihe dịcha mfe, ọtụtụ mgbe nke ndụ, sistèm n'iji nkpụrụ echekwara bụ nwa afọ na mphaghara ebe obibi ahụ ejikọtara ya na nghagharị mkpụrụ ma ọ bụ usoro ndị ọzọ dị mfe iji mee ka ọmịmị kachasị.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ugbo nke na-ebute nri maka onwe onye bụ usoro dị mfe, nkekarịkwa na-eji ihe oriri na-acha, ebe eji osisi nke e chekwara, nke bụ nke obere mpaghara ahụ, na usoro mgbanwe ugbo ma ọ bụ ụfọdụ usoro ndị ọzọ dị mfe iji mee ka mmepụta ya dịkwuo.

translations.source: Historically most farmers were engaged in subsistence agriculture and this is still the case in many developing nations.
translations.reference: Na mgbe gboo ọtụtụ n'ime ndị na-akọ ugbo na-eme ụdị nke onwe n'enweghị nke orire ọ ka dịkwa otu a n'ọtụtụ obodo ka na etolite etolite.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge gara aga, ọtụtụ ndị ọrụ ugbo na-arụ ọrụ ugbo iji mee ka ha na ezinụlọ ha nwee nri, na nke a ka bụ eziokwu na ọtụtụ mba ndị na-eto eto.

translations.source: Subcultures bring together like-minded individuals who feel neglected by societal standards and allow them to develop a sense of identity.
translations.reference: Obere omenaala na-ekpọkọta ọnụ ndị nwere ụdị echiche ndị nwere mmetụta na ụkpụrụ keobodo ha leghaara ha anya ma nye ha ohere ịzụlite echiche nke njirimara.
translations.hypothesis: Subkọltụ na-akpakọta ndị mmadụ nwere echiche yiri ibe ha, ndị na-eche na ha adịghị n'ụkpọrọ na ụkpụrụ obodo, na-enyere ha ohere ịmụta otu ha si dị iche.

translations.source: Subcultures can be distinctive because of the age, ethnicity, class, location, and/or gender of the members.
translations.reference: Enwere ike imata ngalaba omenala site na afo, agburu, klaasi, ebe onye bi, ma o bu etu chukwu si kee mmadu -i bu nwoke ka ibu nwanyi.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị ọdịbendị dị iche iche nwere ike ịbụ nke pụrụ iche n'ihi afọ, agbụrụ, ọkwa ndụ, ebe obibi, na/ma obu ụdị nwoke ma obere.

translations.source: The qualities that determine a subculture as distinct may be linguistic, aesthetic, religious, political, sexual, geographical, or a combination of factors.
translations.reference: Ihe nlereanya aji ama na omenala pụrụ iche bụ asụsụ, ịchọ mma, okpukpe, ọchịchị, mmekọahụ, ọnọdụ ebe, maọbu njikọ ọtụtụ ihe.
translations.hypothesis: Ihe ndị na-eme ka otu obodo dị iche na ndị ọzọ nwere ike ịbụ ihe gbasara asụsụ, ihe omume na mmekọrịta, okwukwu, ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị, mmekọrịta mmadụ, ebe obibi, ma ọ bụ nkwado nke ihe ndị a.

translations.source: Members of a subculture often signal their membership through a distinctive and symbolic use of style, which includes fashions, mannerisms, and argot.
translations.reference: Ndịòtù nke otu okpuru omenala na-akpọtụrụkarị ịdị n'òtù ha site n'otu ojiji akanka pụrụ iche ma dịmara, nke gụnyere ụmụ ejiji, omume, na asụsụ ịgba izu.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị otu subculture na-egosiputa ọmụmụ ha n'ọtụtụ ụzọ, site n'ịji ụdị uwe, omume, na okwu pụrụ iche nke na-echetara ndị ọzọ na ha bụ otu.

translations.source: One of the most common methods used to illustrate the importance of socialization is to draw upon the few unfortunate cases of children who were, through neglect, misfortune, or wilful abuse, not socialized by adults while they were growing up.
translations.reference: Otu n’ime ukpuru akacha mara nke atuzi-aka banyere uru di mmekorita bu iweta n’uche ihe nwute banyere umu-aka ndi elefuuru-anya, na-nwuta, maobu mmeto akpachaara-anya mee, enweghi mmekorita ha ndi toro-eto mgbe ha ka na-eto eto.
translations.hypothesis: Otu n'ime ụzọ kachasị eji akọwa mkpa nke mmezi mmadụ bụ ịkọrịta banyere ụfọdụ ihe ndị na-adịghị mma nke mere n'ime ụmụaka ole na ole bụ ndị, site n'echiche adịghị mma, ọdịda, ma ọ bụ ihe ndị a na-eme n'ihu anya, anaghị akpọọrọ ha n'ime obodo mgbe ha na-eto.

translations.source: Such children are called "feral" or wild. Some feral children have been confined by people (usually their own parents); in some cases this child abandonment was due to the parents' rejection of a child's severe intellectual or physical impairment.
translations.reference: Ụdị ụmụaka a ka a na akpọ ndị azụghị azụ. Ọtụtụ ụmụaka an na azụghị azụ abụrụla ndị ndị mmadụ jituru ejitu (ọ na abụkarị ndị mụrụ ha); oge ụfọdụ ngharịpụ ụmụaka bụ maka ọjụjụ ntụpọ dị na ahụ nwatakịrị ahụ a na ahụ anya maọbụ ntụpọ dị n' akọ n'uche ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ụmụaka ndị a na-akpọ "feral" maọbụ ndị ọhịa. Ụmụaka ụfọdụ ndị a na-akpọ "feral" ebe ndị mmadụ (karịsịa ndị nne na nna ha) jidere ha; n'ụdị ụfọdụ, a hapụrụ ụmụaka ndị a n'ihi na ndị nne na nna ha jụrụ ọnụ ụmụaka ahụ, n'ihi mmerụ ahụ maọbụ nke uche nke ụmụaka ahụ.

translations.source: Feral children may have experienced severe child abuse or trauma before being abandoned or running away.
translations.reference: Ụmụaka azụghịazụ nwere ike ha e nweela ahụmihe nke mmetọ ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ahụmihe mkpasasị uche nke ukwuu tupu agbahapụ ha ma ọ bụ ha na-agbalaga.
translations.hypothesis: Ụmụaka ndị na-ebi ndụ n'ime ime obodo nwere ike ịnwụ ọtụtụ ihe ndị na-emerụ ahụ ma ọ bụ mmerụ ahụ tupu ha akpọrọ ha n'ebe ndị ọzọ ma ọ bụ tụfọ.

translations.source: Others are alleged to have been brought up by animals; some are said to have lived in the wild on their own.
translations.reference: Ndị ọzọ bụ ebubo ka eboro n’ọbụ ụmụ anụmanụ kpọpụtara ha; a sịkwara n’ụfọdụ biri n’ime ọhịa na onwe ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ ndị ọzọ akọwaara na ha toro n'aka anụmanụ; ụfọdụ sooro ndị mmadụ na ha kwuru na ha nọrọ naanị ha n'ebe ọhịa.

translations.source: When completely brought up by non-human animals, the feral child exhibits behaviors (within physical limits) almost entirely like those of the particular care-animal, such as its fear of or indifference to humans.
translations.reference: Mgbe anumanu na-abughi-mmadu zulitechara ya kpam-kpam, nwa-ohia ahu egosi akparama-agwa (na njedebe ebe ana ahu anya) ihe dika nani nke anumanu-nlekota ya, dika ujo ya nye maobu enweghi ujo nye umu mmadu.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe ọmụma nke ụmụaka a na-ebube site n'anya ụmụ anụmanụ na-adịghị bụrụ mmadụ, ụmụaka ahụ na-egosiputa ọrụ (n'ime ihe atụkwaghị anya ahụ) nke dịkarịkarị ka ọrụ ụmụ anụmanụ nke na-elekọta ha, dịka ụfụdụ ha maka ndị mmadụ ma ọ bụ enweghị mmasị na ha.

translations.source: While project based learning should make learning easier and more interesting, scaffolding goes a step beyond.
translations.reference: Dịka ọmụmụ dabere n’arụmarụ kwesịrị ime ka ọmụmụ kara dị mfe ma na-adọkwu mmasị, ịkụ skafoldu gakwuru otu ụzọụkwụ n’ihu.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na ụzọ ọmụma nke na-ebuli ọrụ nwere ike ime ka ọmụma dị mfe na dị mkpa, ụzọ "scaffolding" na-aga ọkara ọzọ.

translations.source: Scaffolding is not a method of learning but rather an aid that provides support to individuals whom are undergoing a new learning experience such as using a new computer program or beginning a new project.
translations.reference: Skafoldin abụghị usoro mmụta kama ọ bụ enyemaka na-akwado ndị na-amụ ihe ọhụrụ dịka iji program ọhụrụ arụ ọrụ na kọmputa maọbụ ibido ọrụ ọhụrụ
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ụlọ ọrụ abụghị ụzọ ọmụma, kama ọ bụ enyemaka nke na-enye akụkụ ndụ na-amụ ihe ọhụrụ, dịka iji ngwaọrụ kọmputa ọhụrụ ma ọ bụ malite ọrụ ọhụrụ.

translations.source: Scaffolds can be both virtual and real, in other words, a teacher is a form of scaffold but so is the little paperclip man in Microsoft Office.
translations.reference: Ụmụ arụrụmarụ osisi nwere ike ịbụ ma kendịnuche ma ịdịrị ire, n'ụzọ ọzọ, onye nkuzi bụ ụdị arụrụmarụ osisi mana ọ dịkwa dị ka nwoke ntakịrị mkpado akwụkwọ n'ime Microsoft Office.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị enyemaka dị iche iche, ọ bụrụla nke zuru ezu ma ọ bụ nke zuru oke, n'ọtụtụ ụdị. Nke a pụtara na onye nkuzi bụ otu ụdị enyemaka, mana ọ bụkwa otu ụdị enyemaka na-apụta n'ime ihe eji eme ọrụ na Microsoft Office, dị ka ọnyà obere nke nwere ọkpụkpụ.

translations.source: Virtual Scaffolds are internalized in the software and are meant to question, prompt, and explain procedures that may have been to challenging for the student to handle alone.
translations.reference: A rụnyechara Ihe nkwado n'ime ngwanro a, ndị ga-ajụ ajụjụ, nye ozi, ma kọwaa usoro ndị gaara ara nwa akwụkwọ ahụ ịghọta n'onwe ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị enyemaka eletrọniki a na-etinye n'ime ngwaọrụ ahụ, ma ha bụ iji jụ, gosi, na kọwa usoro ndị nwere ike ịbụ nke siri ike maka akwụkwọ ụlọ akwụkwọ ịnagide ya naanị.

translations.source: Children are placed in Foster Care for a wide variety of reasons that range from neglect, to abuse, and even to extortion.
translations.reference: Enwere ọtụtụ ihe e ji akpọga ụmụ aka ka onye ọzọ lekọta ha, dịka nleghara anya, mmegbu, nakwa nnapụ ihe.
translations.hypothesis: Anya ụmụ chi dị n'ọrụ nlekọta ndị na-enweghị ezinụlọ maka ihe ndị dị iche iche, nke sitere na enweghị nlekọta, ruo ime ihe ọjọọ, na ọbụna ime ihe iji nweta ego n'ụzọ adịghị mma.

translations.source: No child should ever have to grow up in an environment that is not nurturing, caring, and educational, but they do.
translations.reference: Ọ dị mma ka nwatakịrị tolite na gburugburu ebe a na-adịghị elekọta, elekọta, na agụmakwụkwọ, mana ha na-eme ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dịghị ka ọ dị mma ka ụmụaka toro n'ebe ebe enweghị nkwụsi, enweghị ịhụnanya, na enweghị agụmakwụkwọ, mana ọtụtụ n'ime ha na-eto n'ebe ndị ahụ.

translations.source: We perceive the Foster Care System to be a safety zone for these children.
translations.reference: Anyị na-ahụta Ụkpụrụ Nlekọta anya ahụ ka ebe n’enweghi ihe iyi ndụ egwu nye ụmụaka ndị a.
translations.hypothesis: Anyị na-ahụ sistemụ nlekọta ụmụaka a dị ka ebe nchekwa maka ụmụaka ndị a.

translations.source: Our foster care system is supposed to provide safe homes, loving caregivers, stable education, and reliable health care.
translations.reference: Ụlọ nchekwa ụmụaka anyị kwesịrị inye ụlọ nwere nchekwa, ndị nledo anya nwere ịhụnanya, nkụzi akwụkwọ dị mma, na nlekọta ahụike dị ntụkwasịobi.
translations.hypothesis: Usoro nlekọta ụmụaka anyị na-atụkwasị obi na ọ ga-enye ụlọ dị n'ọdịmma, ndị nlekọta na-enwe mmetụta, agụmakwụkọ zuru oke, na ọrụ ahụike dị mma.

translations.source: Foster care is supposed to provide all the necessities that were lacking in the home they were previously taken from.
translations.reference: Ulo nlekọta anya ndi akpotara-akpota kwesiri inyecha ihe nile di mkpa nke na adighi n’ulo ochie esi na kpota ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ụlọ ezinụlọ nlekọta ụmụaka na-abụkarị ebe eji nye ụmụaka ihe niile ha na-achọ, ihe ndị ha na-enweghị na ezinụlọ ha si n'ebe ha bi tupu.

translations.source: The Internet combines elements of both mass and interpersonal communication.
translations.reference: Ịntanetị na-ejikọ akụkụ nke nkwukọrịta ọha na nkwukọrịta nke mmadụ abụọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ntanetị na-ejikọta ihe dị iche iche nke ọgbakọ na ọdịdị mmadụ n'ime usoro okwu.

translations.source: The distinct characteristics of the Internet lead to additional dimensions in terms of the uses and gratifications approach.
translations.reference: Njirimara pụrụ iche nke Ịntaneetị na-eduga akụkụ agbakwụnyere n’usoro nke ojiji ya na usoro afọ ojuju.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị ihe ndị ọdịiche dị na Intanet na-ebute ụdị ọhụrụ na ụzọ eji atụgharị na echiche banyere otú ndị mmadụ si eji ya na ihe ha na-enweta site na ya.

translations.source: For example, “learning” and “socialization” are suggested as important motivations for Internet use (James et al., 1995).
translations.reference: Maka ọmụmaatụ, “mmụta” na “mkpakọrịta” bụ ndị atụnyere dịka mkpalite dị mkpa maka ojiji Ịntanetị (James na ndị ọzọ., 1995).
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, "mụtakwụ" na "ndọta mmadụ" etuwo dịka ihe ndị dị mkpa na-akpali iji ịntanetị (James na ndị ọzọ, 1995).

translations.source: “Personal involvement” and “continuing relationships” were also identified as new motivation aspects by Eighmey and McCord (1998) when they investigated audience reactions to websites.
translations.reference: Eighmey na McCord(1998) chọpụtara na “nsonye” na “mmekọrịta ga-adịgịde” sokwa na ihe mkpali ọhụrụ mgbe ha nyochara mmeghachi omume ndị na-abịa n'ọtụtụ webụsaịtị.
translations.hypothesis: "Ọrụ onwe na" na "ndọta dịgide" bụkwa ihe ndị Eighmey na McCord (1998) chọpụtara dị ka ihe na-eme ka mmadụ nwee mmasị, mgbe ha nwalere otú ndị na-ele akpa ntanwete (websites) si eme.

translations.source: The use of video recording has led to important discoveries in the interpretation of micro-expressions, facial movements which last a few milliseconds.
translations.reference: Ojiji nke ndekọ vidio edugawo na ụmụ nchọpụta dị mkpa n’ime nkọwa nke nzipụta-n’ihu-kentakịrị, mmegharị ihu nke na-anọru milisekọnd ole na ole.
translations.hypothesis: A ntụzi nke vidio emeela ka a mara ọtụtụ ihe dị mkpa banyere otú esi tụgharị ihe omume dị nta, bụ nke na-apụta n'ihi mgbanwe dị nta na ihu na-adịkarị obere oge.

translations.source: In particular, it is claimed that one can detect whether a person is lying by interpreting micro-expressions correctly.
translations.reference: Akachasị ekwu na mmadụ nwere ike ịma mmgbe mmadụ na atụ asi ma ọbụrụ na onwere ike ịkọwapụta obere mmegharị ahụ dị iche iche ọfụma.
translations.hypothesis: N'ịdịiche, a na-ekwu na enwere ike ịmatụ ma otu onye na-akọ akụkọ ahụhụ site n'ịgụnye usoro mmegharị ihu ndị dị nta n'ụzọ ziri ezi.

translations.source: Oliver Sacks, in his paper The President's Speech, indicated how people who are unable to understand speech because of brain damage are nevertheless able to assess sincerity accurately.
translations.reference: Oliver Saks, n'akwụkwọ ya Okwu Onyeisi Obodo, gosiri ka ndị enweghị ike ịghọta ọnụ okwu n'ihi isi mmebi nwere ike ikwu mgbe mmadụ na-ekwu eziokwu.
translations.hypothesis: Oliver Sacks, n'ime akwụkwọ ya bụ "Onyeisi Ahụ Na-ekwu," gosiri otú ndị na-enweghị ike ịghọta okwu n'ihi mmebi nke ụbụrụ ha, n'agbanyeghị, nwere ike ịmatụta ọdịmma nke okwu ahụ nke ọma.

translations.source: He even suggests that such abilities in interpreting human behavior may be shared by animals such as domestic dogs.
translations.reference: Ọ na-ekwu rịị na ikekwe ụmụ anụmanụ dịka nkịta ụlọ nwekwara ụdịrị ikikere a ịghọta omume mmadụ
translations.hypothesis: Ọ na-ekwu ọbụna na ụdị ikike a nke ịghọta omume mmadụ nwere ike ịbụ nke eji na ụdị anụmanụ ndị ọzọ, dịka nkịta ụlọ.

translations.source: Twentieth century research has shown that there are two pools of genetic variation: hidden and expressed.
translations.reference: Nnyocha na narị afọ nke iri abụọ egosipụtala na enwere ụdịrị genetik variyeshọn abụọ: nke zoro ezo na nke pụtara apụta.
translations.hypothesis: Nnyocha nke narịkwa abụọ egosila na e nwere ụzọ abụọ nke mgbanwe nke akụrụngwa: otu bụ nke ejiri ya, ebe otu ọzọ bụ nke etụkwaghị.

translations.source: Mutation adds new genetic variation, and selection removes it from the pool of expressed variation.
translations.reference: Mgbanwe n'ọdịdị na-agbakwunye ọdịdị kejenetiki ọhụrụ, ma nhọpụta na-ewepụ ya n'ogwu ọdịdị nke a kọwapụtara.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbanwe nke gene na-abawanye ụdị gene ọhụrụ, ma nhọrọ na-ewepụ ya site na ndú nke ụdị gene ndị nwere ike igosi.

translations.source: Segregation and recombination shuffle variation back and forth between the two pools with each generation.
translations.reference: Nkewa na ntughari nkpokorita nkeghari na azu n'etiti ọdọ mmiri abua ahu na ọgbọ o bula.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe ọkụkọ na-agbanwegharị na-ejikọta ọnụ, ha na-agbanwegharị ụdị dị iche iche n'etiti otu ụlọọka abụọ ahụ, ọ bụrụkwa ọkụkọ ọhụrụ.

translations.source: Out on the savanna, it is hard for a primate with a digestive system like that of humans to satisfy its amino-acid requirements from available plant resources.
translations.reference: N'ime savanna, ọ bụ ihe siri ike na primate nwere usoro nri dị ka nke mmadụ iji mejupụta amino-acid chọrọ site na ihe ọkụkụ dịnụ.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime obibi ahụ, ọ bụ ihe isi ike maka anụmanụ nke nwere usoro ahụike dịka nke mmadụ iji nweta ihe ndị ọ chọrọ maka ahụ ya site na ihe ndị utụtụ na-enye.

translations.source: Moreover, failure to do so has serious consequences: growth depression, malnutrition, and ultimately death.
translations.reference: Ọzọ dịka ibe ya, ị jụ ime ihe a nwere nnukwu ntaramahụhụ: nnukwu ndamụmbà, ọtịtaahụ, nakwa ọnwụ n'ikpeazụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọzọkwa, ọ bụrụ na a gaghị eme ya, ọ nwere nsona dị ukwuu: mbelata n'ọganihu, ọrịa nke ibu adịghị ma, na n'ikpeazụ, ọnwụ.

translations.source: The most readily accessible plant resources would have been the proteins accessible in leaves and legumes, but these are hard for primates like us to digest unless they are cooked.
translations.reference: Ihe akụrụngwa a na-enweta ngwa ngwa ga-abụrịrị protein ndị dị na akwụkwọ na legume gasị, mana ihe ndị a siri ike maka ndị nyiri mmadụ ndịọzọ bị n’ọhịa dịka anyị iji gbazèe ma anyị sie ya n’ọkụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịmma, ihe ndị uto na-enwekarịkwa bụ proteinụ ndị dị n'ime akwụkwọ na akụkụ osisi, mana ọ bụ ihe siri ike ka primates dịka anyị wee rie ya, ma ọ bụrụ na ọ gaghị ekpọ ya.

translations.source: In contrast, animal foods (ants, termites, eggs) not only are easily digestible, but they provide high-quantity proteins that contain all the essential amino acids.
translations.reference: N’aka ọzọ, nri anụmanụ arụrụ, ntanta, akwa) abughi naani di nfe, kama ha na-enye oke protein nke nwere amino acid nile di nma.
translations.hypothesis: N'abalị, nri ndị sitere n'ani (ọtụtụ anụ, anụ ọhịa, akwụkwọ) ọ bụghị naanị na ha dị mfe ịkpọta, kamakwa ha na-enye protein dị ukwuu nke nwere ihe niile dị mkpa nke amino acid.

translations.source: All things considered, we should not be surprised if our own ancestors solved their "protein problem" in somewhat the same way that chimps on the savanna do today.
translations.reference: Eleghị anya, ya atụla anyị n'anya ma ọbụrụ na ndị nna nna anyi ji aka ha gboo "mkpa protin" ha n'usoro dị ka nke enwe bi n'ọhịa si eme taa.
translations.hypothesis: N'ile anya, anyị ekwughị na ọ ga-adị anyị ka ihe ijuanya ma ọ bụrụ na ndị nna anyị nwere ụzọ dị otu a, dị ka ndị chimpanzee na-eme taa na akụkụ ubi, iji wepụta "ihe mgbochi protein" ha.

translations.source: Sleep interruption is the process of purposefully awakening during your normal sleep period and falling asleep a short time later (10–60 minutes).
translations.reference: Nkwụsịtụ ụra bụ usoro nke ịkpacharanya eteta ụra mgbe oge ị na-ehikarị ụra ma na-ada n’ụra mgbe obere oge gachara (nkeji 10–60).
translations.hypothesis: Ịgbatị ụra bụ usoro iji atụgharị uche gị wee tọgharịa n'ime ụra n'oge ụra gị nkịtị, wee gaa n'ụra ọzọ mgbe ọtụtụ oge (10-60 nkeji).

translations.source: This can be easily done by using a relatively quiet alarm clock to bring you to consciousness without fully waking you.
translations.reference: Enwere ike ime ka n’uzo mfe site na iweta atanu ogbu-opi uzu ya dikariri nwayo ikpobata gi na uche kama ghara ikpotecha gi na-ozuzuoke.
translations.hypothesis: Enwere ike ime nke a n'ụzọ dị mfe site n'ịji agba ọkụ nke na-eme ụda dị nta iji buru gị ụzọ na ịbụrụ onye nweere onwe ya, mana ọ naghị etinye gị n'ọnọdụ nke ịbụrụ onye tiri kpamkpam.

translations.source: If you find yourself resetting the clock in your sleep, it can be placed on the other side of the room, forcing you to get out of bed to turn it off.
translations.reference: Ọ bụrụ na ị hụtara onwe gị na-ewubergharị elekere gị n’ime nrọ gị, e nwere ike idobe ya n’akụkụ nke ọzọ nke ime ụlọ ahụ, na-amanye gị isi n’akwa bilie ịgbanyụ ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-ahụ onwe gị na-agbanwe ala ụlọ na-eji ekwekọ na mgbe ị na-anwụ anwụ, ọ nwere ike itinye ya n'akụkụ ọzọ nke ụlọ, nke ga-adị ka ị ga-esi pụọ n'ụlọ ọrụ gị iji gbanyụọ ya.

translations.source: Other biorhythm-based options involve drinking lots of fluid (particularly water or tea, a known diuretic) prior to sleep, forcing one to get up to urinate.
translations.reference: Ụzọ biorhythm ndị ọzọ gụnyere ịñụ oke ihe mmiri (karịsịa mmiri maọbụ tii, dayuretik a maara amaara) tupu arahụ ụra, na-amanye mmadụ ibili maka ịnyụ amịrị.
translations.hypothesis: Ụzọ ndị ọzọ nke eji nyocha biorhythm mee bụ ịsa mmiri ọtụtụ (karịsịa mmiri ma ọ bụ ti, nke bụ ihe na-enyere aka ịkpọfu mmiri), tupu ịgba ụra, ya mere ka onye ahụ aghara ịgbatị iji akpọfu mmiri.

translations.source: The amount of inner peace a person possesses correlates oppositely to the amount of tension in one’s body and spirit.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ ole udo nke obi mmadụ nwere na-emekọrịta na nchịkọta ihu na ole obimgbalielu nọ n'ime ahụ na mmụọ nke mmadụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọnọdụ udo nke onye nwere na-adịkarị iche iche n'ụzọ dị iche na ọkụkọ nke onye nwere n'ime ahụ ya na ọsirihi ya.

translations.source: The lower the tension, the more positive the life force present. Every person has the potential to find absolute peace and contentment.
translations.reference: Ka a na-ewetulata esemokwu ahụ, ka ike ndụ nọ ugbu a na-adịkwuo mma. Mmadu niile nwere ike mmepụta ịchọta udo zuru oke na afọ ojuju.
translations.hypothesis: Oge ọ bụla mgbe ọdịdị nke ihe dị ala, ọ bụkwa oge ọ bụla mgbe ike ndụ na-adịkarị. Ọ bụrụ otu onye, ọ nwere ike ịhụ uto na obi ụtọ zuru oke.

translations.source: Everyone can achieve enlightenment. The only thing standing in the way of this goal is our own tension and negativity.
translations.reference: Mmadụ nile nwere ike ịma ihe. Sọ ohe nọchiri ụzọ bụ ekweghị ekwe nke anyi na ụjọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla nwere ike ịnweta ọghom. Ụfọdụ ihe na-egbochi anyị site n'inweta ihe a bụ mgbe anyị na-enwe ọghọ na ọdịmma.

translations.source: The Tibetan Buddhism is based on the teachings of Buddha, but were extended by the mahayana path of love and by a lot of techniques from Indian Yoga.
translations.reference: Buddhism ndị Tibet dabere n’ụmụ nkuzi nke Buddha, mana adọtịkwuru ha site n’aka ụzọ nke ihụnanya mahayana ya na site n’aka ọtụtụ usoro si na Yoga Indịa.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdụlịchị Buddhism nke Tibet dabere n'ụtụaka nke Buddha, mana a kọwara ya ọzọ site n'ụzọ Mahayana nke ịhụnanya, yana site n'ọtụtụ usoro sitere na Yoga nke India.

translations.source: In principle the Tibetan Buddhism is very simple. It consists of Kundalini Yoga, meditation and the path of all-embracing love.
translations.reference: Na ntọala, Buddhism Tibet dị ezigbo mfe. Ọ mejupụtara Yoga Kundalini, ntụgharị uche na ụzọ nke ịhụnanya nnabata-ihe niile.
translations.hypothesis: N'echiche, Buddhism nke Tibet dị mfe karị. Ọ bụ ụzọ nke gụnyere Kundalini Yoga, mmetụta uche, na ụzọ ịhụnanya zuru ụfọdụ.

translations.source: With Kundalini Yoga the Kundalini energy (enlightenment energy) is awakened through yoga postures, breathing exercises, mantras and visualizations.
translations.reference: N’iji Yoga Kundalini ike Kundalini (ike mmepe anya) bụ nke etetara site n’ụmụ postchọ yoga, mgbatị ahụ iku ume, ukwe ntụgharị uche na ihe ngosi.
translations.hypothesis: Na n'oge Kundalini Yoga, ike Kundalini (ike ọdịmma) na-awakọm site na ọrụ ahụ nke yoga, atụmatụ ume, mantras, na ihe ndị a na-echeta n'uche.

translations.source: The center of Tibetan meditation is the Deity Yoga. Through the visualization of various deities the energy channels are cleaned, the chakras are activated and the enlightenment consciousness is created.
translations.reference: Nke bụ isiokwu ntụgharị uche nke ndị Tibet bụ Deyiti Yoga. Site na ichepụta chi dị iche iche, a na ehichapụta ụkpụrụ ike, kpọghee chakra ma kepụta owuweanya nke amamihe.
translations.hypothesis: Otu ebe ọzọ nke atụmụta uche nke ndị Tibetan bụ "Deity Yoga." Site n'ịhụ anya ihe dị iche iche, a na-ehicha ọwaọka mmalite ike, a na-agbasa akụkụ ndị ahụ a na-akpọ "chakras," ma ọ na-ebute ụkpụrụ uche nke ịmata eziokwu.

translations.source: Germany was a common enemy in World War 2, leading to cooperation between the USSR and USA. With the end of the war the clashes of system, process and culture led to the countries falling out.
translations.reference: Jamini bụ ndị iro ọha n'Agha Ụwa nke abụọ, nke mere mba USA na USSR ji nwee mmekọ. Ka agha gwụrụ, esemokwu usoro omume, na omenala mere mba ndị ahụ ji nwee okwu.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge agha ụwa nke abụọ, Germany bụ onye iwe dị iche iche, nke mere ka USSR na USA jikọọ ọnụ. Mgbe agha ahụ kwụsịrị, mgbe ahụ, ihe mgba ọrịa dị n'etiti usoro, usoro ọrụ, na ọdụnwu mere ka mba ndị ahụ kewapụ.

translations.source: With two years of the end of the war, the former allies were now enemies and the Cold War began.
translations.reference: N'etiti afọ abụọ nke nlụcha nke agha ahụ, ndị mba bụbu ndị mmekọrịta bụzi ndị iro ugbu a ma Agha Oyi ahụ bidokwara.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ afọ abụọ gachara mgbe a kwụsịrị agha ahụ, ndị bụ ezi di na ezi n'oge agha ahụ bụ ndị enweghị otu echiche, ma agha "ọchịchị ọkụ" malitere.

translations.source: It was to last for the next 40 years and would be fought for real, by proxy armies, on battlefields from Africa to Asia, in Afghanistan, Cuba and many other places.
translations.reference: O kwesịrị ịnọru ruo afọ iri anọ na-abịa abịa ma a ga-alụkwa ya n'ezie, site n'aka ụsụụ ndị agha nnọchite, n'ama agha site n'Afrịka ruo Eshia, n'ime Afghanistan, Kiuba na ọtụtụ ebe ndị ọzọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ ga-adị ndụ maka afọ iri abụọ na anọ na-abịa, ma a ga-alụ ọgụ n'ime ya, site na ndị agha na-anọchọ ya, na nkịtị egwuregwu, site na Afrika ruo Asia, na Afghanistan, Cuba, na ebe ndị ọzọ dị iche iche.

translations.source: By September 17, 1939, the Polish defense was already broken, and the only hope was to retreat and reorganise along the Romanian bridgehead.
translations.reference: Mgbe Septemba 17, 1939 ruru, a kutuola nchekwa ndị Poland; naanị olileanya ha nwere bụ ịlaghachi tụọ atụmatụ ọzọ n'akụkụ isi briij Romenia.
translations.hypothesis: Na 17 Septemba, afọ 1939, agha nke Poland dị ala, ma naanị olileanya bụ ịgbawa na ịgbasa ọtụtụ ndị agha n'akụkụ osimiri Romania.

translations.source: However, these plans were rendered obsolete nearly overnight, when over 800,000 soldiers from the Soviet's Union Red Army entered and created the Belarussian and Ukrainian fronts after invading the eastern regions of Poland in violation of the Riga Peace Treaty, the Soviet-Polish Non-Aggression Pact, and other international treaties, both bilateral and multilateral.
translations.reference: Mana, o gbughi oge ka atụmatụ a niile laa n'efu, mgbe ihe karịrị ndị Sọviet Yunịọn Red Amị 800,000 banyere, kepụta ogige agha ndị Belarụs na Yukren, ka ha wakpochara akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ Poland na nnupu isi nye Nkwekọrịta Udo Riga, Nkwekọrịta Udo Sọviet Yunịọn na Poland, na ọtụtụ nkwekọrịta ndị ọzọ, ma nke dị n'etiti mba abụọ, na nke dị n'etiti ọtụtụ mba.
translations.hypothesis: Otú ọ dị, atụmatụ ndị a mechara eme ka ọ ghara ịdị, n'ime obere oge, mgbe karịa 800,000 ndị agha sitere na Armi Ahụhụ nke Soviet Union banyere n'ime ma guzobere ọgụ egwu nke Belarusi na Ukraine, mgbe ha rịọrọ mba Poland n'akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwu, na-emezighị usoro Riga, nkwekọrịta a na-enweghị ọgụ n'etiti Soviet na Poland, na usoro mba ụwa ndị ọzọ, ma ndị dị n'etiti ụlọ abụọ na ndị ọtụtụ.

translations.source: Using ships to transport goods is by far the most efficient way to move large amounts of people and goods across oceans.
translations.reference: Iji ụgbọ mmiri ebughari ngwa ahịa bụ ụzọ kachasị mma n'ezie iji buru ọtụtụ ndị na ọtụtụ ngwa gafee oke osimiri.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ mgbe, iji ụgbọ mmiri na-ebu ngwaahịa bụ ụzọ kacha mma iji buru ndị mmadụ na ngwaahịa ọtụtụ n'ime ha n'oge dị mkpirikpi, ma ọ bụkwa iji agafe osimiri.

translations.source: The job of navies has traditionally been to ensure that your country maintains the ability to move your people and goods, while at the same time, interfering with your enemy's ability to move his people and goods.
translations.reference: Ọrụ nke ndị agha nke mmiri abụrụla kemgbe ịgba mbọ hụ na mba gị jidesiri ike ikikere ibugharị ndị gị na ngwaahịa gị, ma n'otu mgbe ahụ, na-egbochi ikikere onye iro gị ibugharị ndị ya na ngwaahịa ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ndị ọrụ osimiri bụ, n'agbanyeghị, iji hụ na mba gị nwere ike ịgafe ndị mmadụ na ngwaahịa, ebe otu oge ahụ, ha na-egbochi onye iji gị isi gafe ndị mmadụ na ngwaahịa ya.

translations.source: One of the most noteworthy recent examples of this was the North Atlantic campaign of WWII. The Americans were trying to move men and materials across the Atlantic Ocean to help Britain.
translations.reference: Otu n’ime ọmụmatụ oge na-etebeghị anya nke a kacha tozuo oke bụbu kampeenụ Ugwu Atlantik nke WWII. Ndị Amerịka nọ na-anwa ibugharị ụmụ nwoke na ngwongwo gafee Oke osimiri Atlantik inyere Britenụ aka.
translations.hypothesis: Otu n'ime ihe omume kacha ama ama nke mere n'oge ahụ bụ ọrụ agha nke North Atlantic n'oge Agha Ụwa nke Abụọ. Ndị Amerika na-agba mbọ iji kwanye ndị mmadụ na ihe ndị ọzọ site na Oké Osimiri Atlantic iji nyere Britain aka.

translations.source: At the same time, the German navy, using mainly U-boats, was trying to stop this traffic.
translations.reference: N'otu mgbe ahụ, ndị agha nke mmiri nke Jamanị, n'iji naanị ụgbọokpurummiri, nọ na-agbalị ịkwụsị mkpọchi ụzọ a.
translations.hypothesis: N'otu oge ahụ, ndị agha osimiri nke Germany, bụ ndị na-eji ụgbọ mmiri ndụ (U-boats) karịsịa, na-agba mbọ iweghachite usoro azụmahịa ahụ.

translations.source: Had the Allies failed, Germany probably would have been able to conquer Britain as it had the rest of Europe.
translations.reference: Ọ bụrụ na ndị mba bụbu ndị mmekọrịta dara, Jamanị nwere ike eleghi anya merie Briten dị ka o mere Yurop ndị ọzọ fọdụrụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na ndị otu ndị na-akwado (Allies) erubeghị, ọ bụ ike na Germany gaara enwekarịkwa ikike iji chịkwa Britain, dịka ọ mere n'akụkụ Europe niile.

translations.source: Goats seem to have been first domesticated roughly 10,000 years ago in the Zagros Mountains of Iran.
translations.reference: Ewu yiri ka e buru ụzọ mee ya anụụlọ n’ihe ruru puku afọ iri gara aga n'ugwu Zagros nke Iran.
translations.hypothesis: Anya ụkọ ahụ yiri ka e malitere ịmụ ha n'ime ụlọ, ihe dị ka afọ 10,000 gara aga, n'okpuru ugwu Zagros na Iran.

translations.source: Ancient cultures and tribes began to keep them for easy access to milk, hair, meat, and skins.
translations.reference: Omenala ndị mgbe ochie na agbụrụ bidoro iji dobe ha maka inweta ohere dị mfe na mmiri ara, ntutu isi, anụ, na anụahụ gasị.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịnala na ndị otu ochie malitere ịdebe ha iji nweta uru dị mfe, dị ka mmiri, isi, anụ, na akpụ.

translations.source: Domestic goats were generally kept in herds that wandered on hills or other grazing areas, often tended by goatherds who were frequently children or adolescents, similar to the more widely known shepherd. These methods of herding are still used today.
translations.reference: E dobere n'ozuzu ụmụ ehu ụlọ n'ime ìgwè ndị nke pagharịrị n'elu ugwu ma ọ bụ ebe ịta ahịhịa ndị ọzọ, nke ọtụtụ mgbe bụ ndị ọzụzụ ehu na-elekọta ha ndị nke na abụkarị ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ụmụ ntorọbịa, nke yiri onye ọzụzụ atụrụ a ka mara ama. A ka na-eji usoro ọzụzụ ehu ndị a ruo taa.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ụlọ a na-eji ebe a na-eji ụmụ ahụ na-agba, na ha na-agba n'oké osimiri ma ọ bụ ebe ndị ọzọ e ji eme nri anụ. Ọtụtụ oge, ndị na-elekọta akwụkwọ ahụ bụ ndị na-agba akwụkwọ, bụ ndị karịrịsịrị ụmụaka ma ọ bụ ndị na-eto eto, dị ka ndị na-elekọta ụkọ. A na-enweghị ụzọ a na-eji agba akwụkwọ ahụ ruo taa.

translations.source: Wagonways were built in England as early as the 16th Century.
translations.reference: E wuru ụzọ ụgbọ ibu gasị n’Ingland dị ka n'oge dị ka narị afọ nke iri na isii ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ụzọ nke ụgbọ oloko bịarala etụlite na England kemgbe narị nke 16.

translations.source: Although wagonways merely consisted of parallel planks of wood, they allowed horses pulling them to achieve greater speeds and pull larger loads than on the slightly more rough roads of the day.
translations.reference: Agbanyeghị ụmụ ụzọwagọn nwere naanị ogwe osisi nọ n’akụkụ n’akụkụ, ha nyere ụmụ ịnyịnya na-esere ha òhèrè irute ekwomọsọ ndị karịrị ma sere ibu kara dị ukwuu karịa n’ụmụ ụzọ nke ụbọchị ahụ ndị karịtụrụ dị ike ike.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na ọrụ ụzọ ahụ dị ka ọ na-abụ, ọ bụ naanị igwe osisi nke jikọrọ ọnụ, ha nyere ahiafulu na-eje ije n'elu ha ohere ịga ngwa ngwa karịa na ụzọ ndị ọzọ dị n'oge ahụ, ọ bụkwa ohere ịbụta ihe karịrị.

translations.source: Crossties were introduced fairly early to hold the tracks in place. Gradually, however, it was realised that tracks would be more efficient if they had a stip of iron on the top.
translations.reference: Ebidoro mgbe gboo were krọstaị na-arụ ụzọ ụgbọoloko ka o were gbasie ike. Obere obere a bịa mata na ụzọ ụgbọoloko ga-esikarị ike ma ọ bụrụ na o nweturu obere igwe n’elu ya.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ụzọ (crossties) bịarutere n'oge mbụ iji dobe ụzọ ndị ahụ n'ebe ha dị. Otú ọ dị, n'oge na-aga, ọ bịara mara anya na ụzọ ndị ahụ ga-arụ ọrụ nke ọma ma ọ bụrụ na ha nwere akara nke írị na elu ha.

translations.source: This became common practice, but the iron caused more wear on the wooden wheels of the wagons.
translations.reference: Nke mechara bụrụ omume a na-emekarị, mana igwe ahụ kpatakwuru ndọwa n'ụkwụ ụmụ ụgbọ ibu ejiri osisi mee.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụrụkwa ya ihe nkịtị, mana akara ahụ mere ka ọtụtụ ihe mgbu bipụta na akwụkwọ ndụ nke ọkwọ ụgbọ.

translations.source: Eventually, wooden wheels were replaced by iron wheels. In 1767, the first full-iron rails were introduced.
translations.reference: N'ikpeazụ, eji wiil ígwè dochie wiil osisi. N'afọ 1767, e wepụtara wiil nke mbụ ejị igwe rụọ kpam kpam.
translations.hypothesis: N'aka ekwu, akara osisi bịara dochie akara igwe. Na afọ 1767, akara igwe zuru oke bịara ebute.

translations.source: The first known transportation was walking, humans began walking upright two million years ago with the emergence of Homo Erectus (meaning upright man).
translations.reference: Usoro njem e bu ụzọ mara ama bụ ịga ije, ụmụ mmadụ bidoro ịkwụ ọtọ aga ije afọ nde abụọ gara aga site na mpụta nke Homo Erektus (nke pụtara nwoke kwụ ọtọ).
translations.hypothesis: Ụzọ mbụ eji aga ebe dị iche bụ ịga n'ụkwụ. Ndị mmadụ malitere ịga n'ụkwụ nke ọma abụọ miriọna afọ gara, mgbe Homo Erectus (ya bụ "onye na-agba n'ụkwụ") pụtara.

translations.source: Their predecessors, the Australopithecus did not walk upright as habitually.
translations.reference: Ndị bụ ha ụzọ, Ọstralopitekus ahụ akwụghị ọtọ gaa ije dị ka n'akparamagwa.
translations.hypothesis: Ọkpara ha, ndị Australopithecus, adịghị eme ka ha na-eje ije n'ụzọ ziri ezi dị ka ọ na-emekarị.

translations.source: Bipedal specializations are found in Australopithecus fossils from 4.2-3.9 million years ago, although Sahelanthropus may have walked on two legs as early as seven million years ago.
translations.reference: Achoputara ọkachamara bipedal na fosil Australopithecus site na nde nde afọ 4.2-3.9 gara aga, o bu ezie na Sahelanthropus nwere ike ije ije n'ukwu abuo na nde afọ asaa gara aga.
translations.hypothesis: Aghụghọ banyere ụdị anụmanụ nke na-eje ije n'ụkwụ abụọ ahụ chọpụtara na afọ fossils nke Australopithecus, nke dị n'oge gara aga site na afọ 4.2 ruo 3.9. Otú ọ dị, ọ nwere ike bụ na Sahelanthropus malitere ịje ije n'ụkwụ abụọ ruo afọ asaa gara aga.

translations.source: We can start living more friendly to the environment, we can join to the environmental movement, and we can even be activists in order to reduce the future suffering in some degree.
translations.reference: Anyị nwere ike malite ibi n’enyi karịa na gburugburu ebe obibi, anyị nwere ike isonye ije nke gburugburu ebe obibi, ma anyị nwekwara ike ịbụ ndị ọchọ mgbanwe ka e nwee ike belata ntaramahụhụ ọdịnihu ruo ogo ụfọdụ.
translations.hypothesis: Anyị nwere ike ịmalite ibi ndụ n'ụzọ nke na-adị mma n'ime gburugburu ebe obibi anyị, anyị nwere ike ịsonye na ọrụ ndị na-elekọta gburugburu ebe obibi, na anyị nwekwara ike ịbụ ndị na-agba ọsọ iji belata ọrụ ọjọọ nke ga-abịa n'ọdịnihu, ọ dịla mma.

translations.source: This is just like symptomatic treatment in many cases. However, if we do not only want a temporary solution, then we should find the root of the problems, and we should deactivate them.
translations.reference: Nke a dị nnọọ ka ọgwụgwọ kemgbaàmà n’ọtụtụ okwu. Agbanyeghị, ọ bụrụ na anyị achọghị naanị ọsịsa nke nwa oge, ya mere anyị kwesịrị ịchọta isi ihe kpatara nsogbu ndị ahụ, ma anyị kwesịrị iwepụ̀ ike ha.
translations.hypothesis: Nke a bụ otu ihe dị ka ọgwụgwọ nke na-atụgharịkarị ahụ na ọtụtụ ọnọdụ. Otú ọ dị, ọ bụrụ na anyị anaghị achọ naanị ngwọta dị obere oge, anyị ga-achọpụta ihe bụ ihe kpatara nsogbu ndị a, wee kwụsị ha.

translations.source: It is obvious enough that the world has changed much because of humankind's scientific and technological advancements, and problems have become greater because of overpopulation and mankind's extravagant lifestyle.
translations.reference: O doro anya nke ọma n'ụwa agbanweela nnukwu n'ihi ụmụ ọganihu nke sayensị na teknụzụ nke ụmụ mmadụ, ma ụmụ nsogbu adịla nnukwu karịa n'ihi ọnụọgụgụ mmadụ karịrị akarị na ibifụga ndụ ókè nke ụmụ mmadụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ihe dị mma ịghọta na ụwa ahụ esịtịrị nnukwu mgbanwe n'ihi mgbanwe sayensị na teknụzụ nke mmadụ, yana na nsogbu ahụ abụrụla karịa n'ihi nnukwu ọha mmadụ na ụdị ndụ dị oke ọnụ nke mmadụ na-ebi.

translations.source: After its adoption by Congress on July 4, a handwritten draft signed by the President of Congress John Hancock and the Secretary Charles Thomson was then sent a few blocks away to the printing shop of John Dunlap.
translations.reference: Mgbe Kọngres nyechara ya nkwekọrịta ha na Julaị 4, e weere ya n'akwụkwọ eji aka dee, nke Jọn Hankọk Onye isi Kọngres na Chals Tọmsin Onye odeakwụkwọ tinyere akara nkwado ha, wega ya n'ụlọ mbipụta Jọn Dunlap nke eteghi aka.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe National Assembly kpebiri ya na 4 ọnwa July, akwụkwọ aka ederede nke ode akwụkwọ nke National Assembly, John Hancock, na ode akwụkwọ, Charles Thomson, bịarutere, wee zipụtara ya n'ebe dị obere, na ụlọ akwụkwọ nke John Dunlap.

translations.source: Through the night between 150 and 200 copies were made, now known as "Dunlap broadsides".
translations.reference: N'ime abali n'etiti mbipụta otu narị na iri ise ya na narị abụọ ka e mere, nke a mara ugbu a dị ka “Dunlap broadsides”.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime abalị ahụ, e wepụtara ihe ruru 150 ruo 200 nkeji, bụ nke a maara ugbu a dị ka "akwụkwọ akụkọ nke Dunlap".

translations.source: The first public reading of the document was by John Nixon in the yard of Independence Hall on July 8.
translations.reference: Oge mbụ a gụpụtara edemede a n'ọha bụ na Julaị 8, nke John Nixn gụrụ na mbaraezi Ụlọọgbakọ Ndipenda.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ahụ ebutebe ya n'ihu ọha bụ nke John Nixon mere n'ebe ọdịda anyanwụ nke Independence Hall na Ụbọchị July nke 8.

translations.source: One was sent to George Washington on July 6, who had it read to his troops in New York on July 9. A copy reached London on August 10.
translations.reference: Na Julaị 6, e zigaara George Washington otu kọpị, onye mere ka a gụọrọ ya ndị agha ya na Niu Yọk na Julaị 9. Otu kọpị ruru Lọndọn n'Ọgọstụ 10.
translations.hypothesis: Otu akwụkwọ bịarutere George Washington na Ụbọchị 6 nke Julaị, wee bịa na ndị agha ya na New York na Ụbọchị 9 nke Julaị, ebe ha gụrụ ya. Otu ihe onyonyo bịarutere London na Ụbọchị 10 nke Ọgọstụ.

translations.source: The 25 Dunlap broadsides still known to exist are the oldest surviving copies of the document. The original handwritten copy has not survived.
translations.reference: Dunlap brọdsaịd 25 ka nọ taa bụ kọpị edemede izizi ndị kachasị dị ochie. Nke izizi e ji aka dee anọzighi.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ndị "broadside" 25 nke Dunlap, bụ ndị ka e ji mara na ha ka dị ndụ, bụ ihe ndị ochie kachasị ebe dị ndụ nke akwụkwọ ahụ. A kwụkwọ akwụkwọ ahụ nke e dere aka n'oge mbụ, enweghị ya taa.

translations.source: Many paleontologists today believe that one group of dinosaurs survived and is alive today. We call them birds.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ ndị ọkàchamara ihe banyere fọsịl anụmanụ na osisi taa kwenyere na otu òtù daịnosọọ lanarịrị ma dị ndụ taa. Anyị na-akpọ ha ụmụ nnụnụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ndị ọmụmụ ihe omume nke ụwa ochie n'ụbọchị a kwenyere na otu otu nke ndị dinosaur nọrọ na ha dị ndụ taa. Anyị na-akpọ ha "anụ ọkụkọ."

translations.source: Many people don't think about them as dinosaurs because they have feathers and can fly.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ anaghị eche bayere ha dị ka daịnosọọ n'ihi na ha nwere nku ma nwee ike ife efe.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ mmadụ anaghị echeta ha dị ka ụmaahịa n'ihi na ha nwere ọkpụkpu na ha nwere ike ịnya.

translations.source: But there are a lot of things about birds that still look like a dinosaur.
translations.reference: Mana a ka nwere ọtụtụ ihe gbasara ụmụ nnụnụ ndị yiri nke daịnosọọ.
translations.hypothesis: Mana, enwere ọtụtụ ihe gbasara anụ ọhịa nke ka na-adị ka anụ ọhịa dị iche.

translations.source: They have feet with scales and claws, they lay eggs, and they walk on their two back legs like a T-Rex.
translations.reference: Ha nwere okpa ya na abuba na mbu aka, ha na eyi akwa, ha nakwa aga ije na ukwu oji ha abuo dika T-Rex.
translations.hypothesis: Ha nwere ụkwụ nwere akpụkpụ na akwa, ha na-ere ahụhụ, ma ha na-agafe n'elu ụkwụ ha abụọ dị n'azụ, dị ka T-Rex.

translations.source: Virtually all computers in use today are based on the manipulation of information which is coded in the form of binary numbers.
translations.reference: Ihe dịka igwe kọmputa niile e ji arụ ọrụ taa bụ ihe sitere na mkpụrụokwu ndị a gwakọrọ agwakọ nke e tinyere dịka mkpụrụọnụọgụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ kọmputa ndị a na-eji taa na-arụ ọrụ site na iji usoro nke ịmepụta ma na-ahazi ozi, nke a na-ede n'ụdị nọmba abụọ (binary).

translations.source: A binary number can have only one of two values, i.e. 0 or 1, and these numbers are referred to as binary digits - or bits, to use computer jargon.
translations.reference: Otu akara ọnụọgụ abụọ nwere ike inwe naanị otu n’ime mbamuru abụọ, ya bụ 0 ma ọ bụ 1, ma a na-akpọ akara ndị a dị ka ọnụọgụ keọnụọgụ abụọ - ma ọ bụ bits, iji asụsụ mpụiche kọmputa.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị nọmba abụọ nwere naanị otu n'ime ụkpụrụ abụọ, ya bụ, 0 ma ọ bụ 1, ma a na-akpọ ụdị nọmba ndị a "ọdịdị nọmba abụọ" - ma ọ bụ "bits," dịka a na-eji na teknụzụ kọmputa.

translations.source: Internal poisoning may not be immediately apparent. Symptoms, such as vomiting are sufficiently general that an immediate diagnosis cannot be made.
translations.reference: Ọrịa ịtụ nsị nke ime ahụ nwere ike ọ gaghị adị ire ozigbo. Ihe ngosipụta ya, dịka ọgbụgbọ, bụ ihe ndị na-emekwa n'ọtụtụ ọrịa ndị ọzọ. Ya mere na enweghi ike ịchọpụta ọrịa a ozigbo ozigbo.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ nwere ike na mmetụta nke ịgba ọgwụ ahụ n'ime ahụ agaghị apụta ozugbo. Otu ihe ndụ, dịka ịgba ọgwụ, bụ ihe zuru oke na ọ nweghị ike ịkọwa ihe mere ya ozugbo.

translations.source: The best indication of internal poisoning may be the presence of an open container of medication or toxic household chemicals.
translations.reference: Ndosipụta kachasị mma maka inwe ńsí n’ime ahụ nwere ike ịbụ ọnụnọ nke mkpọ ogwụ ghe oghe ma ọ bụ kemikalụ ezinụlọ ndị na-egbu agbu.
translations.hypothesis: Otu ihe kacha akpali na enwere mmetụta ọrịa n'ime ahụ bụ oge ụfọdụ, ọ pụrụ ịbụ na enwere akwụkwọ ahụike ma ọ bụ kemịkalụ ndị na-emerụ ahụ nke e jiri eme ihe n'ụlọ, ma ha adịghị na akwụkwọ ụlọ.

translations.source: Check the label for specific first aid instructions for that specific poison.
translations.reference: Lelee nnyeàhà ahụ maka ntụziaka mgbata ọsọ enyemaka mbụ akọwapụtara maka nsi ahụ akọwapụtara.
translations.hypothesis: Lelee akara ahụ ka ịhụ ntuziaka ndị a chọrọ maka enyemaka mbụ maka ihe ndị a na-eji eme poison ahụ.

translations.source: The term bug is used by entomologists in a formal sense for this group of insects.
translations.reference: okwu bụ ahụhụ bụ ndị ọka mmụta ahụhụ n’ụzọ nwere ugwu maka òtù ụmụ ahụhụ a.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ ndị ọkà mmụta anụ ọhịa na-eji okwu "bug" iji akpọ otu a nke anụ ọhịa n'ụzọ ọbụrụ.

translations.source: This term derives from ancient familiarity with Bed-bugs, which are insects highly adapted to parasitize humans.
translations.reference: Okwu a sitere mmarita mgbe-ochie nke akpiri, bu chinchi di oke nko maka ibunye ndi mmadu oria.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị okwu a sitere n'oge ochie, n'oge ndị mmadụ nwere ọmụmụ nke ọma banyere anụ ọhịa, bụ anụ anụ nke nwere ọtụtụ atụmatụ iji bibie mmadụ.

translations.source: Both Assassin-bugs and Bed-bugs are nidicolous, adapted to living in nest or housing of their host.
translations.reference: Ma Assassin-bọg na Bed-bọg dị nidikolous, ha zuru oke ibi na nest maọbụ n'ụlọ nke hostu ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ahụ ndị "Assassin-bugs" na "Bed-bugs" abụọ ahụ bụ ụdị anụ ndị bi n'ime ụlọ ma ọ bụ n'ebe obibi nke onye ha na-ere ahụ. Ha adịworị nke ọma iji bi n'ime ụlọ ndị ahụ.

translations.source: Across the United States of America, there are approximately 400,000 known cases of Multiple Sclerosis (MS), leaving it as the leading neurological disease in younger and middle aged adults.
translations.reference: N'ofe mba Amerịka, e nwere ihe dị ka ọnụọgụ ọrịa Multiple Sclerosis (MS) 400,000 a maara amaara, nke na-eme ya isi ọrịa ụbụrụ na-emetụta ndị ntorọbịa na ndị okenye.
translations.hypothesis: N'ofebe ụmụ amaaka nke United States, e nwere ihe dị ka 400,000 akụkọ a maara nke ọrịa Multiple Sclerosis (MS), na-eme ka ọ bụrụ ọrịa neurological kachasị ewu n'etiti ndị tobala na ndị ọgbọ etiti.

translations.source: MS is a disease that affects the central nervous system, which is made up of the brain, the spinal cord and the optic nerve.
translations.reference: Mọltipụl Sklerosis bụ ọrịa na-emetụta sentral navọs sistem, nke gbakwunyere ụbụrụ, ogwurugwu azụ na ọptik nav.
translations.hypothesis: MS bụ ọrịa nke na-emetụta sistemụ ụbụrụ nke bụ nke oyiyi, nke gụnyere ụbụrụ, akwara mgbanwe, na eriri anya.

translations.source: Research has found that females are two times more likely to have MS then males.
translations.reference: Nnyocha achọpụtala na ụmụ nwanyị bụ ihe yikarịrị ugboro abụọ inwe MS karịa ụmụ nwoke.
translations.hypothesis: Nnyozi nke ama ama gosiri na ụmụ nwanyị nwere ohere abụọ karịa ụmụ nwoke ịmepụta ahụmahụ nke MS (Multiple Sclerosis).

translations.source: A couple may decide it is not in their best interest, or in the interest of their child, to raise a baby.
translations.reference: Di na nwunye nwere ike ikwekọrịta na ọ gaghị abara ha maọbụ nwa ha uru ịzụpụta nwa.
translations.hypothesis: Onye ma ọ bụ otu mmadụ nwere ike ikpe na ọ gaghị adị mma maka ha, ma ọ bụ maka nwa ha, ịgbatị nwa.

translations.source: These couples may choose to make an adoption plan for their baby.
translations.reference: Di na nwunye ndị a nwere ike ịhọrọ ime atụmatụ mkpọta nwa maka nwa ha.
translations.hypothesis: Anya ụmụ nwunye ndị a nwere ike ịhọrọ ịmepụta atụmatụ maka itinye nwa ha n'ọrụ nne na nna.

translations.source: In an adoption, the birth parents terminate their parental rights so that another couple may parent the child.
translations.reference: N’ime otu mkpọRọ nwa, nne na nna mụrụ nwa ahụ ga-akwụsị ikikere ha dị ka nne na nna ka di na nwunye ọ bụla nwere ike izulite nwa ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime usoro itinye nwa n'ọrụ, ndị nne na nna nke nwa ahụ na-akwụsị ikike ha dị ka ndị nne na nna, ka otu ezinụlọ ọzọ nwee ike ịrụ nwa ahụ.

translations.source: Science’s main goal is to figure out the way the world works through the scientific method. This method in fact guides most scientific research.
translations.reference: Isi ọrụ sayensị bụ ịchọpụta otu ụwa si arụ ọrụ site na usoro kesayensị. Usoro n'ezie na-edu ọtụtụ n'ime nnyocha kesayensị.
translations.hypothesis: Ebumnobi bụ ihe omume bụ nke eji anya anya na uche, ọ bụ ezigbo ihe omume nke na-elekwasị anya na ịmatakwu banyere ụwa anyị na otu ọ na-arụ ọrụ. Usoro a, n'ezie, na-eduzi ọtụtụ nyocha sayensị.

translations.source: It isn’t alone though, experimentation, and an experiment is a test that is used to eliminate one or more of the possible hypotheses, asking questions, and making observations also guide scientific research.
translations.reference: Ọ nọghị naanị ya n'ezie, eksperimenteshọn, ma otu eksperimenti bụ otu ule nke eji ewepụ otu haịpotesis kwere omume ma ọ bụ karịa, ịjụ ajụjụ gasị, na ime nyochata nakwa eduzi nnyocha sayensị.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ baghị na ọ nọ naanị ya, ọbụna ụfọdụ, ụfọdụ nyocha na-eme, ma nyocha bụ ule a na-eji iji wepu otu ma ọ bụ karịa ihe a na-achọpụta, ịjụ ajụjụ, na-elekwasị anya, na-eme uche dị iche iche, bụkwa ihe na-eduga nyocha sayensị.

translations.source: Naturalists and philosophers focused on classical texts and, in particular, on the Bible in Latin.
translations.reference: Ndị ọkammụta n'ụmụ ihe ekere na ndị ọkachamara gbadoro ụkwụ n'ederede oge gboo, ọkachasị, n'akwụkwọ nsọ e dere na Latin.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị ọkà mmụta okike na ndị ọkà ihe ọmụma kọwara banyere akwụkwọ akụkọ ochie, yana, karịsịa, banyere Akwụkwọ Ndị Mozu nke edere n'asụsụ Latịn.

translations.source: Accepted were Aristotle's views on all matters of science, including psychology.
translations.reference: A nabatara echiche Aristotle gbasara okwu sayensi niile ma mmuta akparamagwa ya bu psychology
translations.hypothesis: Anọọ m na-anabata echiche Aristotle gbasara ihe niile metụtara sayensị, gụnyere echiche ya banyere ọmụma mmadụ.

translations.source: As knowledge of Greek declined, the West found itself cut off from its Greek philosophical and scientific roots.
translations.reference: Dika amamihe nke ndi Greek biara gbatuwa, ndi odida anyanwu huta onwe ha ka ha na egbubiri site mgbara-ogwu ndi Greek ha nke ihe-omuma na nka.
translations.hypothesis: Ka ihe ọmụma gbasara asụsụ Griki na-ebelata, ndị Western nwetara ọtụtụ nsogbu, ebe ha kewara aka n'ime ụkpụrụ omume na sayensị nke ha si na Griki.

translations.source: Many observed rhythms in physiology and behavior often crucially depend on the presence of endogenous cycles and their production through biological clocks.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ usoro a na-ahụ na fisiọlọji na omume na-adabere ọtụtụ mgbe n'usoro ime ahụ na mmepụta ha site n'elekere nke ime ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ usoro na-agbanwe na ahụmmụnya na omume na-adịkarị, na-adaberekarị n'ọtụtụ ihe dị n'ime ahụ na usoro ndị ahụ na-eme, yana na usoro ndị a na-eme site na ihe ndị ndụ na-achị.

translations.source: Periodic rhythms, which are not simply responses to external periodic cues, have been documented for most living beings, including bacteria, fungi, plants, and animals.
translations.reference: Usoro kwa-oge kwa-oge, nke n'abụghị nzaghachi nye ntụpenye kwa-oge keezi, ka edeturula maka ọtụtụ ihe ndị dị ndụ , nke gụnyere nje bakterịa, fọngaị, akụmakụ na ụmụanụmanụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ndụ, gụnyere bacteria, fungi, osisi, na anụmanụ, nwere ụdị ije ije dị na ha nke na-abịa n'oge ọkacha, ọ bụghị naanị n'ihi ihe ndị sitere n'èzí na-adị na oge ọkacha.

translations.source: Biological clocks are self sustaining oscillators which will continue a period of free-running cycling even in the absence of external cues.
translations.reference: Elekere ime ahụ nwere usoro eje alọ nke na-arụ ọrụ n'onwe ya; usoro a ga na-aga n'ihu ma asịgodị rịị na onweghi ihe ọzọ metụtara ya.
translations.hypothesis: Eji ama ama na ọrụ ahụ bụ ngwaọrụ nke na-eme ka ihe gbanwee n'ime obere oge, na ọ na-arụ ọrụ nke onwe ya, ọ na-agafe oge nke ịgbanwe mgbe mgbe, ọbụlagodi na enweghị ihe ndị sitere n'èzí na-akpali ya.

translations.source: The Hershey and Chase experiment was one of the leading suggestions that DNA was a genetic material.
translations.reference: Nwale Hershey na Chase so na otu aro no na isi siri na DNA wubu otu mkpụrụ ndụ ihe nketa.
translations.hypothesis: Nnyocha nke Hershey na Chase bụ otu n'ime ihe ngosi kacha akọwapụta na DNA bụ ihe omume nke nchọpụta nke ụlọ.

translations.source: Hershey and Chase used phages, or viruses, to implant their own DNA into a bacterium.
translations.reference: Hershey na Chase jiri ụmụ feeji, ma ọ bụ ụmụ nje, iji kụnye DNA nke ha n'ime otu nje bakterịọm.
translations.hypothesis: Hershey na Chase jiri akụkọ, ma ọ bụ virus, iji tinye DNA ha n'ime onye ndụ ọgwụgwụ.

translations.source: They did two experiments marking either the DNA in the phage with a radioactive phosphorus or the protein of the phage with radioactive sulfur.
translations.reference: Ha mere nnwale abụọ ebe ha ji rediyoaktiv fosforọs kaa akara na DNA nọ na fej maọbụ jiri rediyoaktiv sọlfọ kaa akara na protin nọ na fej.
translations.hypothesis: Ha merekwa uzo abụọ iji nyochaa, n'otu n'ime ha, ha jiri phosphorus na-enwu na-acha DNA nke phage ahụ agba, ebe n'otu ọzọ, ha jiri sulfur na-enwu na-acha protein nke phage ahụ agba.

translations.source: Mutations can have a variety of different effects depending on the type of mutation, the significance of the piece of genetic material affected and whether the cells affected are germ-line cells.
translations.reference: Mgbanwe ọjọọ nwere ike inwe ọtụtụ mmetụta dị iche iche na ndabere na ụdị mgbanwe ọjọọ ọ bụ, abamuru nke otu iberibe nke ihe mkpụrụ ndụ ihe nketa o metụtara na ma ọ bụrụ na ụmụ mkpụrụ ndụ o metụtara bụ ụmụ mkpụrụ ndụ geem-laịnụ.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbanwe nwere ike inwe ọtụtụ ụdị mmetụta dị iche iche, dabere na ụdị mgbanwe ahụ, mkpa nke akụkụ nke akụrụngwa nke akụ na-emetụta, na ma ozi ndị metụtara bụ ozi nke sel ndị na-ebipụta.

translations.source: Only mutations in germ-line cells can be passed on to children, while mutations elsewhere can cause cell-death or cancer.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ nanị mgbanwe na mkpụrụ ndụ jem-laịn ka a ga-enyefe ụmụaka, ebe mgbanwe n’ebe ndị ọzọ nwere ike ibute ọnwụ nke mkpụrụ ndụ maọbụ ọrịa kansa.
translations.hypothesis: Nanị mgbanwe nke na-eme na sel ndị na-ebute ụmụ bụ nke nwere ike ịgafe n'aka ụmụ, ebe mgbanwe ndị ọzọ nwere ike ibute ọnwụ nke sel ma ọ bụ ọrịa kansa.

translations.source: Nature-based tourism attracts people interested in visiting natural areas for the purpose of enjoying the scenery, including plant and animal wildlife.
translations.reference: Njem-nlere anya nke dabere na udidi na enweta uche ndi mmadu ndi nwere mmasi izute ebe di na udidi ha maka ihi ikpori-ndu na udi ebe, gunyekwara akumaku anumanu anu-ohia.
translations.hypothesis: Ahụmahụ anya nke nwere isi na akụ na ụlọ ọrụ anya na-adọta ndị mmadụ bụ ndị nwere mmasị ịga na mpaghara okirikiri iji nọrọ na-enwe mmasị na ihe ndị dị n'ime ya, gụnyere osisi na anụmanụ.

translations.source: Examples of on-site activities include hunting, fishing, photography, bird watching, and visiting parks and studying information about the ecosystem.
translations.reference: Ụfọdụ ihe omume enwere ike ime ma anọrọ ya gụnyere ịchụ nta, ịkụ azụ, ise foto, ilele nnụnụ, na ịga n'ogige gụọ maka ihe ndị dị ndụ na gburugburu ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ ihe omume ndị a pụrụ ịme n'ebe ahụ gụnyere ịgba egwu, ịgba azụ, ị chụpu foto, ilekọta anụ ọhịa, na ịgọzi parkị na ịmụta gbasara usoro echiche nke ebe ahụ.

translations.source: An example is visiting, photographing, and learning about organgatuangs in Borneo.
translations.reference: Otu ọmụmaatụ bụ ileta, ise fòto, na ịmụta gbasara na ụmụ ọrangụtanụ nọ n'ime Bọnioo.
translations.hypothesis: Ụzọ otu bụ ịgba ụta, ị chụpu foto, na ịmụta banyere orugbo ndị dị na Borneo.

translations.source: Every morning, people leave small country towns in cars to go their workplace and are passed by others whose work destination is the place they have just left.
translations.reference: Ututu o bula, ndi mmadu n'ahapu obere obodo n'ugbo ala were gawa ulo oru ha ma ndi ozo n'agbafe ha ndi ulo oru ha di n'ebe ha si puta.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe ọdịnihu, ndị mmadụ na-apụ na obere obere obodo site na ọkwọ ụlọ iji gaa ebe ha na-arụ ọrụ, ma ndị ọzọ na-aga n'ụzọ dị iche, ebe ha na-arụ ọrụ bụ ebe ndị ahụ si bịa.

translations.source: In this dynamic transport shuttle everyone is somehow connected with, and supporting, a transport system based on private cars.
translations.reference: N'ime ụgbọ mgbagharị kenjem a na-agbanwegharị agbanwe onye ọ bụla si n'otuọdịla metụta ya, ma na-akwado, otu sistemụ njem dabere na ụgbọala nkeonwe.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime usoro njem a na-agbanwe mgbe niile, onye ọ bụla nwere otu nhọrọ ma jikọrọ na, na-akwalite, usoro njem nke dabere na ndị ụlọ ọrụ obodo.

translations.source: Science now indicates that this massive carbon economy has dislodged the biosphere from one of its stable states that has supported human evolution for the past two million years.
translations.reference: Sayensị na-egosi ugbu a na ekọnọmi a ji oke kabọn arụ ọrụ akupụla mkpokọta ihe ndụ niile nọ n'ụwa site n'otu n'ime ọnọdụ nkwụsi ike ya nke kwadogoro obibi ndụ mmadụ n'afọ nde abụọ gara aga.
translations.hypothesis: Ugbu a, sayensị na-egosi na akụ ụlọ ọrụ nke carbon a dị ukwuu emeela ka usoro ndụ na ụwa (biosphere) gbanara site n'otu n'ime ụdị ebe ọ nọrọ nke amalitela ịkwado mmepe mmadụ kemgbe afọ abụọ milioni gara aga.

translations.source: Everyone participates in society and uses transportation systems. Almost everyone complains about transportation systems.
translations.reference: Onye ọ bụla na-esonye n'ime ọha mmadụ ma na-eji ụmụ sistemụ njem. Ọ fọrọ obere ka ọ bụrụ onye niile na eme mkpesa gbasara ụmụ sistemụ njem.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na onye ọ bụla nọ na obodo, ọ na-eme otú ọ si eme na obodo ahụ, ọ na-eji ụzọ njem. Karịsịrị ndị mmadụ na-akparịta ụzọ njem.

translations.source: In developed countries you seldom hear similar levels of complaints about water quality or bridges falling down.
translations.reference: N'ime ụmụ mba mepere emepe ọ ga-ara ahụ tupu ị nụ larịị mkpesa ndị yirinụ gbasara ogo mmiri ma ọ bụ ụmụ akwa mmiri na-ada n'ala.
translations.hypothesis: Na mba ndị nwere mmepe, ọ dịkarịa ọma na ịghọta ụdị mkpọrọ ahụike ma ọ bụ akụkọ banyere ụzọ dị n'ihe gbasịrị.

translations.source: Why do transportation systems engender such complaints, why do they fail on a daily basis? Are transportation engineers just incompetent? Or is something more fundamental going on?
translations.reference: Gịnị mere sistemụ njem ji akpata ụdịrị ụmụ mkpesa ahụ, gịmị mere ha ji ada kwa ụbọchị? Ọ bụ na ndị injinịa njem amaghị arụ ọrụ ha nke ọma? Ma ọ bụ ihe ọzọ si n'isi na-eme?
translations.hypothesis: Kedu ihe mere ụzọ njem na-ebute ụfụfụ dị otú a, kedu ihe mere ha na-enwe nsogbu kwa ụbọchị? Ọ bụ na ndị injinịa ụzọ njem adịghị maazi? Ma ọ bụ na enwere ihe ọzọ dị mkpa na-eme?

translations.source: Traffic Flow is the study of the movement of individual drivers and vehicles between two points and the interactions they make with one another.
translations.reference: Ọwụwụ trafik bụ ọmụmụ nke ngagharị nke onye ọkwụ ụgbọ ọ bụla na ụgbọ ha n'etiti akara abụọ na mmekọrịta ha na-eme n'etiti onwe ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ọkwa ụgbọ ala bụ nyocha nke usoro ije ije nke ụgbọ ala na ndị na-anya ụgbọ ala n'etiti abụọ ebe, na otú ha si eme mmekọrịta n'etiti ha.

translations.source: Unfortunately, studying traffic flow is difficult because driver behavior cannot be predicted with one-hundred percent certainty.
translations.reference: Na mwute, ịmụ maka otu okporo njem si aga siri maka na e nweghi ike ikwu kpọm n'ọgụ otu narị pasentị ụdị omume ọkwọ ụgbọ nwere ike ime.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dị nwute, ọ bụ eziokwu na ịmụta maka ụzọ mmadụ na-aga bụ ihe siri ike, n'ihi na a nweghị ike ịtọọ ọdịdị omume ndị na-anya ụgbọ ala n'ụzọ zuru oke na enweghị enweghị nsogbu.

translations.source: Fortunately, drivers tend to behave within a reasonably consistent range; thus, traffic streams tend to have some reasonable consistency and can be roughly represented mathematically.
translations.reference: Ọ dabara nke ọma na ndị na-anya ụgbọ ala nwere usoro omume na-adịgide; ya mere, ụzọ njem moto anaghị agbanwecha agbanwe ma bụrụkwa ihe enwere ike iji eserese aritmetik gosipụta.
translations.hypothesis: N'eleghị, ndị na-anya ụgbọ ala na-adịkarị ka ha na-eme ihe n'ụzọ dị iche iche, mana ọ bụghị nke zuru oke; ya mere, ọtụtụ ụzọ ọkwụ ụgbọ ala na-adịkarị ka ha si eme ihe n'ụzọ dị iche iche, ma ọ bụghị nke zuru oke, ma ha nwekwara ike ịbụ ihe dị mma iji atụpụta ha site na usoro ugha.

translations.source: To better represent traffic flow, relationships have been established between the three main characteristics: (1) flow, (2) density, and (3) velocity.
translations.reference: Iji ka mma na-anọchi anya ije nke okporo ụzọ, E mebewo mmekọrịta n'etiti isi njirimara atọ ahụ: (1) eruba, (2) njupụta, na (3) ike ọsọ.
translations.hypothesis: Iji gosipụta usoro njem ụgbọ ala nke ọma, e mepụtara njikọ dị n'etiti atọ ihe ndị bụ isi: (1) usoro njem, (2) ọnụ ọgụgụ, na (3) ọsọ.

translations.source: These relationships help in planning, design, and operations of roadway facilities.
translations.reference: Mmetụta ndị a na-enyere aka n’ime atụmatụ, ncheremee, na arụmọrụ nke akụrụngwa okporo ụzọ ụgbọ ígwè.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ mmekọrịta ndị a na-enyere aka n'ihe gbasara atụmatụ, nrụpụta, na ọrụ ụlọ ọrụ ụzọ okporo ụzọ.

translations.source: Insects were the first animals to take to the air. Their ability to fly helped them evade enemies more easily and find food and mates more efficiently.
translations.reference: Ụmụ ahụhụ bụ ụmụ anụmanụ buru ụzọ fee n'elu. Ike ha n'ife efe nyere ha aka ịgbanaha ndị iro n'ụzọ kara dị mfe ma ịchọtakwa nri na ndị otu mmekọ n'ụzọ dị werewere.
translations.hypothesis: Anụ ọfụrụ bụ ụdị anụmanụ mbụ bụ ndị malitere igba elu. Onye ọrụ ha ịnya elu nyere ha ohere ịgbapụ ndị na-achọ igwu ha ọsọ, ọkachamaaka, wee mee ka ha chọpụta nri na ndị enyere ha aka dị mfe.

translations.source: Most insects have the advantage of being able to fold their wings back along the body.
translations.reference: Ihe karịrị ọtụtụ n’ime ụmụ ahụhụ nwere uru nke inwe ike ịpịa nku ha gaa n’ahụ ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ anụ ọhịa nwere uru nke inwe ike ịgbatị akụkụ ha azụ, n'akụkụ ahụ ha.

translations.source: This gives them a wider range of small places to hide from predators.
translations.reference: Nke a na-eme ka ha nwee ọtụtụ ebe izonarị ndị na-eri ha.
translations.hypothesis: Nke a na-enye ha ohere ịgbasa n'ọtụtụ ebe obere ebe ebe ha ga-esi chebe onwe ha site n'anya mmiri.

translations.source: Today, the only insects that cannot fold back their wings are dragon flies and mayflies.
translations.reference: Ubochi taa, nani ogugu nwere ike ikpalaga nku ya azu bu ogugu drago na ogugu may.
translations.hypothesis: Taa, ọtụtụ anụ ọhịa na-adịghị agba ụkwụ ha azụ bụ naanị anụ ọhịa na-acha aja aja na anụ ọhịa na-adịkarị na mmiri.

translations.source: Thousands of years ago, a man called Aristarchus said that the Solar System moved around the Sun.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ puku afọ gara aga, otu nwoke a kpọrọ Aristarchus kwuru si na Usoro Mbara Igwe nọ na-agagharị gburugburu Anyanwụ.
translations.hypothesis: Eme ọtụtụ puku afọ gara, otu nwoke nke aha ya bụ Aristarchus kwuru na sistemụ anyanwụ na-agba gburugburu anyanwụ.

translations.source: Some people thought he was right but many people believed the opposite; that the Solar System moved around the Earth, including the Sun (and even the other stars).
translations.reference: Ufodu ndi mmadu chere na ihe o na-ekwu bu eziokwu mana ufodu ekweghi; na mbara igwe na-agba uwa okirikiri ma anyanwu(ma kwa kpakpando ndi ozo)
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ mmadụ chere na ọ dị n'ezi, mana ọtụtụ mmadụ kwenyere ihe dị iche; na ụwa ahụ na-agba gburugburu ụwa, gụnyere anyanwụ (na ọbụna ndị ọkụdụ ndị ọzọ).

translations.source: This seems sensible, because the Earth doesn't feel as if it's moving, does it?
translations.reference: Nke a yiri ezi uche, n’ihi na ọ naghị emetụta ka ụwa ọ na-agagharị agagharị, ọ na-emetụta?
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dị mma, n'ihi na anya anyị adịghị ahụ ụzọ ụwa na-agba, ọ bụ ya?

translations.source: The Amazon River is the second longest and the biggest river on Earth. It carries more than 8 times as much water as the second biggest river.
translations.reference: Osimiri Amazọn ahụ bụ nke abụọ kachasị ogologo na osimiri kachasị n’ibu n’ụwa. Ọ na-ebu ihe karịrị nha mmiri ugboro asatọ dị ka osimiri nke abụọ kachasị ibu.
translations.hypothesis: Osisi mmiri Amazon bụ osisi mmiri nke abụọ kacha ogologo na kacha ukwuu n'ụwa. Ọ na-ebu mmiri karịa osisi mmiri ọzọ kacha ukwuu, karịa okpukpu asatọ.

translations.source: The Amazon is also the widest river on Earth, at times six miles wide.
translations.reference: Amazọn bụkwa osimiri kachasị saa mbara n'ụwa, mgbe ụfọdụ ọ na-eru maịlụ isii.
translations.hypothesis: Amazon bụkwa osimiri kacha akọrọ n'ụwa, na mgbe ụfọdụ ọ na-abụkarị kilomita ise n'agba.

translations.source: A full 20 percent of the water that pours out of the planet's rivers into the oceans comes from the Amazon.
translations.reference: Pasentị mmmiri 20 zuru oke nke na-awụpụta site na osimiri ụwa ga na-abanye n'ime oke osimiri ga si n'Amazọn abịa.
translations.hypothesis: Ọkara nke abụọ na ise (20%) nke mmiri nke na-agbaze site na osimiri ndị dị n'ụwa anyị na-abanye n'oké osimiri, si na osimiri Amazon.

translations.source: The main Amazon River is 6,387 km (3,980 miles). It collects water from thousands of smaller rivers.
translations.reference: Isi osimiri Amazọnụ dị km 6,387 (maịlị 3,980). Ọ na-ewetaju mmiri site n’ọtụtụ puku osimiri ndị kara di obere.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdọ mmiri Amazon bụ mmiri dị ukwuu, n'agbanyeghị na ọ nwere kilomita 6,387 (maịlụ 3,980). Ọ na-azụ mmiri site na ọtụtụ mmiri ndị nta.

translations.source: Although pyramid-building in stone continued until the end of the Old Kingdom, the pyramids of Giza were never surpassed in their size and the technical excellence of their construction.
translations.reference: Agbanyeghị na ọrụrụ-piramidi n’okwute gara n’ihu ruo na njedebe nke Alaeze Ochie, ụmụ piramidi nke Giza bụ ndị agafeghị ma ọlị na nha ha na ima mma nka na ụzụ nke ọrụrụ ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na ịmepụta ụlọ elu n'ime ígwè enweghị mmechi ruo mgbe ọwụwa anọ nke Obodo Ochie, ụlọ elu nke Giza adịghịkarịrị ụlọ elu ọzọ n'ụsọ osimiri na ọma nke ụzọ ha si emepụta.

translations.source: New Kingdom ancient Egyptians marvelled at their predecessors monuments, which were then well over a thousand year old.
translations.reference: O juru ndị Niu Kịngdọm Ijipt mgbe ochie anya ihe ncheta ndị bu ha ụzọ, nke gaferela otu puku afọ mgbe ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị e guzoro ọchịchị ọhụrụ nke ndị Egypt ochie nwere ekele dị ha maka ụlọ ọrụ ndị e guzobere tupu ha, bụ ndị dịkarịrị ọtụtụ puku afọ.

translations.source: Vatican City's population is around 800. It is the smallest independent country in the world and the country with the lowest population.
translations.reference: Onu ogugu ndi mmadu obodo Vatican di nari 800. O bu obodo kacha nta n’uwa n’uwa n’uwa na obodo n’ogbe ndi kacha pere mpe.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdụ ụlọ obodo Vatican bụ ihe dị ka 800. Ọ bụ obodo nke n'onwe ya kacha nta n'ụwa, yana obodo nwere ọdụ mmadụ kacha nta.

translations.source: Vatican City uses Italian in its legislation and official communications.
translations.reference: Obodo Vatican na-eji asụsụ Italian na iwu na ukara nkwukọrịta ya.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo Vatican na-ejiasụ Italian na iwu akụkọ na ozi gọọmentị ya.

translations.source: Italian is also the everyday language used by most of those who work in the state while Latin is often used in religious ceremonies.
translations.reference: Asụsụ Itali ka ọtụtụ ndị na-arụ ọrụ na steeti na-asụkwa kwa ụbọchị ebe a na-asụkarị Latin n’emume ndị ụka ga.
translations.hypothesis:
Igbo:

Italiano bụkwa asụsụ a na-eji kwa ụbọchị site n'ọtụtụ ndị na-arụ ọrụ na steeti ahụ, ebe Latin na-ejikarị na usoro ọru Igbo.

translations.source: All citizens of Vatican City are Roman Catholic.
translations.reference: Ndị obodo niile nke Obodo Vatican bụ Roman Katọlik.
translations.hypothesis: Nile anyị niile nke obodo Vatican bụ ndị na-eso ụzọ Katọlik Roma.

translations.source: People have known about basic chemical elements such as gold, silver, and copper from antiquity, as these can all be discovered in nature in native form and are relatively simple to mine with primitive tools.
translations.reference: Ndị mmadụ amarala maka isi kemịkalụ njìmebe ndị dị ka ọlaedo, ọlaọcha, ọla kọpa sitere na oge ochie, dị ka enwere ike ịchọpụta ihe ndị a n’ụwa n’ụdị mbupụtaụwa ma dịrị mfe igwupụta n’iji ngwaọrụ ndị mgbe ochie.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ndị amaala maara banyere ihe ndị kemịta dị mkpa, dị ka ọla edo, ọla ọla, na akara, kemgbe oge ochie, n'ihi na ihe ndị a niile pụrụ ịmịpụta n'ime okike n'ụdị ha kacha mma, ọ bụkwa ihe dị mfe ịkpọọ ha site na iji ngwaọrụ dị mfe.

translations.source: Aristotle, a philosopher, theorised that everything is made up of a mixture of one or more of four elements. They were earth, water, air, and fire.
translations.reference: Aristotle, bụ onye ọka ihe ọmụma, ekwuola na tiori na ihe niile bụ mgwọkọta njimebe otu ma ọ bụ karịa mejupụtara ya. Ha wụbụ aja, mmiri, ikuku, na ọkụ.
translations.hypothesis: Aristotle, onye ọkà mmụta, kwuru na ihe niile nwere ihe ndị dị iche iche, nke bụ otu ma ọ bụ karịa n'ime ihe anọ. Ihe ndị ahụ bụ ala, mmiri, ikuku, na ọkụ.

translations.source: This was more like the four states of matter (in the same order): solid, liquid, gas, and plasma, though he also theorised that they change into new substances to form what we see.
translations.reference: Nke a dị kara yiri ọnọdụ anọ nke mata (n’usoro ahụ kwa): nsiriike, mmiri mmiri, ikuku, na plasma, agbanyeghị na o nyere tiori na ha na-agbanwe ghụọ umi ọhụrụ iji mepụta ihe anyị na-ahụ anya.
translations.hypothesis: Nke a yiri ihe ndị a anọ bụ nke dị iche iche (n'usoro ahụ): ihe siri ike, mmiri, ikuku, na plasma, ọ bụ ezie na ọ makwara na ha na-agbanwe ịbụ ihe ọhụrụ iji mee ihe anyị na-ahụ.

translations.source: Alloys are basically a mixture of two or more metals. Don't forget that there are many elements on the periodic table.
translations.reference: Ụmụ alọị bụgodu mwurikọta ígwè abụọ ma ọ bụ karịa. Echefula na e nwere ọtụtụ njìmebe nọ na tebụlụ pirịọdik.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ahụ bụ n'ọtụtụ iche, ọ bụ nhazi nke otu ma ọ bụ karịa akpụkpọ anụ. Echere m na ị na-atụgharị uche na e nwere ọtụtụ ihe na tebụl nke ihe ndị a na-ahụ.

translations.source: Elements like calcium and potassium are considered metals. Of course, there are also metals like silver and gold.
translations.reference: Ihe ndị dị ka kalsium na potassium bụ igwe. Ee, enwekwara igwe ndị ọzọ dịka ọla ọcha na ọla edo.
translations.hypothesis: Ihe ndị dị ka calcium na potassium a na-akpọkarị "ihe oriri." Ọ bụ ezie na, enwerekwa ihe oriri ndị ọzọ, dị ka silver na gold.

translations.source: You can also have alloys that include small amounts of non-metallic elements like carbon.
translations.reference: I nwekwara ike nwee allọyi nke gụnyere nwa-obere njieme gasị nke enweghị metalik dịka cabọn.
translations.hypothesis: Ị nwekwara ike inwe ihe ndị a na-ejikọta ọnụ, nke nwere obere ọrụ nke ihe ndị na-adịghị eme gị gị, dịka carbon.

translations.source: Everything in the Universe is made of matter. All matter is made of tiny particles called atoms.
translations.reference: Ihe niile dị na elu ụwa a nwere mata. Mata niile bụ njikọ ọtụtụ obere ihe a na-akpọ atọm.
translations.hypothesis: Nkwụsi, ihe niile dị n'ụwa niile emeere site n'ihe. Ihe niile emeere site n'ihe ndị dị obere nke a na-akpọ atom.

translations.source: Atoms are so incredibly tiny that trillions of them could fit into the period at the end of this sentence.
translations.reference: Atọm pere nnọọ mpe ruo na puku ijeri ga-abali n'ime akara kpọm nọ na ngwụcha okwu a.
translations.hypothesis: Atọmụ bụ nnukwu obere ihe, na ọtụtụ narị puku nke ha nwere ike ịbanye n'ime akara nke na-agwụ akwụkwọ a.

translations.source: Thus, the pencil was a good friend to many people when it came out.
translations.reference: Ya mere, pensụl ahụ wụbụ ezigbo enyị nye ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ mgbe ọ pụtara.
translations.hypothesis: Ya mere, penisil ahụ bụ enyi dị mma maka ọtụtụ ndị mgbe ọ bịara n'ụwa.

translations.source: Sadly, as newer methods of writing have emerged, the pencil has been relegated to lesser status and uses.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ ihe mwute na ka ụzọ ọhụrụ e si ede ihe na-apụta, 'ọkwa', mkpịsịodee ọkpọọ bụzi ihe a tụlagara n'akụkụ anaghịzikwa eji ya ede ihe mgbe niile.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dị njọ, ebe usoro ndị ọhụrụ nke ide edere na-apụta, pencil ahụ emeela ka ọ bụrụ ihe dị nta na ọ na-eji ya eme ihe ole na ole.

translations.source: People now write messages on computer screens, never having to come close to a sharpener.
translations.reference: Ndị mmadụ na-edezi ozi na ihuenyo kọmputa gasị, o nweghị mgbe ha na-enwe ịbịaru nso na otu ọmụ nkọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ugbu a, ndị mmadụ na-ede ozi na ihu igwe kọmputa, na ha adịghị mkpa ịbịa nso igwe na-acha akwụkwọ.

translations.source: One can only wonder what the keyboard will become when something newer comes along.
translations.reference: Mmadụ ga na-atụ naanị n’uche ihe kiibọọdụ ga-abụzi mgbe ihe kara dị ọhụrụ bịaziri.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dị mma naanị ịche echiche maka ihe ga-esi na keyboard eme mgbe otu ihe ọhụrụ bịara.

translations.source: The fission bomb works on the principle that it takes energy to put together a nucleus with many protons and neutrons.
translations.reference: Bọmbụ fishọn ahụ na-arụ ọrụ n’iwu na ọ na ewere ike ijikọta otu nuclus ya na ọtụtụ protọnụ na nutrọnụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọnụ ahụ nke ọgụ nke fission na-arụ ọrụ n'igbochi na ọ dị mkpa iji enweghị ike iji jikọọ ọnụ ụlọ nke nwere ọtụtụ proton na neutron.

translations.source: Sort of like rolling a heavy cart up a hill. Splitting the nucleus up again then releases some of that energy.
translations.reference: Dika ibinggasi ugbo-ala nke di elu.Nkewa dị na etiti na elụ wee wepụta ike ụfọdụ.
translations.hypothesis: Dị ka ị na-agba obere ụgbọ mmiri dị arọ elu n'elu nkuku. Mgbe ị na-ebunye isi nke atom ahụ ọzọ, ọ na-ebipụta ụfọdụ nke ahụ ike.

translations.source: Some atoms have unstable nuclei which means that they tend to break apart with little or no nudging.
translations.reference: Ụfọdụ atọm nwere nukei na-anọsighị ike nke pụtara na ha na-agbajikarị n'iji obere ma ọ bụ n'enweghị akwamaka.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ atom nwere mkpakọrịta dị iche na-adịghị kwụsie ike, nke pụtara na ha na-adịkarị na-ebili tupu ha, ọbụlagodi enweghị mmetụta dị nta.

translations.source: The surface of the Moon is made of rocks and dust. The outer layer of the Moon is called the crust.
translations.reference: Elu ọnwa bụ ụmụ okwute na ájá mejupụtara ya. Mkpuchi mpụga ọnwa ka a na-akpọ krọstụ.
translations.hypothesis: Udu nke Ọkụ bụ nke e ji akwụkwọ na ihe ndụrụ. Akụkụ nke ọzọ nke Ọkụ ahụ na-akpọ ya "ọkwụ."

translations.source: The crust is about 70 km thick on the near side and 100 km thick on the far side.
translations.reference: Crọstụ ahụ dị ihe dị ka km70 n'ịgba agba n'akụkụ ya dị nso na km100 n'ịgba ịgba n'akụkụ ya tere anya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọkpụrụkpụ ahụ dị n'okporo nke nso bụ ihe dị ka kilomita 70, ebe ọkpụrụkpụ ahụ dị n'okporo nke anya bụ ihe dị ka kilomita 100.

translations.source: It is thinner under the maria and thicker under the highlands.
translations.reference: Ọ kara taa ahụ n'okpuru marịa ma kara gbaa agba n'okpuru ụmụ ala ugwu ugwu ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dịkarịrị elu n'okpuru obodo Maria, ma ọ dị buru n'okpuru mpaghara dị elu.

translations.source: There may be more maria on the near side because the crust is thinner. It was easier for lava to rise up to the surface.
translations.reference: E nwere ike nwekwuo marịa ọzọ n'akụkụ ya dị nso n'ihi na krọstụ ya kara taa ahụ. Ọ kara dịrị mfe maka lava ịrịgote n'elu ya ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ nwere ike ịbụ na enwere ọtụtụ "maria" na akụkụ ahụ nso n'ihi na akpụkpọ ahụ dị ntakịrị. Ọ dịkwara mfe maka lava ịgbatị elu ruo ọdịdị.

translations.source: Content theories are centered on finding what makes people tick or appeals to them.
translations.reference: Tiori ndịnà bụ ndị a gbadoro anya ha ịchọta ihe na-eme ndị mmadụ kpaa agwa ha na-akpa ma ọ bụ ihe na-amasị ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ụdị echiche gbasara ọdịmma na-elekwasị anya na ịchọta ihe na-eme ka ndị mmadụ ji nwayọọ ma ọ bụ ihe na-adọta ha.

translations.source: These theories suggest that people have certain needs and/or desires which have been internalized as they mature to adulthood.
translations.reference: Tiori ndị a na-ekwu na ndị mmadụ nwere mkpa ụfọdụ na/ma ọ bụ ọchịchọ nke ndị e chechala ma tinye n'uche dị ka ha na-etozuru ntorọbịa.
translations.hypothesis: Nsogbu ndị a na-egosi na ndị mmadụ nwere ụfọdụ mkpa na/ma ọ bụ ọnụnọ uche nke ha na-etolite n'ime ha mgbe ha na-eto ruo mgbe ha bụ ndị ọrịa.

translations.source: These theories look at what it is about certain people that make them want the things that they do and what things in their environment will make them do or not do certain things.
translations.reference: Tiori ndị a na-eleba anya n'ihe gbasara ụfọdụ ndị mmadụ nke kpatara ha ji achọ ihe ndị ha chọrọ na kedu ụmụ ihe nọ na gburugburu ebe obibi ha ga-eme ha mee ma ọ bụ emela ụfọdụ ihe.
translations.hypothesis: Nsọmụzi ndị a na-ele anya na ihe ndị mere ka ụfọdụ mmadụ chọọ ihe ha chọrọ, na ihe ndị dị n'ime gburugburu ha nke nwere ike ime ka ha mee ihe ma ọ bụ meeghị ihe ụfọdụ.

translations.source: Two popular content theories are Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs Theory and Hertzberg's Two Factor Theory.
translations.reference: Uzo-echiche ihe-di_n’ime abuo ama ama bu uzo-echiche ogogo nke mkpa nke Maslow na uzo-echiche ihe abuo kpatara nke Hertzberg.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ ihe atụ nke ihe omume bụ nke Maslow, bụ "Usoro Ọchịchọ," na nke Hertzberg, bụ "Usoro Abụọ Ihe Ọdịmma."

translations.source: Generally speaking, two behaviors can emerge as managers begin to lead their former peers. One end of the spectrum is trying to remain “one of the guys” (or gals).
translations.reference: Ikwu n'izugbe, akparamaagwa abụọ nwere ike ịpụta dịka ndị  nlekọta na-amalite idu ndị ọgbọ ha ochie. Otu mpaghara n'echiche ahụ bụ "ịgbalị ịnọrọ dịka otu n'ime ụmụokorọbịa" (maọbụ ụmụagbọghọbịa).
translations.hypothesis: N'aka nke ọzọ, mgbe ndị isi malitere ịzi otu ndị ọkacha mmasị ha, ụdị omume abụọ nwere ike pụta. Otú ọ dị, otu akụkụ nke usoro ahụ bụ ịgbalị ịga n'ihu dị ka "otú ndị ọzọ si dị" (ma ọ bụ ndị nwanyị).

translations.source: This type of manager has difficulty making unpopular decisions, performing disciplinary action, performance evaluations, assigning responsibility, and holding people accountable.
translations.reference: Ụdịrị onye njikwa a nwere ihe isi ike ime mkpebi ndị amasịghị, ime omume ndị ịdọ aka na ntị, ụmụ nnyocha arụmọrụ, ikenye ibu ọrụ, na ijide ndị mmadụ maka ịza ajụjụ nke ọrụ ha.
