translations.hypothesis: Onye njikwa a nwere nsogbu ime mkpebi ndị na-adịghị amasị ndị mmadụ, ịgba ndị ọrụ ụgwọ, inyocha ọrụ ha, itinye ọrụ n'aka ndị ọrụ, na-eme ka ndị mmadụ zuru oke ọrụ ha.

translations.source: At the other end of the spectrum, one morphs into an unrecognizable individual that feels he or she must change everything the team has been doing and make it their own.
translations.reference: Na njedebe ọzọ nke ụdị ahụ, otu onye ahụ ga-aghọ wụrụ mmadụ a na agali amata nke na- eche na ọ ga-agbanwerịrị ihe niile otu ahụ na- eme ma mee ka ọ bụrụ nke ha.
translations.hypothesis: N'akụkụ nke ọzọ, otu onye nwere ike ịgbanwe gaa bụrụ onye dị iche nke na-enwe mmetụta na ọ ga-achọ ịgbanwe ihe niile otu ahụike ahụ na-eme, wee mee ya dị ka ihe nke ya.

translations.source: After all, the leader is ultimately responsible for the success and failure of the team.
translations.reference: Kaosiladị, onye ndu ahụ bụ ya ka ọ dịịrị n'ikpeazụ ịhụ maka ọdịmma na ọdịda nke òtù ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: N'aka nke ọzọ, onyeisi ahụ bụ onye nwere ọrụ dị ukwuu n'ihe gbasara uru na mmerụ nke otu ahụ.

translations.source: This behavior oftentimes results in rifts between the leaders and the rest of the team.
translations.reference: Omume a ọtụtụ mgbe na adapụta n'esemokwu n'etiti ndị isi na ndị òtù ndị ọzọ fọdụrụnụ.
translations.hypothesis: A mụ, ọtụtụ oge, a na-ahụ ụdị ihe omume a na-ebute ụkọ na-etiti ndị isi na ndị ọzọ n'otu otu ahụ.

translations.source: Virtual teams are held to the same standards of excellence as conventional teams, but there are subtle differences.
translations.reference: A na-ebugowe otu egwuregwu ndị a na-ejighi n'aka n'otu ụdị ụkpụrụ mmapụrụiche dịka otu egwuregwu ndị nke a ma ama, mana ndịiche dị n'etiti ha nke n'eweghi anya.
translations.hypothesis: Otu ndị na-arụ ọrụ n'ịntanetị na-adị otu otu ndị ọrụ ndị ọzọ, mana enwere ọdịiche dị nta.

translations.source: Virtual team members often function as the point of contact for their immediate physical group.
translations.reference: Ndịòtù òtù kedịnuche na-arụkarị ọrụ dị ka ebe nzute mbụ maka òtù ozugbo ha keanahụanya.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị otu nwere ọrụ n'ịntanetị na-adịkarị ka ha bụ ndị na-echetara ndị otu ha n'ụlọ.

translations.source: They often have more autonomy than conventional team members as their teams may meet according to varying time zones which may not be understood by their local management.
translations.reference: Ha na enwekwuru ikike ichoro onwe ha karia ndiotu otu ha na ha dika otu ha nwere ike izute na-ndabere n’oge na-adi iche iche nke obodo ha nwere ike njikwa obodo ha agaghi aghota ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ha na-enwekarị ikike ọrụ karịa ndị otu ndị ọzọ, n'ihi na otu ha nwere ike ịbụ ndị na-ezumara n'oge dị iche iche, nke ndị njikwa ha nọrọ na ebe ha bi ekwepụghị ya.

translations.source: The presence of a true “invisible team” (Larson and LaFasto, 1989, p109) is also a unique component of a virtual team.
translations.reference: Ọnụnọ nke otu "òtù anaghị ahụ anya" n'ezie (Larson na LaFasto, 1989, p109) bụkwa otu ǹsòmebe pụrụ iche nke otu òtù kendịnuche.
translations.hypothesis: Ọnụnọ otu "ezi ndị na-arụ ọrụ n'eziokwu" (Larson na LaFasto, 1989, peeji 109) bụkwa otu akụkụ dị iche nke otu eletrọniki.

translations.source: The “invisible team” is the management team to which each of the members report. The invisible team sets the standards for each member.
translations.reference: “Òtù anaghị ahụ anya” ahụ bụ òtù njikwa nke onye ọ bụla n’ime ndịòtù ahụ na-ekpesa. Òtù anaghị ahụ anya ahụ na-ewube ọkọlọtọ maka onyeòtù ọ bụla.
translations.hypothesis: Otu "na-adịghị ahụ anya" bụ otu ndị na-ahụ maka njikwa, nke ọ bụla n'ime ndị otu ahụ na-akpọrọ. Otu "na-adịghị ahụ anya" na-etinye ụkpụrụ maka ọ bụla n'ime ndị otu ahụ.

translations.source: Why would an organization want to go through the time consuming process of establishing a learning organization? One goal for putting organizational learning concepts into practice is innovation.
translations.reference: Gịnị mere otu ụlọọrụ ga-achọ ịgafe n'ime usoro na-egbu oge nke iwube otu ụlọọrụ ọmụmụ? Otu ebumnobi maka itinye echiche ọmụmụ keụlọọrụ n'ime ọrụ bụ nkepụta ihe ọhụrụ.
translations.hypothesis: Kedu ihe mere otu ọrụ ga-achọ ịgafe usoro ogologo oge nke ịmepụta otu ọrụ nke na-amụta? Otu ihe omume nke ịkpọọ ụkpụrụ mmụta n'ime otu ọrụ bụ inweta ọgbakọ.

translations.source: When all available resources are effectively used across the functional departments of an organization, creativity and ingenuity can transpire.
translations.reference: Mgbe e tinyere ngwaọrụ niile dị adị n’ọrụ n’ụzọ bara uru n’ime ngalaba niile na-arụ ọrụ n'ụlọọrụ ọbụla, nrụpụta ihe na amamihe pụrụ iche ga-enwe ike puta ihe.
translations.hypothesis: Mgbe eji ọrụ niile dị n'ụlọ ọrụ nke ọma n'ofe ngalaba dị iche iche, ọ nwere ike ibute ọganihu na echiche ọhụrụ.

translations.source: As a result, the process of an organization working together to overcome an obstacle can lead to a new innovative process to serve the customer's need.
translations.reference: N'ihi nke a, usoro nke otu ụlọọrụ ịrụkọta ọrụ ọnụ iji merie otu ihe mgbochi nwere ike idunyeru otu usoro nkpepụta ihe ọhụrụ iji jee ozi nke mkpa onye ahịa.
translations.hypothesis: N'ihi ya, usoro nke otu ọganihu na-arụkọrọ ọrụ ọnụ iji merie nsogbu nwere ike ibute usoro ọhụrụ na-emecha iji jikwaa mkpa nke ndị ahịa.

translations.source: Before an organization can be innovative, leadership must create a culture of innovation as well as shared knowledge and organizational learning.
translations.reference: Tupu ulo-oru obula enwee ike idi n’eweputa uche-ohuru, nduzi aghaghi ikepuya omenala uche-ohuu dika kwa nkerita nghota na imu ihe nke ulo-oru.
translations.hypothesis: Tupu otu ọgbakọ nwee ike ịmepụta ihe ọhụrụ, ndị isi kwesịrị ịmepụta usoro ndụ nke na-akwalite ọgbụgbụ, yana ịkekọrịta eziokwu na mmụta nke otu ahụ.

translations.source: Angel (2006), explains the Continuum approach as a method being used to help organizations reach a higher level of performance.
translations.reference: Angel (2006), kowara ukpuru nke agamnihu dika omume nke ejiri nyere otutu ulo-oru aka iru ogo di-elu nke iruputa ihe.
translations.hypothesis: Angel (n'afọ 2006) kọwara usoro "Continuum" dị ka otu ụzọ eji eme iji nyere ụlọ ọrụ aka iru ọkwa arụmụka dị elu.

translations.source: Neurobiological data provide physical evidence for a theoretical approach to the investigation of cognition. Therefore it narrows the research area and makes it much more exact.
translations.reference: Ozi ihe-omumundu-banyere-uburu ewetala akaebe ana ahu anya maka usoro kowaputa nye nyocha nke nkota. Nihi ya obelatala ogbe nchoputa ma mee ya kpom-kwem nke ukwu karia.
translations.hypothesis: Ozi gbasara usoro nke ahụ na akụrụ na-enye ihe aka n'ime maka ụzọ echiche dị iche iche iji nyochaa echiche. Ya mere, ọ na-ebelata mpaghara nyocha ahụ ma mee ka ọ bụrụ nke zuru oke.

translations.source: The correlation between brain pathology and behaviour supports scientists in their research.
translations.reference: Mmekọrịta n’etiti patọlọji ụbụrụ na omume kwadoro ndị ọka mmụta sayensị na nnyocha ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdịnihu dị n'etiti mgbe ahụghị nke ụbọchị na omume na-enyere ndị ọkà mmụta sayensị aka n'ime nyocha ha.

translations.source: It has been known for a long time that different types of brain damage, traumas, lesions, and tumours affect behaviour and cause changes in some mental functions.
translations.reference: Obu ihe ama-ama site na mgbe di anya na otutu mmeru-ahu uburu, mmeru-ahu uche , mmeru-ahu nke ahu, na otuto nke uburu n’emututa akparama-agwa ma kpatakwa mgbanwe na oru oburu ufodu.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dị ka ọtụtụ afọ ka amaara na ụdị mmerụ ahụ dị iche iche, mmetụta, mmerụ, na tumors nwere ike ịmetụta ọdịdị mmadụ ma mee mgbanwe na ụfọdụ ọrụ uche.

translations.source: The rise of new technologies allows us to see and investigate brain structures and processes never seen before.
translations.reference: Mmụbanye nke ụmụ teknụzụ ọhụrụ na-enye anyị ohere ịhụ ma nyochaa ọdịdị na arụmarụ ụbụrụ nke a na-ahụbeghị mbụ.
translations.hypothesis: Mmepe teknụlọji ọhụrụ na-enye anyị ohere ịhụ na ịlebara anya na akụkụ na usoro nke ahụ anụ nke anyị na adịghị ahụ mbụ.

translations.source: This provides us with a lot of information and material to build simulation models which help us to understand processes in our mind.
translations.reference: Nke a na-akuziri anyị ọtụtụ ihe ma na-enye anyị ihe anyị ji arụ oyiri ya nke na-enyere anyị aka ịghọta usoro n'uche anyị.
translations.hypothesis: Nke a na-enye anyị ozi na ihe ọmụma dị ukwuu iji wuo ụdị ihe atụ, nke na-enyere anyị aka ịghọta usoro dị n'ime anyị.

translations.source: Although AI has a strong connotation of science fiction, AI forms a very important branch of computer science, dealing with behavior, learning and intelligent adaptation in a machine.
translations.reference: Agbanyeghị na AI na-ada ka ihe gbasara akụkọ ifo sayensị, AI bụ ngalaba dị oke mkpa na sayensị kọmputa, nke gbasara etu igwe si eme omume, amụta ihe ma na-agbanwe dabere n'ihe ọ mụtara.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na AI nwere otu echiche dị njikọ na akụkọ ifụlụ, AI bụ otu akụkụ dị mkpa nke sayensi kọmputa, nke na-elekwasị anya na omume, mụtakwu, na mmezi ọgụgụ dị mma n'ime akụrume eletrọniki.

translations.source: Research in AI involves making machines to automate tasks that require intelligent behavior.
translations.reference: Nchọpụta na ngalaba AI gụnyere ịmepụta igwe ndị ga na-arụ ụmụ ọrụ ndị na-achọ amamihe nwere usoro.
translations.hypothesis: Nyocha na AI gụnyere ime ka akụrụngwa na-arụ ọrụ nke na-achọ ọrụ uche, ya bụ, na-eme ka akụrụngwa na-arụ ọrụ nke na-achọ nghọta.

translations.source: Examples include control, planning and scheduling, the ability to answer customer diagnoses and questions, as well as handwriting recognition, voice and face.
translations.reference: Ọmumatụ gụnyere njikwa, ịtụ arọ na ịhàzi oge, ike ịza ụmụ nchọpụta ọrịa na ajụjụ onye ahịa, ya na ịmata aka odide, olu na ihu.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ ihe atụ gụnyere njikwa, atụmatụ na itinye ụbọchị, ikike itinye aka na azịza ajụjụ ndị ahịa na nyocha ha, yana ikike ịmata akwụkwọ aka, olu olumba, na ihu.

translations.source: Such things have become separate disciplines, which focus on providing solutions to real life problems.
translations.reference: Ụdị ihe ndị ahụ aghụọla nkebi ọzụzụ ndị iche, nke na-agbado anya na-enye ụmụ azịza maka ụmụ nsogbu keụwa dị ire.
translations.hypothesis: Ihe ndị a abụrụla ọtụtụ ụlọ akwụkwọ dị iche iche, bụ ndị na-elekwasị anya na inye ngwọta maka nsogbu ndị na-apụta n'ọdịnihu.

translations.source: The AI ​​system is now often used in the fields of economics, medicine, engineering and the military, as has been built in several home computer and video game software applications.
translations.reference: Ukpuru nke AI ahu buzi nke ana etinyezi ugbua n’ihe banyere aku-n’uba, ogwu, ikpu-uzu na ndi-agha, dika arunyere n’ime ututu igwe komputa digasi iche-iche ndi ana eji n’ulo ya na ihe ntinye ihe egwuregwu onyonyo.
translations.hypothesis: Usoro arụ ọrụ nke akpọrọ "AI" (Artificial Intelligence) na-eji ugbu a karịrị n'ọtụtụ mpaghara, gụnyere ahịa,ọgwụgwụ, teknoloji, na ndị agha, dịka otu e jiri ya na ụfọdụ ngwaọrụ kọmputa ụlọ na egwuregwu vidiyo.

translations.source: Field trips are a large part of any classroom. Quite often a teacher would love to take her students places to which a bus trip is not an option.
translations.reference: Njem fild bụ otu nnukwu akụkụ nke klaasị ọ bụla. Ọtụtụ mgbe ọ na-amasị otu onye nkuzi ịkpọrọ ụmụ akwụkwọ ya gaa ebe ndị njem bọọsụ esoghị na nhọrọ ya.
translations.hypothesis: Nkwalite ụlọ akwụkwọ bụ akụkụ dị mkpa nke ụlọ akwụkwọ ọ bụla. Ọtụtụ oge, onye nkuzi ga-amasị itinye ụmụ akwụkwọ ya n'ebe ndị ọzọ, ebe ịgba ụgbọ oloko abụghị nhọrọ dị mma.

translations.source: Technology offers the solution with virtual field trips. Students can look at museum artifacts, visit an aquarium, or admire beautiful art while sitting with their class.
translations.reference: Nka na uza n’enye igbo-mkpa nke ime jem site ihu-nanya. Umu-akwukwo nwere ike ilele ihe ngosi n’ulo ngosi, zute ebe izu-azu maobu gosi mmasi nye oru nka dika ha no-odu n’ogige ulo-akwukwo ha.
translations.hypothesis: Teknụlọji na-enye ngwọta site n'ịlegharị ụlọ akwụkwọ na ebe ndị ọzọ n'ịntanetị. Ọrụ akwụkwọ nwere ike ịlewa ihe ndị dị na ụlọ ihe ngosi, gaa na ebe e ji akwụkwọ mmiri, ma ọ bụ hụ ọrụ nkà ndị mara mma, mgbe ha nọ na klasi ha.

translations.source: Sharing a field trip virtually is also a great way to reflect a on a trip and share experiences with future classes.
translations.reference: Ịkekọrịta njem site na kọmputa bụkwa otu ụzọ dị mma iji chee echiche na njem ma kekọrịta ahụmahụ nye klas ndị nke ọdịnihu.
translations.hypothesis: Ịkekọrịta njem ahụmahụ site na vidiyo bụkwa ụzọ dị mma iji nyochaa njem ahụ na ịnye ndị nkuzi na ụmụ akwụkwọ ndị na-abịa ohere ịmatakwu banyere ya.

translations.source: For example, each year students from Bennet School in North Carolina design a website about their trip to the State Capital, each year the website gets remodeled, but old versions are kept online to serve as a scrapbook.
translations.reference: Na imaatu, kwa afo umu-akwukwo sitere Ulo-akwukwo Bennet di na mpaghara ugwu Carolina na aruputa otu websaiti banyere njem ha na Isi Obodo, kwa afo aga arozihari websaiti a, mana aga edowe udidi ochie ya na ikuku iru oru dika akwukwo-efu.
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ọmụmaatụ, ọ bụrụ otu afọ, ụmụ akwụkwọ si n'ụlọ akwụkwọ Bennet na North Carolina na-emepụta weebsaịtị banyere njem ha na-eme gaa n'isi obodo steeti ahụ. Ọ bụkwa otu afọ, a na-eme atụmatụ ọhụrụ maka weebsaịtị ahụ, mana ụdị ndị ochie na-adị na ịntanetị iji jide eziokwu banyere njem ahụ.

translations.source: Blogs can also help improve student writing. While students often begin their blog experience with sloppy grammar and spelling, the presence of an audience generally changes that.
translations.reference: Ụmụ blọọgụ nwerekwara ike inye aka imelite ederede nwa akwụkwọ. Dị ka ụmụ akwụkwọ na-ebidokarị ahụmihe blọọgụ ha n'iji ụtọasụsụ na nsụpe na-adịghị nke ọma, ọnụnọ nke ndị nkiri na-agbanwekarị nke ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Blog ndị ọzọ nwekwara ike inyere aka imezi echiche na usoro akwụkwọ nke ụmụ akwụkwọ. Ọ bụ ezie na ụmụ akwụkwọ na-ebute mmalite nke ha na blog site n'ịbụrụ ndị na-eme ka usoro akwụkwọ ha bụrụ nke adịghị mma na ụdị okwu ha, ọ na-adịkarị ka mmejizi na-abịa site n'ịbụ onye na-ekiri.

translations.source: Since students are often the most critical audience, the blog writer begins to strive to improve writing to avoid criticism.
translations.reference: Ebe ọ bụ na ụmụ akwụkwọ na-abụkarị ndị nkiri kachasị mkpa, odee blọọgụ ahụ na-amalite ịgbalị imelite odide ya iji zere nkatọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ebe ọkọlọ maka ụmụ akwụkwọ bụkarị ndị na-ele anya nke ukwuu, ya mere onye na-ede akụkọ na blog na-amaka ịkwalite echiche ya na ide akwụkwọ iji zaghachi ma ọ bụ wepụ ụdị atụmụta ọ bụla.

translations.source: Also blogging "forces students to become more savvy about the world around them." The need to feed the interest of the audience inspires students to be clever and interesting (Toto, 2004).
translations.reference: Nakwa ime blọọgụ "na-akwanye ụmụakwụkwọ ịmatakwu ihe gbasara ụwa gbara ha gburugburu." Mkpa nke ịkwalite mmasị nke ndị nkiri na-akpali ụmụakwụkwọ inwe amamihe ma na-adọrọ mmasị (Toto, 2004).
translations.hypothesis: Ọzọkwa, ịme blọg na-akpali ụmụ akwụkwọ ka ha nwee nghọta nke ukwuu banyere ụwa ha nọ. Ọ dị mkpa ka ụmụ akwụkwọ na-agbalị ịnye ihe ndị na-atọ ụtọ na ihe ndị na-atụgharị uche ndị na-agụ, nke a na-akpali ha ka ha bụrụ ndị na-eme ihe ọma na ndị nwere ọdịmma (Toto, 2004).

translations.source: Blogging is a tool that inspires collaboration, and encourages students to extend learning well beyond the traditional school day.
translations.reference: Ide blogu bu ngwa oru na akpalite mmekorita, o na akwadokwa umuakwukwo ka ha gbatiaa mmuta ha karia mmuta n’ulo akwukwo.
translations.hypothesis: Ịmepụta akụkọ na ịntanetị bụ otu ngwaọrụ nke na-akwalite ọrụ otu, ọ na-agba ụmụ akwụkwọ ume ka ha gaa n'ihu na mmụta, ọbụna mgbe ụlọ akwụkwọ adịghị.

translations.source: Appropriate use of blogs "can empower students to become more analytical and critical; through actively responding to Internet materials, students can define their positions in the context of others' writings as well as outline their own perspectives on particular issues (Oravec, 2002).
translations.reference: Ojiji kwesịrị ekwesị nke ụmụ blọọgụ "nwere ike inye ụmụ akwụkwọ ike iji dịkwuo na kennyocha na ichekwu echiche; site n'ịza ọsịsọ n'ụmụ ihe ịntaneet, ụmụ akwụkwọ nwere ike ịkọwa ọnọdụ ha na nghọta nke ụmụ ederede ndị ọzọ ya na kwupụtachaa uche onwe ha n'ụmụ nsogbu pụrụ iche (Oravec, 2002).
translations.hypothesis: Onye nwere ike iji blọgụ nke ọma iji nyere ụmụ akwụkwọ aka ịbụ ndị na-atụgharị uche ma na-ele anya; site n'ịdabere onwe ha na ihe ndị dị na ịntanetị, ụmụ akwụkwọ nwere ike ikọwa echiche ha n'ihe gbasara echiche ndị ọzọ, yana ịkọwa echiche ha n'okwu dị iche iche (Oravec, 2002).

translations.source: Ottawa is Canada's charming, bilingual capital and features an array of art galleries and museums that showcase Canada's past and present.
translations.reference: Ottawa bu isi obodo mara mma, nwere asusu abuo nke Canada ma nwekwa galari nka na ebe ngosi nka di iche iche n’egosiputa Canada n’oge gara aga ma n’oge ugbu a.
translations.hypothesis: Ottawa bụ isi obodo Canada, nke mara mma na nke na-ekwu asụsụ abụọ, yana ọ nwere ọtụtụ ụlọ ihe osade na ụlọ ihe ngosi nke na-egosi akụkọ na oge a na-ebu ụzọ na Canada.

translations.source: Farther south is Niagara Falls and the north is home to the untapped natural beauty of the Muskoka and beyond.
translations.reference: Igakwuo ndida bu Mkpoda-mmiri Niagara ma mpaghara ugwu bu ulo nye nma udidi na emetubeghi aka nke Muskoka ma gafere.
translations.hypothesis: N'ebe ndịda anyanwụ, anyị nwere Agwa Niagara, ebe n'ebe ugwu, e nwere ihe ndị ọzọ dị ụtọ na ebe dị ka Muskoka na ebe ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: All these things and more highlight Ontario as what is considered quintessentially Canadian by outsiders.
translations.reference: Ihe ndị a niile na ọzọ na-egosipụta Ọntario dị ka ihe echere na ọ bụ site n'ogo kachasị zuo oke Ndị Kanada site n'aka ndị ọbịa.
translations.hypothesis: Ufọdụ ihe ndị a na ndị ọzọ na-egosi na Ontario bụ ebe a na-akpọkarị "Canada n'ezie" site n'anya ndị na-abata n'ebe ahụ.

translations.source: Large areas further north are quite sparsely populated and some is nearly uninhabited wilderness.
translations.reference: Ebe ndị buru ibu na ngapụga ugwu bụ ọzara nke obere ndị mmadụ bi ma ụfọdụ fọrọ nke nta ka ọ bụrụ ebe ndị mmadụ ebighị.
translations.hypothesis: Ebe ndị dị n'ebe ugwu karịrị, ọtụtụ ebe ha adịghị na mmadụ nke ukwuu, ma ụfọdụ ebe bụ obere mpaghara nke adịghị ebe mmadụ bi.

translations.source: For a comparison of population that surprises many: There are more African Americans living in the US than there are Canadian citizens.
translations.reference: Otu ntule ọnụ ọgụgụ na-agbagwoju ọtụtụ ndị mmadụ anya: Ndị isi ojii amerịka bi na mba Amerịka karịrị ndị Kanada bi ebe ahụ n'ọnụ ọgụgụ.
translations.hypothesis: Maka ihe atụ gbasara ọdịdị mmadụ nke na-atụ ụjọ ọtụtụ ndị: Ndị Afrika-Amerịka karịrị ndị obodo Canada n'ọnụ ọgụgụ na-ebi n'America.

translations.source: The East African Islands are in the Indian Ocean off the eastern coast of Africa.
translations.reference: Obodo-akuku-mmiri nke ndi Owuwa-anyanwu Africa di na Osimiri India na opupu onu mmiri owuwa-anyanwu Africa.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị ọkpụkpụ Afrịka nke Ndagha dị n'okpuru osimiri India, nso na osimiri ọdịda anyanwụ nke Afrika.

translations.source: Madagascar is by far the biggest, and a continent on its own when it comes to wildlife.
translations.reference: Madagaaka kachasị buo ibu, ma bụrụkwa kọntinentị nọọrọ onwe ya ma a bịa n'ihe gbasara anụmanụ ndị bi n'ọhịa.
translations.hypothesis: Madagascar bụ ụlọ ọrụ kachasị ukwuu, ọ bụkwa obere osimiri n'onwe ya ma ọ bịara ụdị anụmanụ dị iche iche.

translations.source: Most of the smaller islands are independent nations, or associated with France, and known as luxury beach resorts.
translations.reference: Ọtụtụ agwaetiti ndị ka obere bụ mba ndị kwụụrụ onwe ha, maọbụ nọrọ na njiko ha na France, ndị a makwaara dịka rezọt ọnụ osimiri bu ebe mkporindụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ n'ime obere ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ndị ahụ bụ mba ndị nweere onwe ha, ma ọ bụ ndị jikọtara ná France, ha na-akpọkwa ha "ebe ntu dị elu."

translations.source: The Arabs also brought Islam to the lands, and it took in a big way in the Comoros and Mayotte.
translations.reference: Ndị Arabụ wetekwara okpukpere Alakụba n'ala ndị ahụ, ma a nabatara ya nke ukwuu na mba Komoros na Mayọtụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị Arab kpebiri Islam na ala ndị ahụ, ma ọ bịara n'ụzọ dị ukwuu na Comoros na Mayotte.

translations.source: European influence and colonialism began in the 15th century, as Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama found the Cape Route from Europe to India.
translations.reference: Ike onwunwe ndị Yurop ọchịchị ala ọzọ bidoro n’ime narị afọ nke iri na ise, dị ka one ngagharị one Pọtugalụ Vasco da Gama chọtara Ụzọ Kepụ site na Yurop ruo Indịa.
translations.hypothesis: Mmetụta nke Europe na ọchịchị colonialism malitere n'afọ nke 15, mgbe onye nyocha Portugiz, bụ Vasco da Gama, chọpụtara ụzọ nke sitere na Europe ruo India.

translations.source: In the north the region is bounded by the Sahel, and in the south and west by the Atlantic Ocean.
translations.reference: N'akụkụ ugwu, Sahel gbara mpaghara a ogige; na ndịda ma n'ọdịda anyanwụ, Oke osimiri atlantik gbara ya ogige.
translations.hypothesis: N'ebe ugwu, obodo a na-echebe ya site na Sahara, ebe n'ebe ndịda na ndịda-ọhụrụ, ọ na-agba n'ọdọmmányá Atlantic.

translations.source: Women: It is recommended that any women travellers say that they are married, regardless of actual marital status.
translations.reference: Ụmụ nwanyị: Ọ bụ ihe akwadoro na ndị njem nwanyị ọ bụla kwuo na ha alụọla dị, n'agbanyeghị etu ọnọdụ ha dị n'ezie.
translations.hypothesis: Ụmụ nwanyị: Ọ dị mma ka ụmụ nwanyị ọ bụla na-eleta ebe ọzọ kwuo na ha lụrụ, n'agbanyeghị ọnọdụ ezinụlọ ha n'ezie.

translations.source: It is helpful to also wear a ring (just not one that looks too expensive.
translations.reference: Ọ na-enyekwara aka ịgba otu ọlaaka (naanị ọ bụghị nke yiri ka ọ dị oke ọnụ).
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dị mma ịgbanye obere ihe n'ucheghị anya (ma ọ bụghị ihe dị mkpa na ọ na-adị ka ọ dị oke ọnụ).

translations.source: Women should realize that cultural differences may result in what they would consider harassment and it is not uncommon to be followed, grabbed by the arm, etc.
translations.reference: Ụmụ nwanyị kwesịrị ịghọta na ndịiche omenala nwere ike ịkpata ihe ha ga-ewere dị ka ịchọ okwu ma ọ bụghị ihe a na-ara ahụ ịhụ isoro gị, ijide site n'aka, dgz.
translations.hypothesis: Ụmụ nwanyị ga-aghọta na ọdịiche omenụ nwere ike ibute ihe ndị ha na-achọpụta dị ka mmetụta iwe, ma ọ bụghị ihe ọjọọ, ọ bụkwa ihe zuru oke ịbụ na otu onye ga-eso ha, ma ọ bụ tụọ ha n'aka, wdg.

translations.source: Be firm in turning down men, and don't be afraid to stand your ground (cultural differences or not, it doesn't make it ok!).
translations.reference: Guzosie ike n'ịsị ụmụ nwoke mba, ma atụla egwu ịkwechiri (na-agbanyeghi ọdịnala ọbụla nke ọ bụ, o kwesighi ekwesi!).
translations.hypothesis: Kwenye na ịghara iji nwayiọrụ na-atụgharị ụmụ nwoke, ma akwụsịkwa ịgha-eri akụkụ gị (ma ọ bụrụ na enwere ọdịiche ọdịnala, ọ naghi emetụta na ọ dị mma!).

translations.source: The modern city of Casablanca was founded by Berber fishermen in the 10th century BCE, and was used by the Phoenicians, Romans, and the Merenids as a strategic port called Anfa.
translations.reference: Obodo nke Casablanca nke ugbu a bụ Berber fishermen wubere ya na BCE narị afọ nke iri, ma ndị Phoenicia, Rome, na ndị Merenid jiri ya dị ka ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri dị oke mkpa akpọrọ Anfa.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo Casablanca nke taa malitere site n'aka ndị mmadụ Berber bụ ndị na-azụ anụ na afọ nke 10 tupu Kristu, ma eji ya site n'aka ndị Phoenicia, ndị Roman, na ndị Merenid dị ka ọdọ ụgbọ oloko dị mkpa nke a na-akpọ Anfa.

translations.source: The Portuguese destroyed it and rebuilt it under the name Casa Branca, only to abandon it after an earthquake in 1755.
translations.reference: Ndị Pọtụgaalụ bibiri ya ma rụgharịa ya n’okpuru aha Casa Branca, naanị ịgbahapụ ya mgbe otu ala ọma jijiji mechara n’ime 1755.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị Portugal kpochara ya wee wụnye ya ọhụrụ, ma kpọrọ ya "Casa Branca," mana ha akwụsịrị iji ya mgbe mmiri ozuzo dị ukwuu merụrụ ya na afọ 1755.

translations.source: The Moroccan sultan rebuilt the city as Daru l-Badya and it was given the name Casablanca by Spanish traders who established trading bases there.
translations.reference: Sọltan Ndị Moroko ahụ rụgharịrị obodo ahụ dị ka Darụ-I-Badya ma e nyere ya aha Casablanka site n'aka Ndị Spen na-azụ ahịa ndị wubere isi ebe ndị a na-ere ahịa ebe ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ Sultan nke Morocco wepụtara obodo ahụ ọhụrụ, wee kpọọ ya "Daru l-Badya." Ndị ochie Spain bụ ndị na-azụ ahịa bụ ndị bịarutere ebe ahụ, bụ ndị kpọrọ obodo ahụ ahụ "Casablanca."

translations.source: Casablanca is one of the least interesting places to shop in all of Morocco.
translations.reference: Casablanca bụ otu n'ime opekata mpe ebe na-adọrọ mmasị ịzụ ahịa na Morocco niile.
translations.hypothesis: Casablanca bụ otu n'ime ebe ndị kacha adịghị mma iji zụrụ ihe niile na Morocco.

translations.source: Around the old Medina it's easy to find places selling traditional Moroccan goods, such as tagines, pottery, leather goods, hookahs, and a whole spectrum of geegaws, but it's all for the tourists.
translations.reference: Gburugburu Medina ochie ahụ ọ dị mfe ịchọta ebe ndị na-ere ụmụ ngwaahịa ọdịnala Ndị Moroko, dị ka ụmụ tagịnị, ite akpụrụ akpụ, ngwaahịa ejiri akpụkpọ anụ mee, huuka, na giigawụ nke ụdịdị dị iche iche zuru ezu, mana ha nille bụ maka ndị nleta.
translations.hypothesis: N'akụkọ ụlọ ochie Medina, ọ dị mfe ịchọta ebe ndị na-ere ngwaahịa ndị Morocco dị mma, dị ka tagines, akwa ụlọ, ngwaahịa ahịhịa, hookah, na ọtụtụ ihe ndị ọzọ, mana ihe niile ahụ bụ maka ndị njalaba.

translations.source: Goma is a tourist city of the Democratic Republic of Congo in the extreme east near Rwanda.
translations.reference: Goma bụ obodo nleta nke Democratic Replublic nke Kongo n'ime akụkụ ọwụwa anyanwụ kachasị anya na nso Rwanda.
translations.hypothesis: Goma bụ obodo nleta nke Repubuliki Dimokratiki Congo, nke dị n'ebe ndịda-ochibe nke mba ahụ, nso Rwanda.

translations.source: In 2002 Goma was destroyed by lava from the Nyiragongo volcano which buried most of the town’s streets, particularly the town centre.
translations.reference: N'afọ 2002, ebibiri Goma site n’aka lava si na ugwu ọkụ Nyiragongo nke liri ọtụtụ n'okporoama obodo, ọ kachasị etiti obodo.
translations.hypothesis: N'afọ 2002, ebuu Goma n'iwu site n'ọdịdị mmiri na-apụta n'ime volcano Nyiragongo, nke mebiri ọtụtụ okporo ụzọ n'obodo ahụ, karịsịa ebe obodo ahụ nwere nnukwu ọrụ.

translations.source: While Goma is reasonably safe, any visits outside of Goma should be researched to understand the state of the fighting that persists in the North Kivu province.
translations.reference: Dịka Goma nwetụrụ nchekwa n’ụdị dịtụ mma, nleta ọ bụla na mpụga Goma bụ nke ekwesịrị inyocha iji ghọta ọnọdụ nke ọgụ ka nogidesiri ike n’Ugwu ngalaba ọchịchị kizu.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na Goma dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ị na-elekọta onwe gị, ọ bụrụ na ị chọrọ ịga ebe ọzọ, ọ dị mkpa ịme nyocha iji ghọta ọnọdụ okwu agha na-enweghị atụ na mpaghara North Kivu.

translations.source: The city is also the base to climb the Nyiragongo volcano along with some of the cheapest Mountain Gorilla tracking in Africa.
translations.reference: Obodo ahụ bụkwa ntọala ịrị ugwu mgbawa Nyiragongo tinyere ụfọdụ nsochi Ọzọdimgba Ugwu dịchasị ọnụ ala n'Afrịka.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo ahụ bụkwa ebe eji malite ịgaba n'elu volcano Nyiragongo, yana ọ bụkwa otu n'ime ebe ndị ọzọ ebe a na-ahụ Mountain Gorilla na ọnụ ahịa kacha ọnụ na Africa.

translations.source: You can use boda-boda (motorcycle taxi) to get around Goma. The normal (local) price is ~500 Congolese Francs for the short ride.
translations.reference: Ị nwere ike iji boda-boda (tagzi ọgba tum tum) ịga gburugburu Goma. Ọnụahịa nkịtị (ebeụlọ) bụ Francs Ndị Congo ~500 maka ọkwụkwọ dị mkpirikpi.
translations.hypothesis: Ị nwere ike iji "boda-boda" (akwụkwọ ndụ akwụkwọ ndụ) gaa ebe ndị ọzọ na Goma. Ọdịdị ahịa nkịtị (ahịa obodo) bụ ihe dị ka 500 francs nke Congo maka njem dị mkpụrụ.

translations.source: Combined with its relative inaccessibility, "Timbuktu" has come to be used as a metaphor for exotic, distant lands.
translations.reference: Tinyere na ira-ahu na nweta ya karia ibe ya, "Timbuktu" aburula ihe eji ama-atu maka ala ndi di anya, di oke-onu.
translations.hypothesis: N'ihi na ọ dị oke ịtụgharị, "Timbuktu" abụrụla ihe eji akọwa ebe ndị dị anya na ebe ndị ọzọ, ebe ndị dị iche iche.

translations.source: Today, Timbuktu is an impoverished town, although its reputation makes it a tourist attraction, and it has an airport.
translations.reference: Taa, Timbuktu obodo agụọ na-egbu, agbanyeghị n'ugwu ya na-eme ya otu ndọta ndị nleta, na o nwere otu ọdụ ụgbọelu.
translations.hypothesis: Taa, Timbuktu bụ obodo na-enweta ọtụtụ nsogbu, ọ bụ ezie na aha ya na-eme ka ndị mmadụ na-abata ya dị ka ebe nleta, yana ọ nwere ọdụ ụgbọ elu.

translations.source: In 1990, it was added to the list of world heritage sites in danger, due to the threat of desert sands.
translations.reference: N'afọ 1990, e debanyere ya n'etiti ebe ọpụrụiche n'ụwa ndị nọ na nsogbu mkpochapụ, maka nsogbu aja si n'ọzara.
translations.hypothesis: N'afọ 1990, e jiri ya n'ọdịnihu na ndepụta ebe ndụ ọdịmma ụwa nke nwere egwu, n'ihi ihe egwu nke ọhịa.

translations.source: It was one of the major stops during Henry Louis Gates' PBS special Wonders of the African World.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ otu isi nkwụsịtụ n'oge Henry Louis Gates Ihe-ebube pụrụ iche PBS nke Ụwa Afrịka.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ otu n'ime ebe ndị isi ebe a na-agụ akwụkwọ na ihe omume "Wonders of the African World" nke Henry Louis Gates họpụtara na usoro nke PBS.

translations.source: The city is in stark contrast to the rest of the country's cities, because it has more of an Arabic flair than of an African.
translations.reference: Obodo ahụ dị n'ọdịiche kachasị ya n'ụmụ obodo nke mba ahụ fọdụrụnụ, n'ihi na o nwere karịa mmasị nke Arabik karịa otu Onye Afrịka.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo ahụ adịghị dị ka obodo ndị ọzọ n'obodo ndị ọzọ n'ụwa anyị, n'ihi na ọ nwere ọtụtụ ihe ndụ nke Arab karịa ihe ndụ nke Afrịka.

translations.source: The Kruger National Park (KNP) lies in the north-east of South Africa and runs along the border of Mozambique in the east, Zimbabwe in the north, and the southern border is the Crocodile River.
translations.reference: Obianụọhịa Kemba Kruger (KNP) nọ n'ebe ugwu-ọwụwa anyanwu nke South Afrịka ma nọrọ ogologo ókè ahụ nke Mozambik n'ime ọwụwa anyanwụ, Zimbabwe n'ime ebe ugwu, na ókè ebe ndịda ahụ bụ Osimmiri Agụiyi.
translations.hypothesis: Parki Nara nke Kruger (KNP) dị n'ebe ndịda-ọhụrụ nke South Africa, ọ na-agba elu n'akụkụ osimiri Mozambique n'ebe ndịda, Zimbabwe n'ebe ugwu, yana akụkụ ndịda ya bụ Osimiri Crocodile.

translations.source: The park covers 19,500 km² and is divided in 14 different ecozones, each supporting different wildlife.
translations.reference: Ogige a ruru 19,500 km² nakwa ekewara ya n'ụzọ mpaghara ecozone 14, ebe nke ọbụla na-akwado ụdịrị anụ ọhịa dị iche.
translations.hypothesis: Park a ahụ obere mpaghara nke kilomita kwadrata 19,500, ma ebe ahụ kewara n'ime mpaghara 14 dị iche iche, ọ bụla n'ime ha na-akwado ụdị anụmanụ dị iche iche.

translations.source: It is one of the main attractions of South Africa and it is considered the flagship of South African National Parks (SANParks).
translations.reference: Ọ bụ otu n’ime nke isi ihe ndọta nke Ndịda Afrịka ma a na-ewe ya dị ka nke kacha mma nke Ebennọkọta Nkeobodo (SANParks) Ndịda Afrịka.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ otu n'ime ihe ndị a na-eleta karịa na ndịda Afrịka, ma a na-akpọ ya isi ihe nke Park ndị Afrịka nke Ndịda (South African National Parks - SANParks).

translations.source: As with all South African National Parks, there are daily conservation and entry fees for the park.
translations.reference: Dịka o si adị n'ogige mba niile nọ na Sawụtụ Afrịka, e nwere ụgwọ nchekwa n mbanye a na-akwụ kwa ụbọchị n'ogige a.
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ọtụtụ ọdụnwa ndị ọzọ nke South Africa, enwere ụgwọ kwa ụbọchị maka nlekọta na ịbanye n'ime ọdụnwa ahụ.

translations.source: It may also be beneficial for one to buy a Wild Card, which provides entry to either selections of parks in South Africa or all of the South African National Parks.
translations.reference: O nwekwara ike iba uru ka mmadu gote Kaadi Ohia nke ga-enye gi ikikere iji banye na ogige ahoputagoro na South Africa ma o bu na Ogige Kemba South Africa niile.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ nwere ike ịbụ nke dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na otu mmadụ zụrụ "Wild Card," nke na-enye ohere ịbanye n'ọtụtụ park dị na Etiti Afrika, ma ọ bụ n'ọtụtụ park ndị ọzọ nke Etiti Afrika.

translations.source: Hong Kong Island gives the territory of Hong Kong its name and is the place that many tourists regard as the main focus.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ site na Agwaetiti Họng Kọng ka mpaghara Họng Kọng nwetara aha ya; Ọ bụkwa ebe a ka ndị njem nlereanya na-ahụta dịka ebe kachasị mkpa.
translations.hypothesis: Agbụrụ Hong Kong bụ ebe a na-akpọkwa Hong Kong, yana bụ ebe ndi mmadụ na-abata n'ọdịnala na-echekarịkarị ka ọ bụ ebe isi.

translations.source: The parade of buildings that make the Hong Kong skyline has been likened to a glittering bar chart that is made apparent by the presence of the waters of Victoria Harbour.
translations.reference: E jirila ụmụ ogologo ụlọ elu na-achọ igwe Họng Kọng mma maa atụ na ha yiri eserese baa chat, nke mmiri Viktoria Habọ mere ka ọ pụta ihe.
translations.hypothesis: Ụlọ ndị dị na Hong Kong, bụ ndị na-eme ka ọdịdị obodo ahụ dị ụtọ, echekwara ka akụkọ efu na-acha anyanwụ, nke e mere ka ọ pụta n'anya site n'ịdị mmiri nke Victoria Harbour.

translations.source: To get the best views of Hong Kong, leave the island and head for the Kowloon waterfront opposite.
translations.reference: Ịhụta Họng Kọng n'ụzọ kachasị mma, pụọ n'agwaetiti gawa na Kowloon, mpaghara akụkụ mmiri, nke chere gị ihu.
translations.hypothesis: Iji hụ ihe ndị kacha mma nke Hong Kong, gaa pụọ ụlọ na gaa n'akụkụ osimiri Kowloon nke dị n'akụkụ.

translations.source: The great majority of Hong Kong Island's urban development is densely packed on reclaimed land along the northern shore.
translations.reference: Oke ihe ka n'ọnụ ọgụgụ n'ime mmepe obodo nke Agwaetiti Hong Kong jupụtara n'ọnụ na ala a napụtara na mmiri dị n'ogologo ụzọ nke ugwu akụkụ oke osimiri.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ebe obibi na mpaghara ụlọ obodo nke Hong Kong Island eterekarị elu n'ebe dịta na ala a chịkọtara n'akụkụ osimiri ahụ nke nọrọnwụ.

translations.source: This is the place the British colonisers took as their own and so if you are looking for evidence of the territory's colonial past, this is a good place to start.
translations.reference: Ebe a bụ ebe ndị nchịkwa mba si Britenụ were dịka nke ha ya mere ọ bụrụ na ị na-achọ maka akaebe nke nchịkwa ókèala ahụ gara aga, ebe a bụ ebe dị mma ịmalite.
translations.hypothesis: Nke a bụ ebe ndị òtù Britain nwere iji dịka ebe ha nwere iji, ya mere, ọ bụrụ na ị na-achọ ihe ngosi nke oge ọchịchị colonial nke obere ala ahụ, ọ bụ ebe dị mma ịmalite.

translations.source: The Sundarbans are the largest littoral mangrove belt in the world, stretching 80 km (50 mi) into the Bangladeshi and Indian hinterland from the coast.
translations.reference: Ebe Sundarbans bụ ebe ala nwere ọhịa mmiri nọ n'akụkụ mmiri kachasị ukwuu n'ụwa dum, na-agbatị ruo kilomita 80 (50 mi) n'ime n'ala Bangladesh na India ahụ nke amaghị ama site n'ụsọ osimiri.

translations.source: The Sundarbans has been declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The part of the forest within Indian territory is called Sundarbans National Park.
translations.reference: E kwupụtawo na Sundarbans bụ otu Ebe Nketa Keụwa UNESCO. Akụkụ nke oke ọhịa n'ime ókèala nke Indịa ka a na-akpọ Obianụọhịa Kemba Sundarbans.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ Sundarbans etuputara dị ka ebe ndụ nke ụwa nke UNESCO. Akụkụ ọhịa ahụ dị n'ime ala India na-akpọ Sundarbans National Park.

translations.source: The forests aren't just mangrove swamps though — they include some of the last remaining stands of the mighty jungles which once covered the Gangetic plain.
translations.reference: Ọhịa ndị a abụghịkwa sọọsọ apịtị mangrov dị na ha – ha gụnyekwara ihe ndị ka fọrọ site n'oke ọhịa ndị juburu Ala nọ na mpaghara Ganjiz.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdụnwa ahụ abụghị naanị ọhịa mangrove, kama ọ gụnyere ụfọdụ n'ime ọhịa osimiri kacha dịkarịcha na-erubeghị, bụ ndị na-adịbeghị ebe, bụ ndị na-adịbe ebe a na-akpọ "Gangetic plain" gara aga.

translations.source: The Sundarbans cover an area of 3,850 km², of which about one-third is covered in water/marsh areas.
translations.reference: Sundabans kpuchiri ohere km² 3850, nke mmiri maọbụ ala apịtị kpuchiri otu ụzọ n'ụzọ atọ ya.
translations.hypothesis: Obere Sundarbans na-agụnye mpaghara nke kilomita kwadrata 3,850, ebe ihe ruru otu ụzọ atọ n'ime mpaghara ahụ bụ mpaghara mmiri na osimiri.

translations.source: Since 1966 the Sundarbans have been a wildlife sanctuary, and it is estimated that there are now 400 Royal Bengal tigers and about 30,000 spotted deer in the area.
translations.reference: Ka mgbe 1966, ka Sundarbans ji buru ebe obibi nso anu ohia ana asi na aga enwe ihe dika 400 Royal Bengal tiger na ihe dika 30,000 mgbada nwere ntupo na mpaghara ebe ahu.
translations.hypothesis: Kemgbe afọ 1966, Sundarbans abụrụla ebe nchekwa anụmanụ, ma a tụrụ anya na ugbu a, e nwere ihe dị ka 400 ụjọ Royal Bengal na ihe dị ka 30,000 ụjọ ndị nwere agba agba na mpaghara ahụ.

translations.source: Buses depart the inter-district bus station (across the river) throughout the day, though most, especially those heading to the east and Jakar/Bumthang leave between 06:30 and 07:30.
translations.reference: Bọọsụ na-esi n'ọdụ ụgbọala njikọ-mpaghara apụ (n'ofe osimiri ahụ) mgbe niile n'ụbọchị, agbanyeghị na nke kacha, tụmadị ndị ahụ na-aga n'ebe ọwụwaanyanwụ na Jakar/Bumthang na-apụ n'etiti 06:30 na 07:30.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtọ ụgbọ oloko na-apụ n'ebe ọdọ ụgbọ oloko dị n'etiti mpaghara (n'akụkụ osimiri) ruo ụbọchị niile, mana ọtọ karịsị, ọkachasị ndị na-aga n'ebe ndị di anya na Jakar/Bumthang, na-apụ n'etiti awa 6:30 na 7:30.

translations.source: As the inter-district buses are often full, it is advisable to purchase a ticket a few days in advance.
translations.reference: Dị ka ụmụ bọọsụ njikọ-mpaghara na-ejukarị eju, ọ bụ ezi ndụmọdụ ịzụta otu tiketi ụbọchị ole na ole n'ọdịnihu.
translations.hypothesis: Ebe ọtụtụ ndị na-eji ụgbọ oluebe anya, ọ ka mma ịzụta tiketi ụbọchị ole na ole tupu ụbọchị ahụ.

translations.source: Most districts are served by small Japanese Coaster Buses, which are comfortable and sturdy.
translations.reference: A na-ejere imirikiti mpaghara ozi site n'ụmụ Nnukwu Bọọsụ nke ndị Japan, nke dị mma ma sie ike.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ mpaghara na-ejikarị ụgbọ oloko ndị Japan, nke bụ "Coaster Buses," na-ebute ndị mmadụ, ụgbọ oloko ndị a dị mma ma jiri ike.

translations.source: Shared taxis are a quick and comfortable means to travel to nearby places, such as Paro (Nu 150) and Punakha (Nu 200).
translations.reference: Tagzi ekere eke bụ ụzọ dị ọsịsọ ma maa mma iji gaa ebe dị nso, dịka Paro (Nu 150) na Punakha (Nu 200).
translations.hypothesis: Ọtọ ụgbọ ala ejikọrọ bụ ụzọ ngwa ngwa na dị mma iji gaa ebe ndị dị nso, dị ka Paro (Nu 150) na Punakha (Nu 200).

translations.source: The Oyapock River Bridge is a cable-stayed bridge. It spans the Oyapock River to link the cities of Oiapoque in Brazil and Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock in French Guiana.
translations.reference: Akwammiri Osimiri Oyapock bụ otu akwa mmiri ejiri kebùl runye ya. Ọ gbara gburugburu Osimiri Oyapock iji jikọọ ụmụ obodo nke Oiapoque n'ime Brazịl na Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock n'ime French Guiana.
translations.hypothesis: Ọnụ ụzọ Oyapock bụ onụ ụzọ nke e jiri eriri na akara. Ọ na-agba n'elu osimiri Oyapock iji jọọta obodo Oiapoque na Brazil na Saint-Georges de l'Oyapock na French Guiana.

translations.source: The two towers rise to a height of 83 meters, it's 378 meters long and it has two lanes of 3.50 m wide.
translations.reference: Towa abuo ahu rigoro 83 meters, ogologo o bu 378 meters n’ogologo ma o nwekwara obodobo uzo abuo di 3.50m.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ abụọ ahụ na-erị elu ruo metres 83, ọ dịkarịrị metres 378 ogologo, ọ nwere ọkpụrụ ọkwụ abụọ nke metres 3.50 n'agba.

translations.source: The vertical clearance under the bridge is 15 meters. Construction was completed in August 2011, it didn't open to traffic until March 2017.
translations.reference: Ogologo ahụ ya kwụ-ọtọ nke akwa mmiri ahụ bụ mita 15. A rụchara ọrụrụ ya n'Ọgọọst 2011, e mepeghị ya nye ụgbọala ruo Maachị 2017.
translations.hypothesis: Ọnọdụ elu dị n'okpuru akụrị ahụ bụ metiru 15. A mechara ọrụ nkwakọwa ahụ na Ọgọọstụ afọ 2011, mana ọ malitere ịgba ụgbọ ala naanị na Machị afọ 2017.

translations.source: The bridge is scheduled to be fully operational in September 2017, when the Brazilian customs checkpoints are expected to be finished.
translations.reference: E hiwere na akwa ahụ ga-ebido rụwa ọrụ n'uju na Septemba 2017, mgbe a na-ele anya ịrụcha ebe nnyocha nke ụlọọrụ na-ahụ maka ọpụpụ na mbata nke ndị Brazili.
translations.hypothesis: Agbụrụ ahụ kwadoro ka ọ malite ịrụ ọrụ ozugbo na ọnwa Septemba afọ 2017, mgbe e kwenyere na ọkacha ụlọ nyocha nke ndị Brazil ga-emechapụ.

translations.source: The Guaraní were the most significant indigenous group inhabiting what is now Eastern Paraguay, living as semi-nomadic hunters who also practised subsistence agriculture.
translations.reference: Ndị Guaraní bụ otu amaala kachasị gbaa ọkpụrụkpụrụ bi n'eba a na-akpọ ugbua Ọwụwaanyanwụ Paragụwa, ha na-ebi ka ndị dinta na-awagharị awagharị ma na-arụkwa ọrụ ugbo mmepụta nri nke onwe.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị Guaraní bụ otu ndị obodo dị mkpa kachasị na mpaghara bụ ugbu a bụ mpaghara ndịda Paraguay, ha nọrọ dị ka ndị na-eje ije na-achọ ọchịchị, ma ha na-eme ụlọ ọrụ obere na-ebufe nri ha chọrọ.

translations.source: The Chaco region was home to other groups of indigenous tribes such as the Guaycurú and Payaguá, who survived by hunting, gathering and fishing.
translations.reference: Mpaghara Chako bụ ụlọ nye ụfọdụ agbụrụ amaala ndị ọzọ dịka Guaykuru na Payagua, ndị ji nta, ntụtụkọ, na ịkụ azụ wee zụọ onwe ha nri.
translations.hypothesis: Obodo Chaco bụ ebe obibi ndị otu ndị Igbo ndị ọzọ, dị ka ndị Guaycurú na Payaguá, bụ ndị nọgide ndụ site n'ịjụ ọchịchị, ịnweta ihe ndị dị n'okpuru, na ịsa nkita.

translations.source: In the 16th century Paraguay, formerly called "The Giant Province of the Indies", was born as a result of the encounter of Spanish conquerors with the native indigenous groups.
translations.reference: N'ime narị afọ nke iri na isii Paragwei, a kpọbụrụ "Nnukwu Ngalaba Ọchịchị nke Ndị Indii", bụ nke a mụrụ n'ihi mbịakwute nke ndị mmeri Ndị Spen ya na ụmụ òtù nwaafọ amaala.
translations.hypothesis: N'ime afọ 16, Paraguay, nke a na-akpọ "Obodo Biafran nke Ukwu" tupu, bịara ebe ahụ n'ihi mmekọrịta nke ndị Spanish na-achọ agụụ na ndị obodo mbụ nke ebe ahụ.

translations.source: The Spaniards started the colonization period which lasted for three centuries.
translations.reference: Ndị Spen bidoro oge ọchịchị ike nke digidere ruo narị afọ atọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị Spain malitere oge ọchịchị ndị mba ọzọ, nke garafa afọ atọ narị.

translations.source: Since the foundation of Asunción in 1537, Paraguay has managed to keep a lot of its indigenous character and identity.
translations.reference: Kemgbe ntọala Asunción n’ime 1537, Paraguay agbalịala idobe ọtụtụ n’ime omume na njirimara amaala ya.
translations.hypothesis: Kemgbe oge e guzoro obodo Asunción na afọ 1537, mba Paraguay enweela ike n'ịchekwa ọtụtụ akụkụ nke ọdịnala na ọnọdụ echiche ndị bi n'ebe ahụ.

translations.source: Argentina is well known for having one of the best polo teams and players in the world.
translations.reference: Amaara mba Ajentịna dịka obodo nwere ndị egwuregwu na otu egwuregwu polo kachasị mma n'ụwa dum.
translations.hypothesis: Argentina maara nke ukwuu maka inwe otu n'ime ndị otu polo kacha mma na ndị egwuregwu n'ụwa niile.

translations.source: The largest tournament of the year takes place in December at the polo fields in Las Cañitas.
translations.reference: Ndọrọndọrọ kachasị ukwu nke afọ ahụ na-eme na Disemba na fịịldị polo n’ime Las Cañitas.
translations.hypothesis: Asọmpi kachasị ukwuu nke afọ ahụ na-eme na Disemba, na mpempe polo dị na Las Cañitas.

translations.source: Smaller tournaments and matches can also be seen here at other times of the year.
translations.reference: Obere asọmpi ga na egwuregwu bọlụ ga ka e nwere ike ịhụ ebe a n'oge ụfọdụ n'afọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ egwuregwu na asọmpi ndị ntaanya na-eme ebe a, ọ bụghị naanị n'oge ụfọdụ nke afọ.

translations.source: For news on tournaments and where to buy tickets for polo matches, check Asociacion Argentina de Polo.
translations.reference: Maka akụkọ gbasara ụmụ ndorondoro na ebe a na-azụ tiketi maka egwuregwu polo, lelee Asociacion Argentina de Polo.
translations.hypothesis: Maka ozi gbasara asọmpi na ebe ị nwere ike ịzụta tiketi maka egwuregwu polo, lelee "Asociacion Argentina de Polo."

translations.source: The official Falklands currency is the Falkland pound (FKP) whose value is set equivalent to that of one British pound (GBP).
translations.reference: Ego azụmahịa mba Fọlkụlandị bụ pam Fọlkụlandị (FKP) nke ọnụ ya na otu pam ndị Britenị (GBP) ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ ahụi nke Falklands bụ Falkland pound (FKP), na uru ya egosiri ka ọ bụrụ otu pound nke Britain (GBP).

translations.source: Money can be exchanged at the only bank in the islands which is located in Stanley across from the FIC West store.
translations.reference: E nere ike ime mgbanwe ego na naanị otu ụlọ akụ nọ n’agwaetiti ndị ahụ nke a ga-achọtali n’ime Stanley n’ofe site n’ụlọ ahịa FIC West.
translations.hypothesis: Akụ nwere ike ịnyefe na ụlọ akụ naanị dị na ndị ọzọ, nke dị na Stanley, nso ụlọ ahịa FIC West.

translations.source: British pounds will generally be accepted anywhere in the islands and within Stanley credit cards and United States dollars are also often accepted.
translations.reference: A ga-anabata n’izugbe pam ndị Britenụ ebe ọbụla n’ime agwaetiti ndị ahụ ma na gburugburu ụmụ kaadị mbiri ego Stanley na dọla mba Amerịka sokwa na ndị a na-anabata.
translations.hypothesis: Ọka Britain (British pounds) ga-anabatakarị na ebe niile na ndị ọzọ n'akụkụ ụwa ahụ, yana na Stanley, kaadị ego (credit cards) na dollar nke United States (United States dollars) na-anabatakarịkwa.

translations.source: On the outlying islands credit cards will probably not be accepted, although British and United States currency may be taken; check with the owners in advance to determine what is an acceptable payment method.
translations.reference: N’agwaetiti ndị nọ na mpụga ebe ahụ ụmụ kaadị akwụmụgwọ nwere ike a gaghị anabata ya, n’agbanyeghị na enwere ike iwe ego Britenụ na United States; leru anya na ndị nwe ya n’ọdịnihu iji chọpụta ihe bụ ụzọ nkwụmụgwọ a na-anabata.
translations.hypothesis: N'akụkọ ụlọ ọrụ ndị dị n'akụkụ osimiri, ọ gaghị ekwe omume itinye akaaka ego, ọ bụ ezie na ha nwere ike itinye ego nke Britain na United States; jụọ ndị nwe ụlọ ndị ahụ tupu oge ahụ iji chọpụta ụzọ ọ dị mma iji kwụọ ego.

translations.source: It is nearly impossible to exchange Falklands currency outside of the islands, so exchange money prior to leaving the islands.
translations.reference: Ọ na-ara ezigbote ahụ ịgbanwe ego Falklands ma e si n'agwaetiti a pụọ, ya mere gbanwee ego gi tupu i si na ya pụọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dị oke mgbagwoju anya ịgbasa ego nke Falklands n'ebe ndị ọzọ na-adịghị nso na ndị ọzọ, ya mere, gbasa ego tupu ịhapụ ndị ọzọ ahụ.

translations.source: Since Montevideo is south of the Equator, it is summer there when it's winter in the Northern Hemisphere and vice versa.
translations.reference: Ebe Montevideo dị na ndịda Iquetọ, ọ bụ oge ọkọchị ebe ahụ mgbe oge oyi dị na Ebe ugwu Emisfee ma n'otu aka ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ebe Montevideo nọ, ọdịda anyanwụ nọ n'ebe ndịda, ya mere ọ bụ oge ọkụkọ anya ebe ahụ mgbe ọ bụ oge oyi na akụkụ osimiri ugwu, ma ọ bụkwa ọkụkọ anya mgbe ọ bụ oge oyi na akụkụ osimiri ugwu.

translations.source: Montevideo is in the subtropics; in the summer months, temperatures above +30°C are common.
translations.reference: Montevideo nọ n'ime ebe na-ekpọ ọkụ ma jụọkwa oyi; n'ime ụmụ ọnwa ọkọchị, okpomọkụ gafere +30°C bụ ihe nkịtị.
translations.hypothesis: Montevideo dị n'obere mpaghara tropika; n'oge ọkọchị, ọ bụ ihe nkịtị ka okpomọkụ ruo karịa +30°C.

translations.source: The winter can be deceptively chilly: temperatures rarely go below freezing, but the wind and humidity combine to make it feel colder than what the thermometer says.
translations.reference: Oge oyi nwere ike ịjụ ezigbo oyi n'aghụghọ: okpomọkụ na-ara ahụ tupu ya gaa n'okpuru ịghọ okwute mmiri, mana ikuku na oruru mmiri na-abịakọta ọnụ ime ka o nwee mmetụta kara jụọ oyi karịa ihe temometa kwuru.
translations.hypothesis: Oge ọkụ na-abụkarị oge na-adị jụụ nke na-atụ ụjọ: ọ bụ ezie na ọtụtụ oge, okpomọkụ adịghị enye ala, mana ikuku na mmiri na-ejikọta ọnụ iji mee ka ọ dị jụụ karịa ihe thermometer na-egosi.

translations.source: There are no particular "rainy" and "dry" seasons: the amount of rain stays roughly the same throughout the year.
translations.reference: Enweghị ihe dị ka "udu mmiri" na "ọkọchị": ogo mmiri ozuzo na-anọkarị otu ebe ogologo afọ niile.
translations.hypothesis: Enweghị oge "ọụụ" na oge "enweghị ọụụ" dị iche iche: ọkụkpụ ọụụ na-adịkarị otu na ọtụtụ ọnwa nke afọ.

translations.source: Though many of the animals in the park are used to seeing humans, the wildlife is nonetheless wild and should not be fed or disturbed.
translations.reference: Agbanyeghị na ọ maala ahụ ọtụtụ n'ime ụmụ anụmanụ nọ n'obianụmanụ ịhụ ndị mmadụ, ka o sina dị anụ ọhịa bụ nke azụghịazụ ma e kwesịghị inye ha nri ma ọ bụ nye ha nsogbu.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụ ezie na ọtụtụ anụmanụ na park ahụ na-adị mma ịhụ mmadụ, anụ ọhịa ahụ ka bụ anụ ọhịa, ya mere ekekwala ya ma ọ bụ mee ka ọ dị njọ.

translations.source: According to park authorities, stay at least 100 yards/meters away from bears and wolves and 25 yards/meters from all other wild animals!
translations.reference: Site n'aka ndị na-ahụ maka ogige anụmanụ, nọtee aka opekata mpe yadị maọbụ mita 100 n'ebe anụ ọhịa bea na wulfu nọ na yadị maọbụ mita 25 n'ebe anụ ọhịa ndị ọzọ niile nọ!
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ndị ọchịchị park ahụ si kwuo, debe onwe gị na akụkụ dị anya karịa 100 yaarda/mita site na nkịta na ụjọ, yana 25 yaarda/mita site n'ani ọzọ niile.

translations.source: No matter how docile they may look, bison, elk, moose, bears, and nearly all large animals can attack.
translations.reference: Agbanyeghị etu ha siri dị nwayọọ, bison, elk, muuz, bea, na anụmanụ ukwu niile nwere ike iluso ọgụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ dịghị mgbe ọ ga-adị ka ha dị nwayọọ, mana ụmụ bison, ụmụ elk, ụmụ moose, ụmụ arụ, na ụmụ anụmanụ ndị ọzọ dị ukwuu, nwere ike igwu egwu.

translations.source: Each year, dozens of visitors are injured because they didn't keep a proper distance. These animals are large, wild, and potentially dangerous, so give them their space.
translations.reference: Afọ ọ bụla, a na-emerụ ọtụtụ ndị nleta ahụ n'ihi na ha enyeghị ezigbo ohere. Ụmụ anụmanụ ndị a buru ibu, azụghịazụ, ma nweekkwa ike ịbụ ihe ize ndụ, ya mere nye ha ohere.
translations.hypothesis: Otu afọ, ọtụtụ ndị na-agbata ahụ na-emeri mmerụ ahụ n'ihi na ha adịghị enye ụdị oghere dị mkpa. Anụmanụ ndị a bụ nnukwu anụ, anụ ọhịa, na ha nwere ike ịkpata egwu, ya mere, debe ha n'ebe ha chọrọ.

translations.source: In addition, be aware that odors attract bears and other wildlife, so avoid carrying or cooking odorous foods and keep a clean camp.
translations.reference: Na mgbakwunye, mara amara na usi na adọta ụmụ bea na anụ ọhịa ndị ọzọ, ya mere zere ibu ma ọ bụ isi ụmụ nri na-esi usi ma debe kampụ dị ọcha.
translations.hypothesis: Ọzọkwa, cheta na ọdịdị anụ na-adọta ụma na ụmụ anụ ọhịa ndị ọzọ, ya mere, gabaa n'inweghị ụkpụrụ ma ọ bụ isi nri na-arụ ọdịdị, ma jide ogige gị ka ọ dị ọcha.

translations.source: Apia is the capital of Samoa. The town is on the island of Upolu and has a population of just under 40,000.
translations.reference: Apia bụ isi obodo Samoa. Obodo ahụ nọ n'agwaetiti Upolu ma ma nwee ngụpụta mmadụ nke ji obere ihe ghara eru 40,000.
translations.hypothesis: Apia bụ ibuọdụ obodo nke Samoa. Obodo ahụ dị na ọkpụkpụ Upolu, yana ọ nwere mmadụ karịrị 40,000.

translations.source: Apia was founded in the 1850s and has been the official capital of Samoa since 1959.
translations.reference: E kepụtara Apịa n'afọ ndị 1850; kemgbe 1959, ọ bụ isi obodo Samoa.
translations.hypothesis: Apia malitere ịdị na afọ 1850, ma abụọla isi obodo ugochọ nke Samoa kemgbe afọ 1959.

translations.source: The harbor was the site of an infamous naval standoff in 1889 when seven ships from Germany, the US, and Britain refused to leave the harbor.
translations.reference: Ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ahụ bụ ebe nguzosike nke ndị agha mmiri wuru ewu na 1889 mgbe nnukwu ụgbọ mmiri asaa si Jamani, US, na Briten jụrụ ịhapụ ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ákwá ụgbọ mmiri ahụ bụ ebe e mere okwu na-adịghị mma n'afọ 1889, ebe ụgbọ mmiri asaa sitere na Germany, United States, na Britain jụrụ ịhapụ ákwá ụgbọ mmiri ahụ.

translations.source: All the ships were sunk, except for one British cruiser. Nearly 200 American and German lives were lost.
translations.reference: Nnukwu ụgbọ mmiri niile ndị ahụ miri, ewezụga otu ụgbọ agha Ndị Briten. Ọ fọrọ obere ka o ruo Ndị Amerịka na Ndị Jamani 200 nwụrụnụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ufọdụ ụgbọ mmiri niile bịara agbaze, eweghachila otu ụgbọ mmiri nke Britain. Karịrị ụmọ 200 nke ndị Amerika na ndị Jamanị nwụrụ.

translations.source: During the struggle for independence organised by the Mau movement, a peaceful gathering in the town resulted in the killing of the paramount chief Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.reference: N'oge mgba maka nnwereonwe nke a haziri site n'aka ngagharị Mau, otu nzukọ keudo n'ime obodo rụpụtara n'ogbugbu nke ezigbo onyeisi Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.
translations.hypothesis: N'oge agha maka nnwere onwe nke Mau malitere, otu mkpeke udo nke mere na obodo ahụ butere iwu ahụ, ebe onye isi kachasị elu, Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III, nwụrụ.

translations.source: There are many beaches, due to Auckland's straddling of two harbours. The most popular ones are in three areas.
translations.reference: E nwere ọtụtụ ọnụ mmiri, n’ihi nnọnetiti nke Ọklandị nke ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri abụọ. Ndị nke kacha ewu ewu nọ n’ebe atọ.
translations.hypothesis: E nwere ọtụtụ osimiri, n'ihi na Auckland dị n'etiti abụọ osimiri. Ọtụtụ osimiri ndị a ma ama dị n'ọtụtụ ebe atọ.

translations.source: North Shore beaches (in North Harbour district) are on the Pacific Ocean and stretch from Long Bay in the north to Devonport in the south.
translations.reference: Akụkụ mmiri Ọnụmmiri Ugwu (nọ na mpaghara Ugwu Ebe ndote ụgbọ mmiri) nọ n’oke osimiri Pacifik ma dọtịa site na Long Bay nọ n’ugwu ruo Devonport nọ na ndịda.
translations.hypothesis: Ọdọ mmiri nke North Shore (n'obodo North Harbour) dị n'oké osimiri Pacific, na ha na-agba ọsọ site na Long Bay n'ebe ugwu ruo Devonport n'ebe ndịda.

translations.source: They are almost all sandy beaches with safe swimming, and most have shade provided by pohutukawa trees.
translations.reference: Ha niile fọrọ obere ka ha bụrụchaa akụkụ mmiri aja aja ya na igwu mmiri echedoro echedo, ma ọtụtụ n'ime ha nwere ndo enyere site n'aka ụmụ osisi pohutukawa.
translations.hypothesis: Ha bụ ọtụtụ osimiri nke dị na ala ọcha, ebe enwere ọdịmma ịnwụ mmiri, ma ọtụtụ n'ime ha nwekwara ọdịdị nke osisi pohutukawa na-enye ụkwụ.

translations.source: Tamaki Drive beaches are on the Waitemata Harbour, in the upmarket suburbs of Mission Bay and St Heliers in Central Auckland.
translations.reference: Ụmụ akụkụ mmiri Tamaki Drive nọ n’Ọdụ ụgbọ mmiri Waitemata ahụ, n’ime ahịa ndị bara ụba nọ mpaghara ebe obibi nke Mission Bay na St Heliers n’ime Central Auckland.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị mmadụ na-aga ịsa ahụ na ọdọ mmiri Tamaki Drive dị n'okpuru osimiri Waitemata, na mpaghara ndị kasị ewu ewu nke Mission Bay na St Heliers, nke dị n'etiti obodo Auckland.

translations.source: These are sometimes-crowded family beaches with a good range of shops lining the shore. Swimming is safe.
translations.reference: Ebe ndị a bụ mgbe ụfọdụ akụkụ mmiri ezinụlọ ndị mmadụ juru ya n’ọtụtụ ụdị ụlọ ahịa nọ n’ogologo ọnụ mmiri ahụ. Igwu mmiri dị mma.
translations.hypothesis: Nke a bụ ọdọ ụlọ ezinụlọ ụfọdụ, bụ nke na-adịkarị na mmadụ, yana ụlọ ahịa ọtụtụ dị n'akụkụ osimiri. Ọ dị mma ịsa ahụ n'osimiri.

translations.source: The main local beer is 'Number One', it is not a complex beer, but pleasant and refreshing. The other local beer is called "Manta".
translations.reference: Isi biya imeobodo ahụ bụ 'Number One', ọ bụghị biya na-agbagwoju anya, mana dị mma n'ahụ ma na-edo ahụ nke ọma. Biya imeobodo nke ọzọ bụ nke a na-akpọ "Manta".
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ mmanya obodo kachasị ewu bụ "Number One"; ọ bụghị mmanya siri ike, mana ọ masịrị na ọ na-enye mmadụ ume. Ọrụ mmanya obodo ọzọ bụ "Manta".

translations.source: There are many French wines to be had, but the New Zealand and Australian wines might travel better.
translations.reference: Enwere ọtụtụ mmanya si Frans mmadụ ga-aṅụ, mana mmanya Niu Ziland na Ọstrelia ga-aka mma maka njem.
translations.hypothesis: Enwe ọtụtụ mmanya ndị Farịsị na-ere, mana mmanya sitere na New Zealand na Australia nwere ike ịbụ nke ọma karị.

translations.source: The local tap water is perfectly safe to drink, but bottled water is easy to find if you are fearful.
translations.reference: Mmiri mgbata ebeụlọ dị mma nke ọma ịn̄ụ, mana mmiri bọtụlụ dị mfe ịchọta ma ọ bụrụ na ụjọ na-atụ gị.
translations.hypothesis: Mmiri umu na-ebute n'obere ọwa dị mma ma ọ bụrụ na ị na-eṅo ya, mana ọ dị mfe ịchọta mmiri dị n'ọkwọ ụlọ ma ọ bụrụ na ị nwere ụfụ.

translations.source: For Australians, the idea of 'flat white' coffee is foreign. A short black is 'espresso', cappuccino comes heaped high with cream (not froth), and tea is served without milk.
translations.reference: Maka ndị Australia, kọfị 'flat white' bụ ihe ala ọzọ. Shọt blak bụ 'espresso', cappuccino na-ebu nnukwu krim abịa (ọ bụghị froth), ha na-añụ tii na-etinyeghị mmiri ara ehi.
translations.hypothesis: Dịka ndị Australia, echiche banyere "kọfị flat white" bụ ihe ọhụrụ. "Espresso" bụ kọfị dị mkpụrụ, cappuccino na-abịa n'ụdị dị ukwuu na krim (ọ bụghị foam), na ti na-enye ya na-enweghị mmiri.

translations.source: The hot chocolate is up to Belgian standards. Fruit juices are pricey but excellent.
translations.reference: Chokoleeti ọkụ a ruru ogo nke Beljiọm. Mmanya mkpụrụ osisi dị ọnụ mana ha amaka.
translations.hypothesis: Ọgwụgwụ chocolate ahụ dị mma, ọ bụ nke zuru oke na ụkpụrụ Belgium. Mmanya mkpụrụ osisi ahụ dị oke ọnụ, mana ọ dị mma nke ukwuu.

translations.source: Many trips to the reef are made all year around, and injuries due to any of these causes on the reef are rare.
translations.reference: A na-eme ọtụtụ njem ịga na ime ala osimiri gburugburu afọ niile, ma mmerụ ahụ n'ihi otu n'ime ihe mkpata ndị a n'ime ala osimiri ahụ na-ara ahụ inweta.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ njem na-eme gaa ebe mmiri na-adị gbaa, na-anọchi anya afọ niile, ma ọ bụrụ na enwere mmerụ ahụ ọ bụla site n'akụkụ ọ bụla nke ihe ndị a na ebe ahụ, ọ bụ ihe nke na-adịkarị.

translations.source: Still, take advice from authorities, obey all signs, and pay close attention to safety warnings.
translations.reference: N’agbanyeghị, were ndụmọdụ si n'aka ndị nọ n’ọchịchị, rube isi n’ihe ntụaka niile, ma gee ntị nke ọma maka ịdọ aka na ntị nke nchekwa.
translations.hypothesis: N'agbanyeghị, na-elekwasị anya na ndụzi ndị ọchịchị na-enye, soro iwu niile, ma jidekwa anya na ihe ndụzi gbasara nchekwa.

translations.source: Box jellyfish occur near beaches and near river estuaries from October to April north of 1770. They can occasionally be found outside these times.
translations.reference: Azụjelii igbe na-apụta n'akụkụ ọnụ osimiri ma n'ụso ụmụ njekọta osimiri site n'Ọktoba ruo Eprel ugwu nke 1770. E nwekwara ike ịhụ ha mgbe ụfọdụ n'oge ndị ọzọ n'abụghị oge ndị a.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ mmiri na-acha ọbara ọbara a na-ahụ nso ọdọ na nso ebe osimiri na mmiri na-agbakọta, site na Ọktoba ruo Apụrọ, n'ebe ndị dị n'úfọdụ ebe ndị dị n'ebe ugwu nke 1770. Ọ nwere ike ịbụ na a ga-ahụ ya n'oge ndị ọzọ.

translations.source: Sharks do exist, however they rarely attack humans. Most sharks are scared of humans and would swim away.
translations.reference: Shaakị gasị dị adị, otú ọ dị, ha adịkarịghị awakpo ụmụ mmadụ. Imirikiti shaakị na-atụ ụmụ mmadụ egwu yana ga-egwu mmiri pụọ.
translations.hypothesis: Ahụ mmiri (sharks) nọ n'ụwa, mana ha adịghịkarị asị ndị mmadụ. Ndị mmiri (sharks) karịsịrị na-atụ ụjọ ndị mmadụ, ma ha ga-agba ọsọ pụọ.

translations.source: Saltwater Crocodiles do not actively live in the ocean, their primary habitat is in river estuaries north from Rockhampton.
translations.reference: Agụiyi mmiri nnu anaghị ebikewe n'ime oke osimiri, ebe ha na-ebikarị bụ na ngwọkọta osimiri na mmiri nnu dị n'ugwu sitere na Rọkhamptịn.
translations.hypothesis: Akwụkwọ ndụ nke njikọ osimiri (saltwater crocodiles) anaghị ebekarị n' osimiri, ma ebe ha bi karịsị bụ n'ọdụ ụzọ osimiri na osimiri, n'ebe ndịda nke Rockhampton.

translations.source: Booking in advance gives the traveller peace of mind that they will have somewhere to sleep once they arrive at their destination.
translations.reference: Itinye akwụkwọ n’ọdịnihu na-enye onye njem ahụ obi udo na ha nwere ebe ha ga-arahụ ụra ozugbo ha rutere ebe ha na-aga.
translations.hypothesis: Ịchọpụta ebe obodo tupu oge na-enye onye njem udo nke uche, na ọ ga-enwe ebe ọ ga-anọ mgbe ọ rutere ebe ọ na-aga.

translations.source: Travel agents often have deals with specific hotels, although you may find it possible to book other forms of accommodation, like camping grounds, through a travel agent.
translations.reference: Ndị nnọchi anya ndị njem na-enwekarị nkwekọ azụmahịa ha na kpọmkwem ụmụ họteelụ, agbanyeghị na ị nwere ike ịhụ na o kwere omume itinye akwụkwọ maka ụdị nnabata ndị ọzọ, dị ka ala ebe a na-ama ụlọikwu, sitere n'otu onye nnọchite anya njem.
translations.hypothesis: Ọtụtụ ndị na-ere tiketi njem nwere nkwekọrịta pụrụ iche na ụlọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ ụfọdụ, mana ọ nwere ike ịbụ na ị nwere ike ịkpọta ụdị ụlọ ndị ọzọ, dịka ebe ị na-ebi n'ime ụlọ tent, site na onye na-ere tiketi njem.

translations.source: Travel agents usually offer packages that include breakfast, transportation arrangements to/from the airport or even combined flight and hotel packages.
translations.reference: Ndị nnọchi anya ndị njem na-enyekarị ụmụ ngwungwu na-agụnye nri ụtụtụ, nhazi ụzọ esi eje njem ịga na/site na ọdụ ụgbọelu ma ọ bụ njem ụgbọelu etikọrọ ọnụ ya na ụmụ ngwungwu họteelụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị na-ere tiketị njem na-eji ihe atụ, na-enye ngwakọta nke gụnyere nri ụtụtụ, usoro njem gaa na banye ụlọ ọgbakọ, ma ọ bụ ọbụna ngwakọta nke ụgbọ elu na ụlọ obodo.

translations.source: They can also hold the reservation for you if you need time to think about the offer or procure other documents for your destination (e.g. visa).
translations.reference: Ha nwekwara ike idobere gị ohere a ma ọ bụrụ na ị ka chọrọ oge ịtụgharị uche na ya maọbụ ịnweta akwụkwọ ndị ọzọ maka ebe ị na-aga (ọmụmaatụ: visa).
translations.hypothesis: Ha nwekwara ike idozi ozi nchekwa maka gị ma ọ bụrụ na ị chọrọ oge iji atụle ọhụrụ ma ọ bụ nweta ihe ndị ọzọ dị mkpa maka ebe ị ga-aga (dịka visa).

translations.source: Any amendments or requests though should be coursed through the travel agent first and not directly with the hotel.
translations.reference: Ihe ọbụla a chọrọ ịgbanwe maọbụ ịna, ọ bụ onye ejenti njem ka a ga-ebu ụzọ gakwuru; ọ bụghị họteelụ n'onwe ya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na enwere mgbanwe ọ bụla ma ọ bụ arịkwụ, ọ ga-esi na onye na-ahụ maka njem ahụ, ọ bụghị ozugbo na otu obodo ahụ.

translations.source: For some festivals, the vast majority of the attendants to music festivals decide to camp on site, and most attendants consider it a vital part of the experience.
translations.reference: Maka ụfọdụ mmemme, nnukwu ọtụtụ n’ime ndị bịara na mmemme egwu ahụ kpebiri ịnọ na kampụ n’ebe ahụ, ma ọtụtụ n’ime ndị bịara na-ewe ya otu akụkụ dị oke mkpa nke ahụmihe ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: N'ibu ụfọdụ ememme, ọtụtụ ndị na-eleta ememme egwu na-akpọrọrọ ịgbasa ụlọ n'ebe ememme ahụ na-eyi, na ọtụtụ ndị na-eleta na-eche ya bụ akụkụ dị mkpa nke ahụmịhe ahụ.

translations.source: If you want to be close to the action you're going to have to get in early to get a camping site close to the music.
translations.reference: Ọ bụrụ na ị chọrọ ịnọ nso na emereme ahụ ị ga-ekwesị ịbanye ọsịịsọ iji nweta otu ebe a na-ama ụlọikwu nọ nso n'egwu ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na ịchọrọ ịbụ onye nọ n'ebe dị nso na ihe niile na-eme, ị ga-abịa n'oge mbụ iji nweta ebe ị nọrịrị na obere ihe nkwari akụ, nso na ebe egwu si eme.

translations.source: Remember that even though music on the main stages may have finished, there may be sections of the festival that will keep playing music until late into the night.
translations.reference: Cheta na obu ezie na egwu ogbo-egwu nwere ike gwula, enwere ike inwe mpaghara mmeme ahu gana aku egwu ruo ime abali.
translations.hypothesis: Cheta na, ọ bụrụla na egwu na ngalaba ndị isi ahụ kwesịrị izu, enwere ike ịbụ ụdị ọtụtụ akụriji ahụ nke egwuregwu na-agafe na festival ahụ nke ga-enwe egwu ruo ọtụtụ elekere n'abalị.

translations.source: Some festivals have special camping areas for families with young children.
translations.reference: Ụfọdụ ememme nwere ebe ndị a na-ama ụlọikwuu pụrụ iche maka ezinụlọ nke nwere ụmụ na-eto eto.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ emempe nwere ebe ndị mmadụ nwere ike ịgbasa akwụkwọ ụlọ maka ezinụlọ nwere ụmụaka.

translations.source: If crossing the Northern Baltic in winter, check the cabin location, as going through ice causes quite horrible noise for those most affected.
translations.reference: Mgbe ị na-agafe Ebe ugwu Baltic n’oge oyi, lelee ebe kabịn ahụ, dị ka ịgafe okwute mmiri na-akpata mkpọtụ dị nnọọ egwu maka ndị ọ kacha metụta.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na ị na-agafe Oké Osimiri Baltic nke dị n'ebe ugwu n'oge ọkụ, lelee ebe ụlọ ahụ dị, n'ihi na ịgafe ice na-eme ụda nke na-emetụta ndị na-abụkarị n'ụzọ dị egwu.

translations.source: Saint Petersburg cruises include time in town. Cruise passengers are exempted from visa requirements (check the terms).
translations.reference: Njem nnyagharị nke Senti Piitasbọg gụnyere oge n'ime obodo. Ndị njem nke njem nnyagharị bụ ndị ewezụgara site n'ụmụ ihe ndị achọrọ maka visa (lelee usoro ahụ).
translations.hypothesis: Nkwụrụ ụjọ nke Saint Petersburg gụnyere oge dị na obodo. Ndị na-eme njem nkwụrụ ụjọ ahụ anaghị achọ visa (lee usoro ndị ahụ).

translations.source: Casinos typically make many efforts to maximize time and money spent by guests. Windows and clocks are usually absent, and exits can be hard to find.
translations.reference: Ụlọ chaa chaa gasị na-eme ihe niile ịhụ na ndị mmadụ mefuru oge na ego ha niile. Windo na elekere anaghị adịkewe n'ime ha; ọzọ, ụzọ ọpụpụ na-arakarị ahụ ịchọta.
translations.hypothesis: N'aka nwa, ụlọ azụ na-agba ọsọ iji mee ka ndị mmadụ na-eji oge ha na ego ha na ya. Ọdịdị ụkwụ na agbàràọrụ adịghịkarị, ọ bụkwa ọrụ siri ike ịchọpụta ụzọ pụọ.

translations.source: They usually have special food, drink and entertainment offers, to keep guests in a good mood, and keep them at the premise.
translations.reference: Ha na-enwekarị nri pụrụ iche, mmanya na ụmụ onyinye ntụrụndụ, iji debe ndị ọbịa n'ọnọdụ dị mma, ma debe ha n'ogige ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ha na-eji otu ụzọ dị iche iche, dị ka nri pụrụ iche, ihe ọṅụṅụ, na mmemme dị ụtọ, iji mee ka ndị bisịntọ nọọrọ n'obi ụtọ ma nọọrọ n'ebe ahụ.

translations.source: Some venues offer alcoholic beverages on the house. However, drunkenness impairs judgement, and all good gamblers know the importance of staying sober.
translations.reference: Ụfọdụ ebe mgbakọ na-enye ụmụ ihe ọn̄ụn̄ụ na-eme n'anya n'efu. Mana, mmanya ogbugbu na-egbochi echiche, ma ndị nille na-agba chaa chaa nke ọma mara mkpa nke ọ dị ịnọ n'ezi echiche.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ ebe na-enye mmanya dị iche iche n'efu. Otú ọ dị, ịṅụ mmanya karịrị njikere nwere ike ịgbagwo echiche, ma ụmụ mmadụ niile na-achọ ihe ọma na egwuregwu ịgba oge maara mkpa ịkwụsi onwe ha n'anya.

translations.source: Anyone who's going to drive at high latitudes or over mountain passes should consider the possibility of snow, ice, or freezing temperatures.
translations.reference: Onye ọ bụla nke na-aga ịnya ụgbọ ala ya elu latitude maọbụ n’elu ugwu gafere, kwesịrị ịtụle ihe enwere ike ịbụ oge snow, ice, ma ọ bụ oke oyi.
translations.hypothesis: Onye ọ bụla ga-eje ije n'ebe dị nso na akụkụ ugwu ma ọ bụ n'okporo ụzọ dị elu, ga-atụgharị uche ya maka ohere nke igwe ojii, ice, ma ọ bụ okpomọkụ na-agba ụtụ.

translations.source: On icy and snowy roadways, friction is low and you cannot drive as if you were on bare asphalt.
translations.reference: N’okporo ụzọ ebe ais na sno dị, nrapara dị ala nakwa ịnweghị ike ịnya moto n'elu ya dịka ị nọ na asfalt nkịtị.
translations.hypothesis: N'okporo ndị dị jụụ na ndị dị ọcha, ọ dịghịkwa ọtụtụ ọdịmma, yabụ ị nwekwara ike ịnya ụgbọ ala dị ka ị na-anya n'okporo dị ọcha.

translations.source: During blizzards, enough snow to get you stuck can fall in very little time.
translations.reference: N'oge ụmụ oke ozuzo okwute mmiri, sinoo ga-ezu iji mee ka ị tọọ nwere ike izo n'ime ntakịrị oge.

translations.source: Visibility may also be restricted by falling or blowing snow or by condensation or ice on vehicle windows.
translations.reference: Enwere ike igbochi mgbàràìhè site na ịda ma ọ bụ ịfụ sinoo ma ọ bụ site na umu irighiri mmiri ma ọ bụ mmiri kpụkọrọ akpụkọ na windo ụgbọala.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ nwere ike bụkwa na ihe ndị na-ebutere ma ọ bụ na-efu, ma ọ bụ mmiri na-agbaze ma ọ bụ ice na akwụkwọ ụgbọ ala, ga-ebelata ọdịdị nke ihe ndị dị n'okpuru.

translations.source: On the other hand, icy and snowy conditions are normal in many countries, and traffic goes on mostly uninterrupted all year round.
translations.reference: N'aka nke ọzọ, ụmụ ọnọdụ okwute mmiri na sinoo bụ ihe nkịtị n'ọtụtụ mba, ma ụmụ ụgbọala na-anyagharị n'enweghị nsogbu afọ niile.
translations.hypothesis: N'akụkọ ọzọ, ọ bụ ihe nkịtị na mba ndị ọzọ na-enwe oke anwụrụ na snow, ma ọtụtụ oge, ọtọ ụgbọ ala na-aga n'ụzọ zuru oke, ọbụla oge nke afọ.

translations.source: Safaris are perhaps the greatest tourism draw in Africa and the highlight for many visitors.
translations.reference: Safari nwere ike ịbụ ihe kachasị akpọta ndị njem nlereanya na Afrịka ma bụrụkwa ihe kachasị atụ ha n'anya.
translations.hypothesis: Ọrụ njem na ugwu (safaris) bụ, ma eleghị anya, ihe kacha akọwapụta na ụlọ ọrụ nleta na Afrika, yana ihe dị mkpa na ọtụtụ ndị na-agbata akwụkwọ.

translations.source: The term safari in popular use refers to overland travel to view the stunning African wildlife, particularly on savanna.
translations.reference: Okwu bụ safari n’ojiji ama ama pụtara ime njem n’ofe ala ileleanụ ọhịa Afrịka dị ịtụnanya, tụnadị na savanna.
translations.hypothesis: Ụkpụrụ "safari" dị ka a na-eji ya n'ọtụtụ ebe, pụtara njem n'okporo ụzọ iji hụ ụmụ anụmanụ ndị mara mma nke Afrịka, karịsịa na mpaghara savanna.

translations.source: Some animals, such as elephants and giraffes, tend to approach closely to cars and standard equipment will allow good viewing.
translations.reference: Ụmụanụmanụ ụfọdụ, dịka enyi ga na mgbara ga, na-abịaru nso n’ụgbọala ma ngwaọrụ izugbe dị mma ga-enye gị ohere iji hụ ha nke ọma.
translations.hypothesis: Ụfọdụ anụmanụ, dịka ndị ika na ndị giraffe, na-adịkarị ka ha na-abịa nso na ndị isi, na ngwaọrụ ndị ọzọ ga-enyere gị aka ịhụ ha nke ọma.

translations.source: Lions, cheetahs and leopards are sometimes shy and you will see them better with binoculars.
translations.reference: Ọdụm, agụogbu na agụ na-eme ihere mgbe ụfọdụ ma ị ga-ahụ na nke ọma karịa n'iji baịnokụlaasị.
translations.hypothesis: Anya, ụma, na ụma-ọhịa bụ ụdị anụmanụ na ha na-enwekarị ụjọ, ma ị ga-ahụ ha nke ọma ma ọ bụrụ na ị jiri anya-ele anya.

translations.source: A walking safari (also called a "bush walk", "hiking safari", or going "footing") consists of hiking, either for a few hours or several days.
translations.reference: Safari ngagharị (nke a na-akpọkwa "njem ọhịa", "safari ọrịrị", maọbụ "nzọụkwụ") gbakwunyere ịrị ugwu ruo awa ole na ole maọbụ ọtụtụ ụbọchị.
translations.hypothesis: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nke ịga ije n'okpuru osisi (ọ bụkwa ka a na-akpọ ya "ịga ije n'ebe dị anya," "ịga ije n'okpuru osisi," ma ọ bụ "ịga ije n'ụkwụ") pụtara ịga ije, ma ọ bụ maka awa ole na ole ma ọ bụ ụbọchị ole na ole.

translations.source: The Paralympics will take place from 24 August to 5 September 2021. Some events will be held in other locations throughout Japan.
translations.reference: Engwuregwu Paralimpiks ga-eme site n'Ọgọọst 24 ruo na Septemba 5 2021. A ga-eme ụfọdụ emume n'ebe ndị ọzọ gburugburu Japan.
translations.hypothesis: Asụsụ Paralympics ga-ebu ibu site na Ọgọọstụ 24 ruo Septemba 5, afọ 2021. Ụfọdụ ihe omume ga-eme na ebe ndị ọzọ n'ofe Japan.

translations.source: Tokyo will be the only Asian city to have hosted two summer Olympics, having hosted the games in 1964.
translations.reference: Tokyo ga-abụ naanị obodo Eshia nke kwadoro asọmpi nke oge okpomọkụ ugboro abụọ, ebe akwadoro egwuregwu ahụ na 1964.
translations.hypothesis: Tokyo ga-abụ obodo Asia naanị nke nwere ịgbasa ọkpụkpọ abụọ nke Summer Olympics, ebe ọ gbapụrụ ọkpụkpọ ahụ na afọ 1964.

translations.source: If you booked your flights and accommodation for 2020 before the postponement was announced, you may have a tricky situation.
translations.reference: Ọ bụrụ na ị kwụrụ ụgwọ maka ụgbọelu gị na ebe obibi gị maka 2020 tupu ekwuputa myigharịrị oge, i nwere ike inwe ọnọdụ tara akpụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na ị rụchara atụmatụ maka ụgbọ elu na ebe obibi gị maka afọ 2020 tupu ọkwa atụmatụ ahụ gbanwere, ọ nwere ike ịbụ na ị nọ na ọnọdụ siri ike.

translations.source: Cancellation policies vary, but as of late March most coronavirus-based cancellation policies don't extend to July 2020, when the Olympics had been scheduled.
translations.reference: Iwu nkagbu na-adị iche iche, mana ka ọ dị na Maachị gara aga ọtụtụ n'ime ụmụ iwu nkagbu dabere na njecorona agbatịghị ruo Julaị 2020, mgbe ahazirioge Olumpiks ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ụkpụrụ mbelata ọrụ na-adị iche iche, mana ka ọ dị n'ọnwa Machị nke gara aga, ọtụtụ iwu mbelata ọrụ metụtara akụrụngwa ahụike (coronavirus) adịghị etolite ruo ọnwa Julaị afọ 2020, bụrụ otu e kwadoro maka egwuregwu Olimpik.

translations.source: It's expected that most event tickets will cost between ¥2,500 and ¥130,000, with typical tickets costing around ¥7,000.
translations.reference: Ọ bụ ihe atụwara anya ya na ọtụtụ tiketị emume ga-adị ọnụ n'etiti ¥2,500 na ¥130,000, ya na tiketị a na-ahụkarị na-adị ọnụ ruo ihe dị ka ¥7,000.
translations.hypothesis: A tara akụkọ, ọtụtụ tiketi maka mkpebi ndị a ga-adị n'etiti ¥2,500 na ¥130,000, ebe tiketi ndị ọzọ ga-adị n'ihe dị ka ¥7,000.

translations.source: Ironing damp clothes can help them dry. Many hotels have an iron and ironing board available for loan, even if one is not present in the room.
translations.reference: Ide akwa butụ mmiri nwere ike inyere ha aka ịkọ. Ọtụtụ ụlọ nkwarị akụ nwere otu igwe ndetị akwa na bọọdụ ide akwa dị adị maka mgbaziri, ọbụlagodi ma otu anọghị anọ n'ime ụlọ ahụ.
translations.hypothesis: Ịcha akwa dị n'ọchịchị bụ ikekwe inyere aka ka ha sie n'anya. Ọtụtụ otu obodo nwere akwa na tebụl ịcha akwa nke ha na-enye ndị mmadụ iji, ọbụlagodi edoghị akwa ma ọ bụ tebụl ịcha akwa n'ime ụlọ.

translations.source: If an iron isn't available, or if you don't fancy wearing ironed socks, then you can try using a hairdryer, if available.
translations.reference: Ọ bụrụ na igwe ndetị akwa adịghị adị, ma ọ bụ ọ bụrụ na ọ masịghị gị iyi sọks edere ede, mgbe ahụ ị nwere ike ịnwa iji otu igwe ịkọ ntutu, ma ọ dịrị.
translations.hypothesis: Ọ bụrụ na ị nweghị akwa eletrik, ma ọ bụ ọ bụrụ na ị maghị ịkpụcha akwa, mgbe ahụ, ọ ga-ekwesị ịnwale iji akwa ikuku (hairdryer), ọ bụrụ na ị nwere ya.

translations.source: Be careful not to allow fabric to become too hot (which can cause shrinkage, or in extreme cases, scorch).
translations.reference: Kpachara anya ka akwa ghara ịdị oke ọkụ (nke a nwere ike ime ka akwa hịkpọọ, maọbụ ọ ka njọ, o nwere ike ịgba ọkụ).
translations.hypothesis: Kwenye ịgha aghụghọ mgbe ị na-arụ ọrụ akwa, ma tụkwasị obi ka akwa ahụ adịghị na-awụli nke ukwuu (nke nwere ike ibute na akwa ahụ gaa n'ime, ma n'ọnọdụ siri ike, ọ nwere ike ịla).

translations.source: There are different ways of purifying water, some more effective against specific threats.
translations.reference: E nwere ọtụtụ ụzọ e ji eme ka mmiri dị ọcha, ụfọdụ kara dị ire maka ụmụ ihe iyi egwu pụrụ iche.
translations.hypothesis: Enwere ụzọ dị iche iche iji ehicha mmiri, ụfọdụ n'ime ha na-arụ ọrụ nke ọma karị iji gbochie ihe egwu dị iche iche.

translations.source: In some areas boiling water for a minute is enough, in others several minutes are needed.
translations.reference: N'ebe ụfọdụ isi mmiri n'ọkụ ruo otu nkeji ezuola, n'ebe ndị ọzọ achọrọ ọtụtụ nkeji.
translations.hypothesis: N'ebe ụfọdụ, ịkpọ mmiri na akwụkwọ n'ime nkeji otu bụ ezigbo ihe, mana n'ebe ndị ọzọ, ọ dị mkpa ịkpọ ya maka nkeji ole na ole.

translations.source: Filters vary in effectiveness, and should you have a concern, then you should consider buying your water in a sealed bottle from a reputable company.
translations.reference: Ụmụ m̀yọ̀ na-adị iche n’ịdị irè, ma ọ bụrụ na ị nwee nchebara echiche, mgbe ahụ ị kwesịrị itule uche ịzụ mmiri gị n’ime otu karama amachiri siye na otu ụlọ ọrụ nwere aha ọma.
translations.hypothesis: Ezigbo mmepụta mmiri na-adị iche n'ihe ọ dị mma, ma ọ bụrụ na ị nwere nọmba, mgbe ahụ, ị ga-atụgharị uche ịzụta mmiri gị n'ime akwụkwọ ụlọ ọrụ a mara mma.

translations.source: Travellers may encounter animal pests that they are not familiar with in their home regions.
translations.reference: Ndị njem nwere ike ịhụta ụmụ anụ ọtapịa ndị nke ha na-amaghị n'ebe ụlọ ha.
translations.hypothesis: Ndị na-eje ije nwere ike ịhụ ụdị anụ ọhịa na-emerụ ahụ nke ha na-enweghị amụma banyere ya n'ebe ha bi.

translations.source: Pests can spoil food, cause irritation, or in a worse case cause allergic reactions, spread venom, or transmit infections.
translations.reference: Pesti nwere ike imebi nri, kpata Pests can spoil food, cause mmeka ahụ, ma ọ bụ n’ọnọdụ ka njọ kpata mmeghachi omume nfụkasị, kesaa venọm, ma ọ bụ ọrịa ofufe.
